title: Wild HRC Civic Type R Is In Development For US, Honda Says
raw_summary: Honda's Civic Type R hot hatch received a modest nip and tuck for the 2027 model year , but some of us were left wanting bigger changes to keep the CTR at the top of the class. Maybe someone at American Honda was listening, because the automaker is bringing its Type R HRC Concept to SEMA, and now says the car is "in development for the U.S. market." Sport compact fans are surely rejoicing as this car will debut under the same roof as the Nissan Sentra Spec-V concept . Honda's concept made its debut at this year's Tokyo Auto Salon, alongside a modified Prelude Coupe that had also been breathed on by the automaker's racing division, HRC (Honda Racing Corporation). It now heads Honda's SEMA lineup at the Las Vegas Convention Center. Honda hasn't detailed the exact changes that turn a regular Type R into an HRC variant, but if the base car is the 911 GT3 of hot hatches, the HRC looks set to play the GT3 RS role. No timeframe has been given for a U.S. production launch.

Maybe someone at American Honda was listening, because the automaker is bringing its Type R HRC Concept to SEMA, and now says the car is "in development for the U.S. market." Sport compact fans are surely rejoicing as this car will debut under the same roof as the Nissan Sentra Spec-V concept .

Honda's concept made its debut at this year's Tokyo Auto Salon, alongside a modified Prelude Coupe that had also been breathed on by the automaker's racing division, HRC (Honda Racing Corporation). It now heads Honda's SEMA lineup at the Las Vegas Convention Center. Honda hasn't detailed the exact changes that turn a regular Type R into an HRC variant, but if the base car is the 911 GT3 of hot hatches, the HRC looks set to play the GT3 RS role. No timeframe has been given for a U.S. production launch.

Although still covered in camouflage in Honda's latest pictures, the HRC Civic clearly has a more aggressive front bumper, aerodynamic winglets over the front wheelarches, and a serious rear spoiler. Those tweaks all point to additional downforce, and we'd expect them to be paired with uprated springs and dampers, and larger brakes. The biggest question is whether HRC is able to liberate any more power from the turbocharged, 2.0L inline four. It currently makes 315 hp (319 PS) in U.S. trim, which is sent to the front wheels via a six-speed manual transmission.

The HRC is one solid reason to swing by Honda's SEMA stand next month (November 3-6, 2026), but it's not the only one. There's also Honda's Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck , which has a twin-turbo, 2.4L V6 powertrain that employs hybrid technology to help it wind out a monstrous 1,300+ horsepower (1,318 PS). The Trophy Truck is backed up by a trio of modified Passport Trailsport chase vehicles.

For anyone who's looked at the new Prelude hybrid coupe and wished Honda would junk the electric bits and drop in the Civic Type's engine and six-speed manual transmission, they'll want to check out the Hasport Prelude Club Racer. It's the modern-day Prelude most of us have dreamed about, but the Honda gurus at Arizona's Hasport wasn't content to leave the idea as a dream.

Felix Rosenqvist's 2026 Indy 500-winning Honda IndyCar, the Honda-powered 2026 Aston Martin Aramco Racing AMR26 F1 racer, and a 35-horsepower Honda N600 microcar that competed in the 1970 Baja 1000 race are also on display. And HRC U.S. is launching its line of official performance parts at SEMA 2026, including sports exhausts, lightweight forged wheels, and a short-throw shifter for models like the Civic Type R, Passport Trailsport and Integra Type S. Honda and Acura will offer the upgrades through dealerships and online starting March 2027.

raw_title: FAA Finally Certifies Boeing 737 Max 10 For Commercial Delivery, Bringing The Entire 737 Family Into Service
title: FAA Finally Certifies Boeing 737 Max 10 For Commercial Delivery, Bringing The Entire 737 Family Into Service
raw_summary: It has finally happened: the Federal Aviation Administration has certified the Boeing 737 Max 10, meaning that the entire range of the company's best-selling aircraft is now suitable for delivery to airlines in the U.S. The 10 variant is the largest of the 737 Max family, able to seat up to 210 passengers in a two-class configuration, making it something of a successor to the mid-size 757. It now joins its siblings, the 8 and 9 variants that have been flying for years, and the smallest 7 variant that only got certified a few months ago . This is great news for Boeing, which is on a hot streak lately: It recently recovered the ability to self-certify individual planes for safety and overtook archrival Airbus in annual sales . The 737 Max 10's certification was stuck on the runway for a long time before finally achieving liftoff. The variant flew its first test flight way back in 2021. This was after the horrible 737 Max crashes of 2018 and 2019, so the FAA was quite suspicious of the company and really put this model through the wringer. In addition, the Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act was passed in 2020, mandating much stricter standards. The 737 Max 10 is the first plane to go through the new process, though it took five years. You'll be pleased to learn that both Boeing and the FAA are aware of a software glitch that messes with the navigation system, but never mind that! The plane is flyable, and you might well be on one sometime next year.

article_paragraphs: It has finally happened: the Federal Aviation Administration has certified the Boeing 737 Max 10, meaning that the entire range of the company's best-selling aircraft is now suitable for delivery to airlines in the U.S. The 10 variant is the largest of the 737 Max family, able to seat up to 210 passengers in a two-class configuration, making it something of a successor to the mid-size 757. It now joins its siblings, the 8 and 9 variants that have been flying for years, and the smallest 7 variant that only got certified a few months ago . This is great news for Boeing, which is on a hot streak lately: It recently recovered the ability to self-certify individual planes for safety and overtook archrival Airbus in annual sales .

The 737 Max 10's certification was stuck on the runway for a long time before finally achieving liftoff. The variant flew its first test flight way back in 2021. This was after the horrible 737 Max crashes of 2018 and 2019, so the FAA was quite suspicious of the company and really put this model through the wringer. In addition, the Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act was passed in 2020, mandating much stricter standards. The 737 Max 10 is the first plane to go through the new process, though it took five years. You'll be pleased to learn that both Boeing and the FAA are aware of a software glitch that messes with the navigation system, but never mind that! The plane is flyable, and you might well be on one sometime next year.

Each of the 737 Max variants has its purpose. For the 10, being larger means that it can handle a route's passenger traffic in fewer flights, giving it the lowest per seat cost of any single-aisle aircraft, according to Boeing . Functionally, it's a replacement for the old 757, which the aviation sector has been waiting for a long time.

With a 3,100-nautical-mile range, the 10 can cover a broad range of routes; however, this is the shortest range of any 737 Max, which limits its appeal a bit. By contrast, the tiny 7 can go 3,800 nautical miles, which can cover the vast bulk of routes, though it can only carry up to 160 passengers in a two-class configuration. Still, the 7's light weight means it's great for high-altitude or high-temperature airports.

The all-around champions here are the 8 and its very close twin, the 9. You've probably been on one. The former can take up to 180 passengers up to 3,500 nautical miles; the latter can take up to 195 passengers up to 3,300 nautical miles. These two combined have made the 737 Max into Boeing's top seller ever. Getting the 7 and 10 certified adds icing to that cake.

It's a good amount of icing, though, since over 30% of current 737 Max orders are for the 10 variant. Simple Flying reports that Canadian airline WestJet will be the first to get the shiny new planes in early 2027 (provided that Canadian regulators also certify them). Boeing will then fulfill orders, all 1,555 of them, for other customers all over the world. Now all Boeing has to do is get the 777X finally certified .

title: Xpeng's G9L Lands As A Threat To The European Establishment
raw_summary: More Chinese EVs headed to Europe, but at least this one looks good It's not just BYD that has used the recent Paris Motor Show to unveil an important new SUV for the European market. Fellow Chinese brand Xpeng has done the same, unveiling its flagship G9L SUV in battery-electric and range-extender configurations. If any European brands weren't taking the threat from China seriously, they now have to.
summary: More Chinese EVs headed to Europe, but at least this one looks good It's not just BYD that has used the recent Paris Motor Show to unveil an important new SUV for the European market. Fellow Chinese brand Xpeng has done the same, unveiling its flagship G9L SUV in battery-electric and range-extender configurations.
article_paragraphs: More Chinese EVs headed to Europe, but at least this one looks good

It's not just BYD that has used the recent Paris Motor Show to unveil an important new SUV for the European market. Fellow Chinese brand Xpeng has done the same, unveiling its flagship G9L SUV in battery-electric and range-extender configurations. If any European brands weren't taking the threat from China seriously, they now have to.

Xpeng has priced the G9L from €74,600 ($83,300) in Germany, and between €74,990 ($83,700) and €75,990 ($84,900) in other European markets, including France, Austria, and the Netherlands. This makes it comfortably cheaper than something like a new BMW X5, which starts at €102,800 ($114,800) in plug-in hybrid X5 50e xDrive configuration. The G9L won't only be sold in Europe either, as Xpeng plans to sell the G9L in 64 separate markets, including Australia and New Zealand. It's been designed as a truly global SUV and will be manufactured at the firm's plant in China and Magna Steyr's factory in Austria.

The range-extender version is perhaps the most intriguing. It uses a turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-four with a powerful electric motor and a 63-kWh lithium-ion phosphate battery, which itself is larger than the batteries of some smaller EVs. Xpeng says combined grunt sits at an impressive 577 horsepower and 513 pound-feet (695 Nm) of torque, allowing the EREV to hit 62 mph (100 km/h) in 5.4 seconds.

More impressive than the performance on offer is Xpeng's claim the G9L EREV can travel up to 270 miles (435 km) on electric power alone and has a combined driving range of 996 miles (1,602 km) on the optimistic CLTC cycle. The powertrain includes regenerative braking to maximize efficiency and intelligently adapts to the driving scenario. For example, if you're in an urban environment, it will prioritize electric power, and on a highway, the range-extender will be activated as required. Crucially, the engine never drives the wheels and only generates electricity, so the G9L EREV will accelerate as smoothly and instantly as a traditional EV.

Two all-electric versions have been announced alongside the EREV. Base models will use a 91.9-kWh battery while others will be available with a 110-kWh pack. The most powerful version will use a pair of electric motors with 577 hp and 513 lb-ft (695 Nm) of torque. This power does come at the cost of efficiency. On the WLTC cycle, the range of this version will be capped at 344 miles (553 km). Somewhat making up for that is that the G9L supports DC charging speeds of up to 540 kW, allowing the battery to be charged from 10 to 80% in under 12 minutes.

It's not just the available powertrains that may encourage some European buyers to ditch their BMWs and Audis for the Xpeng G9L. It is rocks the company's latest intelligent driving technologies that include city and highway assisted driving, navigation-based assisted driving, and intelligent hands-free lane changes.

The G9L's cabin also prioritizes luxury and comfort. Found in the front row are Nappa leather seats with heating, ventilation, and a 16-point massage function. The second row will be available with either a bench seat or captain's chairs, all trimmed in the same Nappa leather as the front and also include heating, ventilation, and massage functions. As for the third row, it includes heated seats and a 50:50 split folding function.

The ultra-luxury brand offers BYD’s most high-end and technically advanced vehicles, including the U7 sedan, the U8, a hardcore off-road SUV, and the U9, an electric supercar.

Yangwang vehicles have previously debuted with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including its quad-motor e4 platform (delivering over 1,300 hp), its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging, and its DiSus-X intelligent body control system.

Its next model will push further into the elite segment. After BYD revealed the name of its new flagship executive sedan earlier this week, the Yangwang Altior, the company has released several new details ahead of its official debut.
Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing confirmed on Friday that the new Yangwang Altior will feature suicide doors, a first for a BYD model.
The new door design swings open nearly 90 degrees, Hu said, creating a dramatic, wide-open entrance.
Hu also posted a preview of the vehicle’s front fascia, complete with a dot-matrix Gemstrone grille and crystal-inspired headlights.

title: What happened in Mexican GP FP1 with 10 rookies
raw_summary: Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc led Mercedes’ Formula 1 drivers’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli in first practice for the 2026 Mexico Grand Prix as 10 rookie drivers took to the track. article_paragraphs: Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc led Mercedes’ Formula 1 drivers’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli in first practice for the 2026 Mexico Grand Prix as 10 rookie drivers took to the track.
Leclerc set the benchmark of 1m18.128s to go 0.659 seconds faster than Antonelli, whose stand-in team-mate Fred Vesti was just 0.074s slower in third.
Mercedes’ Vesti was the fastest rookie in FP1, with every team bar Ferrari fielding a substitute for FP1.
Leclerc’s team-mate Lewis Hamilton was 0.005s off Vesti in fourth, the top four having set their fastest times on softs.
Red Bull stand-in Ayumu Iwasa meanwhile went fifth, 0.985s off the pace, on mediums.
Pierre Gasly took sixth for Alpine, just over a second away, while his rookie team-mate Gabriele Mini was 14th.

Fernando Alonso was 1.229s off the pace in seventh for Aston Martin on mediums. Alonso’s team-mate Jak Crawford, 19th, brought out the VSC late on as his Aston Martin stopped off track with a suspected ERS issue.
Oscar Piastri went eighth on softs while Leonardo Fornaroli, driving in place of Lando Norris in FP1, was 17th in the second McLaren.

raw_summary: As the CEO of Bugatti Rimac responsible for making some of the most powerful and fastest interal-combustion and electrified vehicles in the world, Mate Rimac was already a pretty cool dude, but the latest situation he found himself in takes things to another level. Rimac, being the very rich and apparently very trusting man that he is, decided it's a good idea to leave his cars unlocked with the keys inside them at his company's headquarters in Croatia, in case employees ever needed to move them. It hadn't really been an issue for the 38-year-old ... until now. Rimac, as he always does, left his Bugatti Chiron unlocked with the keys in it outside a garage at the company's campus recently when everything went very wrong. An employee spotted the seven-figure supercar speeding away and quickly alerted colleagues, according to an Instagram video posted by the CEO. A group of employees quickly figured out that no one authorized the vehicle to be moved, and somebody had indeed stolen the car. Rimac didn't take this news lying down. Of course, he contacted police, but he also jumped behind the wheel of his fully fueled Porsche 911 (we think it's this very nice purple 992.2 Turbo S that coincidentally uses Rimac batteries) and went after the stolen car at "full throttle."

article_paragraphs: As the CEO of Bugatti Rimac responsible for making some of the most powerful and fastest interal-combustion and electrified vehicles in the world, Mate Rimac was already a pretty cool dude, but the latest situation he found himself in takes things to another level. Rimac, being the very rich and apparently very trusting man that he is, decided it's a good idea to leave his cars unlocked with the keys inside them at his company's headquarters in Croatia, in case employees ever needed to move them. It hadn't really been an issue for the 38-year-old ... until now.

Rimac, as he always does, left his Bugatti Chiron unlocked with the keys in it outside a garage at the company's campus recently when everything went very wrong. An employee spotted the seven-figure supercar speeding away and quickly alerted colleagues, according to an Instagram video posted by the CEO. A group of employees quickly figured out that no one authorized the vehicle to be moved, and somebody had indeed stolen the car. Rimac didn't take this news lying down. Of course, he contacted police, but he also jumped behind the wheel of his fully fueled Porsche 911 (we think it's this very nice purple 992.2 Turbo S that coincidentally uses Rimac batteries) and went after the stolen car at "full throttle."

Luckily for Rimac, the Bugatti was equipped with live telemetry, meaning that, despite the thief having a one-hour head start, he and his colleagues were able to tell exactly where the car was and relay that information back to Croatian police.

There was hope that police would intercept the Chiron and the thief before it left Croatia, but that wasn't meant to be. In fact, it made it all the way to Austria, crossing through Slovenia in the process. In Austria, the driver found himself low on fuel — not a terrible surprise given the Chiron has a quad-turbo W16 engine . After throwing half a tank of fuel in the car, which he didn't pay for, he continued driving. Eventually, Austrian police were able to catch up with him thanks to information from Rimac's group chat.

Rimac says he had decided not to press charges against the man who stole his car, but that doesn't mean he's going to walk away scot-free. I'm sure the police in Croatia, Austria, and possibly Slovenia are going to want to talk to him. Initially, Rimac, maybe with a bit of naivety, thought he'd be able to just pick up the car from the cops and drive the thief back home to his family, no harm, no foul, but "because of the value of the car, there was like 10 police cars," and he couldn't just take the car back. However, just a day later he got it back after proving he was the real owner. Apparently, the thief was local to Croatia, and had shown up to the Rimac HQ asking for job before he stole the Chiron.

The incident has already changed Rimac's approach to locking his cars' doors. He's no longer going to leave keys lying around or leave cars unlocked. At the beginning of his video, he says Croatia is "super, super safe," which he admits might sound strange to folks in the U.S. and abroad. That's why he always felt fine leaving his cars unlocked.
"I did that for years, and nothing ever happened. Until, of course, something did happened, so I will not do that anymore," Rimac joked on Instagram . "Don't try your luck — will not happen again."

title: New BMW Alpina B7 Will Have A Great-Sounding V8
raw_summary: One of the best concept cars of this year was the Vision BMW Alpina , a stunning two-door coupe that previews the direction the Alpina brand is going now that it's fully under BMW's control. Our spies have now caught the first production car that will be the fruit of that labor: The new BMW Alpina B7, based on the facelifted 7 Series . This will be the fourth generation of 7 Series to have an Alpina version that was sold in the U.S., and the first time this current G70 model is getting the Alpina treatment. BMW recently showed off the M760, which has a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 making around 570 horsepower, and the B7 should share that same powertrain just with even more power — the last B7 had 600 hp . The Vision concept had a real V8 in it that made very good noises from its lovely quad exhaust, and this B7 prototype has the same exhaust, which is a good sign.

BMW recently showed off the M760, which has a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 making around 570 horsepower, and the B7 should share that same powertrain just with even more power — the last B7 had 600 hp . The Vision concept had a real V8 in it that made very good noises from its lovely quad exhaust, and this B7 prototype has the same exhaust, which is a good sign.
I don't need that as a sign to know it sounds good, though. These spy shots were taken at the Nürburgring, and as you can hear from the clip above, this B7 prototype sounds quite good itself.

In addition to the quad exhaust, this prototype has a unique front grille with horizontal lower slats, a larger and wider lower bumper intake, and a prominent chin splitter, an Alpina hallmark. There's a little spoiler on the trunk lid, and the rear diffuser is new. New BMW M cars like the M350 and iX4 M60 feature yellow LED running lights, and it seems like the Alpina models will have a different amber shade, like the Vision concept. The big wheels are a design we haven't seen before, but I don't think they'll be the final ones. BMW has already said Alpina will stick with its classic multispoke designs.

Expect the B7 to get its own suspension and chassis tuning that give it a more comfortable, grown-up vibe compared to M cars, focused on grand touring performance. There will surely be Alpina-specific paint colors (the brand is known for its emerald greens and sapphire blues) and exterior graphics packages, while the interior will have crystal controls, Alpina's signature blue and green stitching and other patterns, special badging and other touches.

It shouldn't be long before the new Alpina B7 gets revealed and goes on sale, and it will be closely followed (or maybe even preceded) by the Alpina XB7 version of the next-gen X7 that recently got spotted .

title: Fuel From Bamboo Costs Just $2.75 Per Gallon
raw_summary: At CleanTechnica , we are passionate champions of the “electrify everything” movement promoted by Tony Seba and Mark Jacobson, among others. However, being realistic, internal combustion engines will continue to play an important role in transportation by land, sea, and air for the remainder of this century and perhaps beyond. Almost any plant that grows could potentially be turned into a biofuel with a lower emissions footprint than gasoline or diesel. Currently in the US, millions of tons of corn are used every year to make ethanol , which is then blended with gasoline. In theory, the ethanol helps lower emissions, but the reduction, if any, is modest and it decreases fuel economy, so motorist are actually using more fuel than they would if they used ordinary, unadulterated gasoline.

article_paragraphs: At CleanTechnica , we are passionate champions of the “electrify everything” movement promoted by Tony Seba and Mark Jacobson, among others. However, being realistic, internal combustion engines will continue to play an important role in transportation by land, sea, and air for the remainder of this century and perhaps beyond.

Almost any plant that grows could potentially be turned into a biofuel with a lower emissions footprint than gasoline or diesel. Currently in the US, millions of tons of corn are used every year to make ethanol , which is then blended with gasoline. In theory, the ethanol helps lower emissions, but the reduction, if any, is modest and it decreases fuel economy, so motorist are actually using more fuel than they would if they used ordinary, unadulterated gasoline.

The other part of the equation is that the conversion process itself requires a fair amount of energy and makes its own greenhouse gas emissions, which politicians conveniently choose to ignore. Ethanol , then, is mostly a scam that rewards farmers, but has few other benefits. While the science is sound, the rewards are far less than claimed. However, farmers are an important political group and no one wants to tell them that corn for ethanol is no longer a thing.

Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute think they have found a better way. In a study published September 24, 2026 in the Royal Society of Chemistry journal Sustainable Energy And Fuels , Michael Timko, the head of the chemical engineering department at WPI, and Timothy Woodard, PhD, claim that bamboo may be the perfect source material for making biofuels. In the published study, they write:

“Corn stover, an agricultural residue widely available in the U.S., has been one of the most studied biomass sources for biofuel production.6 Yet its relatively modest yields and high ash content have created significant challenges for scaling up production. Alternative feedstocks such as switch grass have been explored, but these offer only incremental improvements in performance relative to corn stover, particularly in ash content and growth rate. These limitations highlight the importance of identifying and evaluating less conventional biomass sources that may offer superior attributes for fuel production.

“Bamboo has emerged as a strong candidate due to its rapid growth, high productivity per unit area, and low input requirements. Some bamboo species reach their full height within a few months and mature within four years. Bamboo’s deep root systems improve soil stability, promote subsurface carbon sequestration, and support water conservation. It can also be grown on marginal or degraded land, reducing competition with food crops and offering economic opportunities for rural communities.

“Critically, bamboo also possesses an exceptionally low ash content compared with most lignocellulosic feedstocks, which minimizes inorganic fouling and catalyst poisoning during thermochemical conversion and improves the quality of the resulting biocrude. Furthermore, the presence of ash complicates thermochemical conversion to products, with frequently reported adverse effects on yields.

“The characteristics of fast growth, low fertilizer and water use, and low ash content make bamboo stand out as a promising source of biomass that can achieve economic competitiveness that has not been obtained with other feedstocks. Unfortunately, despite these advantages, bamboo remains largely underexplored as a feedstock for liquid fuel production, especially in thermochemical conversion processes such as hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL).”

The competition will then spend the next dozen days traversing over 4,200 miles of rugged Moroccan terrain, finishing in Marrakech on January 23. Dakar Rally organizers let fans use their imaginations as to why the event was temporarily moved out of Saudi Arabia, using the vague explanation, "In light of recent events." But it's not hard to connect the dots and realize it was due to the U.S. war against Iran.

While the war has cooled in recent months , Saudi Arabia became the direct target of a renewed offensive by Houthi forces in Yemen amid their ongoing conflict. Earlier this month, the Houthis launched a barrage of drones and missiles at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and two other international airports. The attacks killed at least 21 people and injured over 300 more. Also, U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly implied that the United States would resume hostilities against Iran after next week's midterm elections. It simply wasn't safe to run the Dakar Rally anywhere in the region.

The Dakar Rally is no stranger to relocation. As the event name implies, it was originally a cross-country rally from Paris to Dakar in Senegal . It largely remained that way from 1979 until 2008, when four French tourists were killed by a North African wing of al-Qaida and the race was canceled. Fearing that the Dakar could be a target for insurgents in the Maghreb, the rally relocated to South America from 2009 until 2019. The Amaury Sport Organization, Dakar's organizers, moved the event to Saudi Arabia in 2020 after signing a multi-year deal with the country . The return to Africa in 2027 will only be temporary because of how lucrative the Saudi agreement must be.

raw_title: Tesla drops car referral rewards, now pays owners in FSD for referrals
title: Tesla drops car referral rewards, now pays owners in FSD for referrals
raw_summary: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying. At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.
summary: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.
article_paragraphs: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.

At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.

To share a link, you need to be paying for FSD (Supervised) monthly or own it outright from before Tesla stopped selling it, according to Tesla’s FSD referral support page . Owners who got FSD through a one-year grant can’t participate. The link lives under “Refer and Earn” in the Tesla app, version 4.62.0 or later.

The person on the other end has to own a registered Tesla with compatible hardware, can’t have paid for FSD in the past 12 months, and can’t have bought it outright. There’s also a catch for recent buyers: anyone who got a free FSD trial with a new car is locked out of referral links until 12 months after that trial ends.

If the friend converts, subscribers get a free month and outright owners get a $99 credit, the same as one month of the subscription. Credits expire after 12 months and can’t be cashed out. Tesla caps it at 12 rewards per calendar year, so the most anyone can earn is a year of FSD or $1,188 in credits.
Tesla’s own pages don’t quite agree on timing. The FSD page says the referrer is rewarded when the friend subscribes during the trial, while the main Refer and Earn page says after it.

The bigger change is buried in Tesla’s Refer and Earn page . Buyer benefits now apply to solar panels only. Referrer benefits cover solar, first demo drives (up to 30 over an account’s lifetime) and the new FSD referral.
Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck only show up under loyalty benefits, for existing owners buying another Tesla product. Model S and Model X aren’t listed at all.

title: Polaris Has Just Created A Dune Buggy With More Power Than An Audi RS3
raw_summary: Polaris put sports car power into its sand-slinging buggy, which debuts at the 2027 King of the Hammers desert race A couple of months ago, Polaris unveiled an extreme version of its popular RZR , badged the Pro R Boost. article_paragraphs: Polaris put sports car power into its sand-slinging buggy, which debuts at the 2027 King of the Hammers desert race

A couple of months ago, Polaris unveiled an extreme version of its popular RZR , badged the Pro R Boost. With a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four and 275 horsepower, it's a side-by-side that packs a serious punch. Polaris obviously wasn't satisfied with Hyundai Elantra N levels of performance and has now unveiled an even crazier version of the RZR with significantly more grunt. Meet the RZR Pro R Factory Boost.

Unlike the standard Pro R Boost, the Pro R Factory Boost is designed for desert and sand racing. It uses a new turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder known as the ProStar Fury with 400 hp. We don't yet know how much torque this engine has, though with 400 hp, the latest RZR has more power than a U.S.-spec Audi RS3 with 394 hp. That should make it an absolute weapon in the sand and on pretty much any other terrain imaginable.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost is so focused that it features lightweight carbon fiber bodywork and has been designed to slice through the air at over 100 mph. This explains why it looks much sleeker than the normal, consumer-focused RZR Pro R. It also benefits from a 6.5-inch longer wheelbase to improve stability and body control. A set of beefy BF Goodrich tires connects the side-by-side to the terrain, while custom three-inch internal bypass Dynamix DV Live Valve shocks soak up any and all bumps. A Fox steering damper absorbs larger impacts.

The modifications don't stop here. The RZR Pro R Factory Boost includes a new competition-ready cage and a cab that's two inches wider. It also includes a large 34-gallon fuel tank and has a driving range of more than 200 miles. A full MoTeC package and ECU with different power distribution settings control the 2.0-liter engine's monstrous power output.

Each example will be built by the Polaris RZR Factory Racing team, and the RZR Pro R Factory Boost will make its competitive debut at the 2027 King of The Hammers event running from January 21, 2027, through to February 6, 2027. Crucially, you don't need to run a racing team or be a competitive racer to buy one, but you will need a lot of money. Prices start at $200,000, or almost three times the starting price of the aforementioned Audi RS3. Evidently, you'll need to be a serious off-roading enthusiast to drop this kind of money on a non-road-legal side-by-side.

raw_title: Koenigsegg's Latest $3.6 Million Hypercar Has Just Been Recalled
title: Koenigsegg's Latest $3.6 Million Hypercar Has Just Been Recalled
raw_summary: No matter how expensive a new car may be, there's a good chance it'll be recalled at some stage. For the Koenigsegg CC850 , that time has come, and now all seven examples delivered in the United States need to be fixed because of an issue with the electronic parking brake. The NHTSA says Koenigsegg received a report of a CC850 rolling away in the U.S. on October 12. According to the recall notice, the driver exited the vehicle with the engine running and reverse gear engaged, causing it to start rolling away. The notice doesn't say whether any damage occurred, though the incident prompted the Swedish hypercar manufacturer to launch an investigation. After a week of internal testing, Koenigsegg discovered that the parking brake will not engage while the transmission is in Reverse and the engine is running. In this case, the only way to engage the parking brake is to hold the button down continuously. The NHTSA says this condition falls outside the scope of its static parking brake tests, so it appears Koenigsegg issued this recall of its own accord, not because the CC850 fails to comply with any Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.

article_paragraphs: No matter how expensive a new car may be, there's a good chance it'll be recalled at some stage. For the Koenigsegg CC850 , that time has come, and now all seven examples delivered in the United States need to be fixed because of an issue with the electronic parking brake. The NHTSA says Koenigsegg received a report of a CC850 rolling away in the U.S. on October 12. According to the recall notice, the driver exited the vehicle with the engine running and reverse gear engaged, causing it to start rolling away.

The notice doesn't say whether any damage occurred, though the incident prompted the Swedish hypercar manufacturer to launch an investigation. After a week of internal testing, Koenigsegg discovered that the parking brake will not engage while the transmission is in Reverse and the engine is running. In this case, the only way to engage the parking brake is to hold the button down continuously. The NHTSA says this condition falls outside the scope of its static parking brake tests, so it appears Koenigsegg issued this recall of its own accord, not because the CC850 fails to comply with any Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.

Koenigsegg manufactured the seven impacted vehicles between September 28, 2025 and August 2, 2026. All of these CC850s will receive a free over-the-air software update to resolve the issue. If customers opt against having the software update implemented, they'll have the opportunity to bring their vehicle to an authorized Koenigsegg dealership and have the update completed on site.

The CC850 stands out from other Koenigsegg models in part by using the Swedish automaker's part-manual, part-auto nine-speed Lightspeed transmission . It uses three shafts and seven clutches, and can be operated with a traditional clutch pedal as well as a gated manual transmission. Alternatively, the CC850 can be driven like a typical automatic. Ferrari recently introduced its own manual transmission for the 12Cilindri , which has a similar philosophy to Koenigsegg's approach. However, the Ferrari version operates as an add-on to the existing dual-clutch transmission.

title: It Didn't Take Long For Someone To Make The New Audi RS 5 Even Crazier
raw_summary: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design. summary: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design.
article_paragraphs: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant

Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design. It serves as the perfect antidote to all the boring EVs flooding the market. Now, German tuner and race team ABT Sportsline is developing an upgraded version of the RS5, giving it more power than even the limited-edition Audi RS6 GT .

ABT's creation, the RS5-R, follows a similar formula to other upgrade packages the firm sells. The firm started by looking at how it could make this beast even more intoxicating. To do this, they tweaked the software for the twin-turbocharged 2.9-liter V6 and the electric motor, resulting in a combined 710 horsepower and 667 pound-feet (905 Nm) of torque. The 80 hp and 59 lb-ft (80 Nm) gains should transform how this beast drives and let it easily outperform an RS6, even though that car has two extra cylinders. This is just the start of what ABT is developing for the RS5. Next year, it will release another performance upgrade with an Akrapovic titanium exhaust, helping the engine churn out 789 hp.

The upgrades extend beyond the engine. ABT has designed an eye-catching aerodynamic kit for the RS5-R with a sharp new front splitter, louvers on the front wheel arches, extended side skirts, and new wing mirrors. Stretching out from the roof is a large spoiler, and working with it to stick the rear wheels to the pavement is a striking rear diffuser. These parts are available in either standard carbon fiber or forged carbon fiber.

Oftentimes, the wheels of a modified car can make or break the overall design. In the case of the RS5-R, ABT has designed new 22-inch forged wheels with a gloss black finish and bold triangular spokes, clad in huge 315/25 tires. A set of lowering springs adds to the car's overall road presence, while sportier anti-roll bars have also been fitted.

ABT plans to sell just 130 examples of its RS5-R package, and each will include a special numbered plaque in the cabin. Speaking of the cabin, it will also include newly trimmed seats, an even plusher dashboard, and red contrast stitching. Carbon fiber paddle shifters complete the modifications.

For as impressive as all of the upgrades are, they're not cheap. In fact, prices for the RS5-R package start at €62,000 ($69,400) for the Sedan and Avant and €65,000 ($72,800) for the Avant when equipped with a standard carbon fiber finish, or an extra €3,000 ($3,300) for forged carbon fiber. ABT also charges a hefty €7,160 ($8,000) installation fee for the Sedan and €7,600 ($8,500) for the Avant. Oh, and all of these prices are in addition to the price of the actual car, which starts at €106,200 for the Sedan and €107,850 for the Avant (U.S. pricing and availability have yet to be announced).

raw_title: Electric Hydrofoils Save Energy, But Do They Earn Their Price?
title: Electric Hydrofoils Save Energy, But Do They Earn Their Price?
raw_summary: Hydrofoils have an obvious appeal. Lift a boat’s hull clear of the water, reduce drag and move passengers faster while consuming less energy. I’ve written before about the proposed electric hydrofoil ferry between Vancouver, Bowen Island and Gibsons, where floating logs, coastal conditions and uncertain passenger demand make the economics difficult. Hydrofoils have been commercially available for decades, but their operating niche remains narrower than their technical appeal suggests. A different opportunity emerged when Antwerp pilotage operator Brabo ordered an Artemis EF-12 electric hydrofoil pilot boat in August 2024. The vessel combines electric propulsion with submerged foils and active controls. Artemis has also demonstrated ship-contact manoeuvres using its EF-12 workboat platform, while the EF-12 Pilot design entered sea trials in 2026. The handling benefits are relevant to pilot transfers even when the boat isn’t operating at full speed.

I’ve written before about the proposed electric hydrofoil ferry between Vancouver, Bowen Island and Gibsons, where floating logs, coastal conditions and uncertain passenger demand make the economics difficult.
article_paragraphs: Hydrofoils have an obvious appeal. Lift a boat’s hull clear of the water, reduce drag and move passengers faster while consuming less energy. I’ve written before about the proposed electric hydrofoil ferry between Vancouver, Bowen Island and Gibsons, where floating logs, coastal conditions and uncertain passenger demand make the economics difficult. Hydrofoils have been commercially available for decades, but their operating niche remains narrower than their technical appeal suggests.

A different opportunity emerged when Antwerp pilotage operator Brabo ordered an Artemis EF-12 electric hydrofoil pilot boat in August 2024. The vessel combines electric propulsion with submerged foils and active controls. Artemis has also demonstrated ship-contact manoeuvres using its EF-12 workboat platform, while the EF-12 Pilot design entered sea trials in 2026. The handling benefits are relevant to pilot transfers even when the boat isn’t operating at full speed.

The financial question is whether a hydrofoil can spend enough of its working life taking advantage of its design. Antwerp pilot boats work around locks, docks, ship movements and changing assignments. Reaching a high maximum speed is of limited value when the vessel spends much of its day manoeuvring or travelling through constrained waterways.

I tested that question using a Python-based operating model with synthetic assignments and three hypothetical sets of port-speed permissions. Depending on how much suitable high-speed water was available, the EF-12 spent zero, approximately 6% or approximately 13% of its underway time foilborne. These are modeled scenarios, not measurements of Brabo’s operations or actual Antwerp speed authorizations.

The resulting financial comparison was unflattering to the hydrofoil. In the central case, the EF-12’s modeled fifteen-year discounted cost was approximately €5.32 million, compared with €3.81 million for a conventional diesel tender, a premium of about 40%. Both figures include purchasing new vessels, rather than comparing a new hydrofoil with the marginal cost of keeping an existing diesel boat.

Electric propulsion still brought substantial energy benefits. The hydrofoil’s problem was that lower purchased energy did not compensate for the assumed capital cost and the limited opportunity to operate in its most efficient regime. Its active controls and potential ride-quality benefits remain relevant, but the available evidence did not justify assigning them a financial value.

An alternative electric approach also deserves consideration. Norway’s Moen Marin and Pascal Technologies have developed an air-cavity electric personnel vessel that reduces hull resistance without lifting most of the vessel above the water. It performed better financially than the hydrofoil in the exploratory comparison, although the existing craft was designed for aquaculture work and would require appropriate adaptation and certification before serving as a pilot tender.

The lesson resembles the one I drew from the Vancouver hydrofoil ferry proposal . Hydrofoils can be excellent machines, especially where sustained high-speed passages and suitable sea conditions allow them to exploit their advantages. In congested harbours, their additional complexity and capital cost need much stronger justification.

summary: Lewis Hamilton intends to continue racing in Formula 1 “for the foreseeable future” if he can remain competitive, having been asked if he can realistically expect to race in the newly-announced African Grand Prix. article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton intends to continue racing in Formula 1 “for the foreseeable future” if he can remain competitive, having been asked if he can realistically expect to race in the newly-announced African Grand Prix.
Earlier this month F1 revealed its plan for a new race in Rwanda, which will hold the title of the African GP, from 2030 at the earliest.
Hamilton, a long-standing figure who pushed for F1 to return to Africa, would therefore need to remain in the series well into his 40s to compete in the inaugural race in Rwanda.

The 41-year-old dismissed doubts he would retire from F1 before the first African GP would take place despite acknowledging he would be in his mid-40s if the race was to take place in 2030 – the earliest the event is planned, subject to track and infrastructure construction being completed in that time frame.
“Firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years. I feel that I'm built differently,” Hamilton said ahead of this weekend’s Mexican GP.

“Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee, that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off. Did you see my reaction in the last race? My reaction is faster than some of the youngest people here.

“So there are lots of tools that you can utilise to continue to keep yourself, your mind sharp, as long as you're willing to sacrifice everything, which I am right now. I can't say in four years whether I want to continue to do what I'm doing, but I love what I'm doing still now.
“I'm still all in, and I will be for the foreseeable future.

raw_summary: Earlier this month, McLaren told the world that the 750S supercar will end production sometime next year. Naturally, we wondered what will come next. The US auto industry is littered with has-beens, wanna-be’s, never-was, and just plain exhausted cars that retired along with their names. Hmmm….perhaps Ford is sending a not so subtle signal about the future of EV sales in the US…

By now, everyone knows that EV sales cratered last fall, after US President Donald Trump and his Republican majority in Congress engineered the “OBBA” tax bill to eliminate federal tax credits for EVs.

Still, EV sales did not actually stop in their tracks, let alone reverse course. A fresh wave of off-lease, used EVs helped keep the momentum up earlier this year, and some automakers (looking at you, Subaru ) stayed on track with plans for new EVs in the US.
Plug-in hybrids also factored in as a sort of gateway drug, with Audi CEO Gernot Döllner among those looking forward to strong EV sales in that category.

EV stakeholders must smell blood in the water as Election Day 2026 approaches. With polls indicating that Trump will lose his chokehold on federal EV policy, news about EVs has been tumbling through the Intertubes over the past several weeks. Among the examples, Slate Auto opened its first showroom in Chicago, and General Motors unveiled its gen-4 EV platform .

Somewhat bizarrely, the Trump administration also contributed to the news cycle with the launch of the new “BattMan” battery collaboration earlier this week. Under the umbrella of the US Department of Energy, BattMan hooks up federal laboratories with academic and private sector partners to push the envelope on next-gen batteries for transportation applications as well as stationary energy storage.

Of course, Tesla also weighed in with its “flying car” stunt , but that was just a stunt. Over in the world of street legal EVs, Ford has been working the publicity machine to gin up interest in the forthcoming Fathom all-electric pickup truck , which is on track for volume production early next year at an MSRP starting at the affordability benchmark of $28,350 with a built-in inverter that cuts the cost of bidirectional charging , too.

The Fathom illustrates how much blood, sweat, and tears go into naming a new car. It’s a mid-sized pickup like the popular Maverick, but Ford went off in a new direction with the Fathom , considering hundreds of options over a months-long naming journey before settling on a maritime-adjacent reference to deep understanding.

title: Volkswagen hits pause on the Golf EV as it faces an ‘urgent need for action’
raw_summary: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs. “We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
summary: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs. “We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
article_paragraphs: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs.

“We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
VW Group’s operating loss swelled to €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter because of a write-down of its Porsche stake, weak sales in China, and lower profit margins on electric vehicles.
As part of its latest cost-control efforts, Volkswagen is pausing development of the all-electric Golf at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said in an internal memo Reuters reviewed on Friday. The Wolfsburg plant, or the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.
Schäfer said the “decision was really not an easy one for us,” knowing what the Golf means to Wolfsburg.

The decision comes after Volkswagen’s Supervisory Board approved its restructuring strategy, “Future Plan 2030,” last month, which includes reducing its global workforce by 100,000, trimming its lineup, and closing several plants in Germany.
Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer confirmed earlier this year that the electric hatch will be delayed until closer to 2030.

In all seriousness, there were literally oodles of great answers, so feel free to go back and read through the other comments that didn't make this roundup. These are a few of my favorite answers, but if yours didn't make the cut, or maybe you missed the chance to leave an answer, go ahead and leave yours in the comments below, after you read all of my thoughtful commentary, of course. These are the cars you're always surprised to see people actually bought.

My vote is the Nissan Murano CrossCabriolet. If you are not familiar, it is essentially a convertible version of the Nissan Murano. Any criticism you may have for that make or Murano base model aside, the concept of a crossover with a convertible roof baffles me. A convertible top can enhance the look of a sporty car...this does not. Since it is a crossover with higher ground clearance than a sedan, it is unlikely to benefit from the improved visibility of having the top down. I assume it provides a noisy highway ride, and in many regions in the US, winter weather likely makes it a less practical daily driver (and 19 mpg ?!). The one time I remember seeing one, the driver had the top down (of course), was wearing a button down shirt with a sweater tied around his neck (why not I guess), and was probably heading to/from the municipal golf course acting like he belonged to a country club. It's like he had less money than sense to buy this vehicle. Ultimately it feels like this weird combo of crossover and convertible, excellently captured by the name "CrossCabriolet," is a Jack of some trades, master of none.

Listen here, Jasonator, the Nissan Murano CrossCabriolet is a saint. It's one of those cars that should have never made it to production, and yet the universe was generous enough to enjoy its wackiness for four years. I say the same about the Buick Cascada later on in this blog, but I love a big four-seat convertible that stays in its lane rather than trying to be a sports car.

It's not like the Murano was ever truly marketed as an off-roader, so the CrossCabriolet didn't really have any off-road pretensions. It just lived its life as a big, squishy, top-down cruiser, and I, for one, am immensely grateful to exist in a reality where, despite being utterly silly and underbaked, Nissan sent the Murano CrossCabriolet to market. "'Tis better to have Murano CrossCabrioleted and lost than to have never Murano CrossCabrioleted at all," or whatever Socrates said.

The three-wheeled cars like the Polaris Slingshot. Give me something with none of the maneuvering benefits of a motorcycle, and like half of the comfort of a four-wheel car. No top to it so worse than a conventional convertible. I can't imagine they drive better, even as well as a conventional supercar.

Brent, I couldn't agree more. I lived with one for a week and found the experience to be so miserable that my fitness tracker kept recognizing my time behind the wheel as periods of elevated stress. And it wasn't from excitement.

Cars and vans produce 16% of the EU’s CO₂ emissions. A strong automotive package puts them on track, keeping 720 million tonnes of CO₂ out of Europe’s air by 2050.

General Motors is going to pay $220 million to settle allegations that it had illegally collected and sold drivers' private behavior and location data to brokers , who then sold that information to insurers that used it to set and sometimes increase rates. Not a very cool move, if ya ask me. The settlement resolves claims made by 35 U.S. attorneys general over the automaker's Smart Driver program , which enrolled millions of drivers between 2016 and 2024 — when it was discontinued. Other regulators have also been reviewing GM's handling of driver data.

The automaker was accused of pitching Smart Driver as a program to help people improve their personal driving safety, but GM quickly violated their privacy by reneging on its promise not to sell their data without permission. Many folks who signed up were also enrolled in GM's OnStar safety, navigation and diagnostic service. From Reuters :
The settlement also requires GM to limit driving data it ‌collects, ⁠and obtain drivers' express consent before collecting or sharing that data.
A GM spokesperson said the settlement reinforces other steps the Detroit automaker has taken to strengthen privacy.

"Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to ​being clear about what ​information is used, how ⁠it's protected, and the choices customers have about what they share," the spokesperson said.
Insurers such as Allstate, Progressive and Berkshire Hathaway's Geico use so-called telematics in monitoring drivers' habits. They say the ​technology rewards ⁠good driving through lower premiums.

article_paragraphs: Daniel Ricciardo believes Kimi Antonelli ’s age and innocence are what have made him so successful in the 2026 Formula 1 season.

Nine victories so far in his sophomore F1 campaign have taken Antonelli to the brink of his maiden world title. All the Mercedes driver needs to be crowned in Sunday’s Mexican Grand Prix is ninth place, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win.
This would make the 20-year-old F1’s youngest-ever champion, beating Sebastian Vettel ’s current record by more than three years.
Ricciardo, who made his F1 debut at 22 years old and retired from the world championship at 35, believes he knows exactly how Antonelli feels – and how that makes him so strong.

“I got asked by a friend about Kimi Antonelli the other day, and I said ‘ignorance is a superpower’ – you know, ‘being young’ is what I’m really trying to say, I’m not trying to be mean to him at all,” the Australian told the Beyond The Grid podcast. “Being young is a superpower, being ignorant and not having been so exposed to the world and things like that.

“I remember my first year at Red Bull Racing ; you’re naive, you’re young, you’re ignorant. I don’t know, everything’s easy and it comes easy, and it’s just, ‘Oh wow, I’m winning, cool, I’ll just keep winning, cause I’m the best’.”

Ricciardo joined Red Bull’s main squad for the 2014 season following compatriot Mark Webber ’s retirement, teaming up with Sebastian Vettel; he unexpectedly took all three of the outfit’s victories that year, noticeably outperforming the reigning four-time world champion.

raw_summary: When getting a new car, the age-old question is always whether it's better to buy or lease . Of course, the answer often comes down to the individual, their financial situation, and what sort of commitment they're looking for, but there's another important part of the equation: The car itself. Some cars are just better to lease than they are to buy, and that idea is what brings me to today's question.

I want to know what car you would lease, but would never consider buying. What car, for one reason or another, could you stomach making a financial commitment to for two or three years, but once that time is over, have a dealership take it back off your hands for good?

Obviously, there are plenty of reasons why some cars are better to lease than buy. Maybe an automaker is running good lease rates on a particular model. Maybe they've got a bit of a reputation for — let's say — being around for a good time, not a long time. Maybe you've done the math, and you've realized that a certain type of car (electric) is being updated so rapidly that committing to the technology of today long-term probably isn't going to pay off five or 10 years from now, so getting into a car for two or three years just makes more sense.

My pick is a simple one, and it checks two of the boxes I just mentioned: unreliability and a rapidly changing EV landscape. It's the Lucid Air. I absolutely adore the Air . There's an argument that it's the best sedan on sale today, perhaps even the best vehicle, regardless of body style. It's especially appealing if you opt for the quarter-million-dollar version, the Air Sapphire , but I won't be greedy with my choice. Unfortunately, the Sapphire is a bit unreliable , and there are several known bugs with the car's software that make it hard to justify such a big price tag. It does, however, also check the EV box.

So, while it is a fantastic car now, it probably won't be in a decade's time. And why would I want to deal with the headache and heartache of having a car that is so deeply outdated — especially when it's supposed to be software-defined? I wouldn't, and neither would you. Anyway, that's enough out of me. How about you all head on down below and let your fellow Jalops know what car you would absolutely lease but would never buy? As always, cash prizes will be given out to those who explain their answers.

raw_summary: Waymo is adding the Toyota bZ4X to its robotaxi lineup. Toyota will build a custom version of the electric SUV with the Waymo Driver integrated right on the line in Japan, and a test fleet will start operating there in 2027. article_paragraphs: Waymo is adding the Toyota bZ4X to its robotaxi lineup. Toyota will build a custom version of the electric SUV with the Waymo Driver integrated right on the line in Japan, and a test fleet will start operating there in 2027.
It’s the first actual vehicle to come out of the partnership the two companies signed last year. And it gives Waymo a Japanese-built car for its Tokyo launch, with the UK and other markets to follow.

When Waymo and Toyota first announced their deal in April 2025 , it was a preliminary agreement to “explore” working together on autonomous driving, including in personally owned vehicles. Lots of intent, no product.

Now there’s a product. According to Waymo’s announcement , Toyota will produce the vehicles at its Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, and Waymo’s self-driving hardware will be installed and integrated at that same site instead of being retrofitted somewhere else.

The robotaxi bZ4X gets a few rider-focused changes: extra rear legroom, automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting. Waymo didn’t share sensor specs, unit volumes, or what each vehicle costs.
Operations in 2027 are about testing and validating the autonomous bZ4X fleet in Japan. The UK and “other Waymo markets” come in later years, with no dates attached.
The two companies also say they’ll keep working on autonomous tech for Toyota’s personal vehicles, plus safety projects with Woven by Toyota, the automaker’s software arm.
Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said that “Toyota’s commitment to zero traffic accidents resonates deeply with us at Waymo.”

article_paragraphs: In our transportation reporting, we rarely come across something as fun as today’s review of the Jasion Poki.

The Poki is a severely overpowered electric minibike that looks like it came from yesteryear. If the power isn’t enough, it also packs some cool tricks, and we’re not (just) talking about wheelies this time.

So taking a look at this bad boy, it just screams fun. It is really low to the ground, has a big, wide seat large enough for 2 people as long as they are under 350lbs total, and has pegs for 2 people and a basket, great for carrying a picnic and an extra helmet.

This thing is built like a tank, and it tips the scales accordingly. Getting this thing in my SUV ruptured a few discs in my back, though its compact nature means it fit quite well. Loosen the handlebars and it is downright compact. But that weight is strangely like 50lbs heavier than I would expect at close to 140lbs.

That also makes the built-in wheelies a little bit more suspect. My son, who is by now becoming an expert at wheelies, found this one to be a bit more difficult than the auto wheelies on bikes like the Anyland or new Yozma IN11.

OK so not only does this little powerhouse get you (and your friend) around town in style and it also makes wheelies a bit easier; but it also has a huge Bluetooth speaker in the back that sounds like a Harley and is all synced up with the actual controller so it sounds real.
Sure, it is a gimmick, but it is a fun one, and it might actually make the low-down bike a little safer since it is going to be out of the sight of most cars.

I love this thing. It is my favorite bike to go to the beach on (and it does well in the sand with those fat tires). But I think there are some big misses here. First of all, it has no business going over 40mph. Not only does it feel scary with those tiny wheels, but speed wobbles puts both the rider a possible second rider at significant risk here. This is a fun bike and it should top out at 20-28mph max. Keep all the torque, just cut out the power at a reasonable top speed.

There comes a point when Corvette ownership demands something more than clunky white walking shoes, jorts worn with tall socks, and the non-ironic possession of at least one of those creepy little 'Time Out' car show dolls. Certain Corvettes, especially those built in this millennium, offer performance levels that demand respect when carving up windy roads or revving at a stoplight.

The 2007 Chevy Corvette Z06 we looked at yesterday is one of those serious editions. With the largest naturally aspirated small-block ever wedged into a Corvette engine bay and a specially lightened chassis, the Z06 handily outshone its lesser brethren. Our car was also touted as having "tasteful updates" and would be accompanied in the sale with a slew of maintenance and repair receipts.

A bit of research showed that the seller's $47,000 asking price is at the bottom of the Z06 market, making it an intriguing opportunity. While the car's desirability and value were both noted by many in the comments, that price inexplicably fell by a 68% 'No Dice' loss in the vote. That's a bit of a head-scratcher, because, honestly, these cars ain't gonna get any cheaper.

Recently, popular YouTuber Rich Benoit, aka "Rich Rebuilds," aka "Massachusetts Man," posted a video detailing a 2023 Polestar 2 Performance he bought at a salvage auction for around $3,000. The car, an ex-Hertz rental with around 80K on the clock, was listed with undercarriage damage and as not running. Aesthetically, however, the car looked pretty great for a former "rent it and dent it." Rich diagnosed several issues with the car, including a coolant leak, a missing fireman's loop, and, puzzlingly, a broken rear shock mount. Having fixed all of those issues, the car ran and, according to Rich, went like stink. The total outlay for the Polestar was under five grand, making it a relative bargain despite the salvage title.

This is an important fact, as it sets the baseline for how much the value of Polestar products has dropped in recent months. The cars, built by automaker Geely in China, have recently been in the news because the current administration has banned them from being sold in the States — based on the brand's Chinese ownership percentage. It's been pandemonium for Polestar dealers, but it may be a boon for used-market buyers looking for a deal on a decent EV.

This 2024 Polestar 2 Long Range looks to be more than just decent. This model is a significant update over the earlier 2021-2023 cars, offering a larger battery, dual motors with more performance, and a standard package (Pilot Pack) that offers adaptive cruise control, lane assist, and parking aids.

Together, the front and rear motors produce 421 horsepower and a stonking 545 pound-feet of torque, available from zero rpm. Juicing those motors is a 78 kWh under-floor battery. It can charge at up to 200 kW for reasonably quick refueling and offers around 275 miles of range if treated with care. The electricity to charge that battery and propel the Polestar is getting increasingly more expensive (like everything), but on average, it's still a heck of a lot cheaper than buying gas for any similar-spec car or truck. According to the ad, this Polestar has a clean title and comes with a mere 18,250 miles on the ticker.

raw_title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid's Silence Speaks Volumes
title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid's Silence Speaks Volumes
raw_summary: Standing out from the crowd is never easy, especially in the compact crossover segment . Whether it's the Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, Chevy Equinox or the mighty Toyota RAV4, all compact crossovers sort of look the same, are similarly sized, have the same sort of tech, and usually drive the same, too. However, with the 2027 Rogue Hybrid , Nissan is looking to switch up the game by leaning on its trick e-Power series hybrid drivetrain that gives the Rogue a driving experience unlike any hybrid vehicle I've ever driven before — and more importantly, it's unlike any gas-powered crossover I've ever driven. I mean, hell, it even has one-pedal driving. The name of the game when it comes to the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is peace and quiet. Throughout my introduction to the car, Nissan's designers and engineers emphasized how silent the Rogue Hybrid's cabin is and the lack of any sort of serious engine noise, and those claims were backed up over the 70-ish miles of testing I did on a rare rainy day in Southern California. Add in a simple yet comfortable cabin, a decent amount of tech, thoughtful safety features, solid build quality, competitive efficiency, and soft looks that buck the trend of simulated machismo that is all the rage these days, and Nissan delivered a package that's impressive as hell.

article_paragraphs: Standing out from the crowd is never easy, especially in the compact crossover segment . Whether it's the Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, Chevy Equinox or the mighty Toyota RAV4, all compact crossovers sort of look the same, are similarly sized, have the same sort of tech, and usually drive the same, too. However, with the 2027 Rogue Hybrid , Nissan is looking to switch up the game by leaning on its trick e-Power series hybrid drivetrain that gives the Rogue a driving experience unlike any hybrid vehicle I've ever driven before — and more importantly, it's unlike any gas-powered crossover I've ever driven. I mean, hell, it even has one-pedal driving.

The name of the game when it comes to the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is peace and quiet. Throughout my introduction to the car, Nissan's designers and engineers emphasized how silent the Rogue Hybrid's cabin is and the lack of any sort of serious engine noise, and those claims were backed up over the 70-ish miles of testing I did on a rare rainy day in Southern California. Add in a simple yet comfortable cabin, a decent amount of tech, thoughtful safety features, solid build quality, competitive efficiency, and soft looks that buck the trend of simulated machismo that is all the rage these days, and Nissan delivered a package that's impressive as hell.
Full Disclosure: Nissan flew me out to Santa Barbara, California, put me up in a lovely hotel and fed me all so I could check out the 2027 Rogue Hybrid.

The Rogue Hybrid drives like nothing else on the road today in America, simply because the closest thing to it in our country is actually a train. Unlike every other non-plug-in hybrid on the market, which are parallel hybrid systems with gas and electric motors that work in tandem to motivate the drive wheels, the Rogue Hybrid's e-Power drivetrain is a series hybrid .

That means the 148-horsepower turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-three cylinder motor under the hood is only responsible for charging up the 1.67-kWh battery, and it has absolutely no mechanical connection to the front or rear wheels. That motor also achieves 42% thermal efficiency, which is damn good for an internal combustion engine. It might be the same size as the normal Rogue's engine, but Nissan engineers tell me it's a completely different motor.

The wheels are actually powered by electric motors on the front and rear axles, meaning all-wheel drive is standard. Up front, the motor produces 202 hp and 243 pound-feet of torque; the less-powerful rear motor makes 134 hp and 144 lb-ft of torque. All in all, the system generates 225 hp, which is enough to rocket the 4,065-pound Rogue Hybrid from 0-60 mph in just 6.4 seconds. Nissan claims that's the quickest in its class, and that's incredibly important if you're the kind of compact crossover buyer who cares about that sort of thing. While that is very exciting, something that may be a bit of a letdown is the gas mileage the Rogue Hybrid achieves.

Nissan says the new crossover will get 41 mpg city, 36 mpg highway and 38 mpg combined. Sure, those are respectable numbers, but they're certainly behind the now-hybrid-only RAV4's 46 mpg city, 39 mpg highway and 42 mpg combined. The Rogue Hybrid asks what comfort and refinement are worth to you, because the experience behind the wheel of Nissan's vehicle is a far more pleasant one. It's much quieter and far more upscale than the Toyota, and the rest of its competitors. Plus, in day-to-day life, the near-EV-like driving experience it delivers is far more pleasant than the admittedly rattly four-popper noises of Toyota's hybrid system. Adding in the fact there's no transmission to shift makes things even smoother — no, there blissfully isn't even a CVT. My time with the Rogue Hybrid made me very curious as to how this powertrain technology would feel in a more luxurious application, like an Infiniti, where comfort is key and efficiency isn't nearly as important. I've got a feeling it would be rather lovely.

Stepping on the gas pedal gave me the exact sort of acceleration feel I'd get from a conventional electric vehicle, just with the added hum of that three-cylinder in the distance. Nissan did a solid job of muffling its noise as much as possible, so for the most part, I didn't even notice it was running.

There are some familiar FP1 names there who have already driven in 2026, but Mexico is probably the most interesting roster of the season, with three names in particular standing out as significant in F1 driver market terms…
Cadillac believes Colton Herta is now just one point away from finally earning the 40 he needs to successfully apply for an F1 superlicence.
That's if he can successfully complete the mandated 100 kilometres of running in FP1 when he takes over Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac on Friday.

article_paragraphs: BMW is giving its M cars yellow DRLs, but this M5 prototype didn't get the message

BMW's new 3 Series is only weeks away from arriving in dealerships, and it looks like the facelifted 5 Series and M5 won't be too far behind. Fresh spy shots from Germany show the latest prototypes of the hot PHEV midsize sedan are fitted with production lights, a sign that a debut isn't far off.

Each of the two headlight bodies has a pair of slim LED DRLs arranged horizontally, rather than diagonally, as on the new 3 Series and electric i3. And zooming in on the images appears to show LED headlight units located under each DRL. BMW's big 7 Series sedan and X7 have split headlights treatments, but the 5 is sticking with a more conventional layout.

There is one important change, though, still to come to this M5's lighting setup before its ready for an official reveal. BMW has begun fitting yellow DRLs to mark out its M cars, like the new M350 , but this car has white ones. That suggests they're from the regular 5 Series, which is getting the same facelift treatment.

This prototype is still wearing heavy disguise over the kidney grille area and down the center of the hood. But now that the 3 Series is out, we have a good idea of what we'll find underneath that camo when the M5 makes its debut, probably in the first half of next year. That plate riveted to the hood must hide a deep gulley that culminates in BMW's trademark roundel badge, and the visor-like face of the smaller sedan will be replicated.

We're not seeing any obvious changes to this M5's rear, but the taillights are sure to get a subtly different LED graphic to help distinguish the car wearing them as a facelift – or what brand fans know as Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) – model.

And the M5's trademark quad exhaust tailpipe arrangement isn't going anywhere. That's been an M5 staple since the introduction of the first V8 M5, the E39, back in 1999 . The M5 switched to V10 power after that, before coming back to a V8, this time with twin turbochargers. And the current G90-code M5 that arrived in 2024 added plug-in hybrid assistance.

Going the hybrid route added a staggering 1,045 lbs (474 kg) to the M5's curb weight, but it also pushed total output to 717 horsepower (727 PS). Will this new-look M5 and its M5 Touring wagon twin get more ponies? BMW tends not to mess with its M powertrains at facelift time, so we're not banking on it. But we wouldn't be surprised if it leveraged BMW's clever new battery technology to improve on a 38-mile (62 km) WLTP range. That figure looks off the pace in an era of hybrids like the Range Rover Sport that can do over 70 miles (113 km) on a charge.

title: Why 'motocross' Sepang wasn't fixed
raw_summary: Multiple MotoGP riders have expressed concerns about the state of the Sepang International Circuit’s asphalt ahead of this weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix. A track already in need of resurfacing was further damaged by this month’s replacement Formula 1 race - running as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' in lieu of a race at the country's actual Sakhir track - to the point where it has now, according to some racers, become borderline dangerous to ride on.

article_paragraphs: Multiple MotoGP riders have expressed concerns about the state of the Sepang International Circuit’s asphalt ahead of this weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix.

A track already in need of resurfacing was further damaged by this month’s replacement Formula 1 race - running as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' in lieu of a race at the country's actual Sakhir track - to the point where it has now, according to some racers, become borderline dangerous to ride on.

Last resurfaced 10 years ago, the track was due to receive new asphalt ahead of this year’s MotoGP event, but delays to logistics caused by the geopolitical situation in the Middle East saw this work pushed back.
And the high downforce generated by F1 cars has caused considerable further degradation of the track at a number of key corners.

The unexpected arrival of F1 also saw remedial work planing the straights, in an attempt to remove bumps - which appears to have exacerbated the situation in other regards. The track is now shedding stones due to the forces generated by the bikes as they accelerate.

MotoGP had a similar issue at the second round of the 2026 season at the inaugural Brazilian Grand Prix in Goiania, where the main race on Sunday was cut in distance at the last minute as the track started to crumble during the Moto2 and Moto3 races.

And, speaking to riders after the opening day of practice on Friday, a number were less than happy that their request to resurface after testing hadn’t been accomplished given the state of the asphalt right now.
“The asphalt is, pardon my French, f**ked,” Jack Miller told the media.
