article_paragraphs: The Audi Formula 1 team has announced that veteran engineer and director Beat Zehnder will leave the operation at the end of 2026.
The 60-year-old Swiss was part of the Sauber organisation - which Audi took over to enter F1 - since even before its grand prix debut in 1993.
He went from being a mechanic there, with its factory-backed Mercedes operation in World Sportscars, to serving as team manager for much of Sauber's time in F1.

Team founder Peter Sauber stepped away from the team in 2012 and retired in 2016, as Finn Rausing's Longbow Finance took over the team. Zehnder retained a senior role then, but shortly following Audi's takeover he transitioned to a factory-based role.
He will now exit the project entirely "following the restructuring of operations ahead of the 2027 season".
Zehnder, who had worked at 601 consecutive F1 grands prix, "has been a mentor to hundreds of team members and drivers who have passed through Hinwil over the years", Audi wrote.
"We thank him for 39 years of outstanding service and wish him all the very best for the future."

title: Why F1 teams and manufacturers face more unknowns in Mexico than ever
raw_summary: At 2,286 metres above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is by far the highest-altitude venue on the Formula 1 calendar. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways. Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways. Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico.
article_paragraphs: At 2,286 metres above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is by far the highest-altitude venue on the Formula 1 calendar. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways.

Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico. At altitude, there are fewer oxygen molecules per cubic metre, meaning the turbo has to work harder to get the same amount of oxygen into the engine as it would at sea level.

The turbo has to spin considerably faster to achieve the required boost pressure and airflow, which presents a challenge not only in terms of outright performance but also reliability, with the turbo operating at significantly higher temperatures than under normal conditions.

This is always a challenge in Mexico and also explains why George Russell pointed so clearly towards Ferrari as the favourites during Thursday's press conference, given that the Scuderia is widely known in the paddock to have a smaller turbo than many of its rivals. A smaller turbine wheel has less mass and inertia, allowing the turbo to spool up more quickly after the driver presses the throttle.

This helps to keep turbo lag to a minimum, and that is precisely what promises to be a hugely important factor this weekend. In 2026, this challenge has become considerably greater than before because the MGU-H has been removed and can no longer assist in counteracting turbo lag.

“Last year, we had the MGU-H, so we had some support from MGU-H, but this year we don't have the MGU-H anymore, so that makes it quite challenging,” Honda’s chief engineer Shintaro Orihara said when asked about the challenges by Autosport.

“For example, even just in idle conditions, we had MGU-H support to get enough boost pressure, but this year we don't have any support even in idle conditions. That is a big difference from last year and therefore turbo lag is the most interesting and important topic at this track. I think that is not only the case for Honda, but for all manufacturers. They will all struggle with turbo lag at this track.”

Besides turbo lag, there is another important factor: the extent to which the engine’s power output is affected. If manufacturers cannot achieve the desired level of turbo boost in general, Honda says this could also have consequences for how it has to run the internal combustion engine – in other words, in the worst-case scenario, with a lower power output.

article_paragraphs: MotoGP championship leader Marc Marquez completed a clean sweep of Friday practice at Sepang, as Jorge Martin withdrew from the afternoon session after three laps.

Martin, who broke his wrist in a crash last Saturday at Phillip Island but has foregone rest for now in favour of trying to keep his title chances alive, did 12 laps in the morning but had to end his day early.

"Together with the doctors, we decided all together to not continue and wait tonight and see tomorrow morning, because, at the moment, if he [Martin] wants to make the laptime, to make the time attack, it's for him difficult to manage the force," Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora explained to MotoGP.com.
"So it's better to take no risk, absolutely, and we decided all together, together in particular with the doctors, Dr. [Angel] Charte, that we don't go forward during the session."

Q2 by virtue of a top-10 spot would have been a monumental longshot for Martin anyway, whereas for Marquez it looked a foregone conclusion - despite him crashing at the final corner in the early phase of the session.
He bounced back from this to head his Sepang-specialist brother Alex by 0.109s at the conclusion of the session, despite sacrificing the opportunity of one final run on a fresh soft rear.

Trackhouse Aprilia rider Ai Ogura had looked off for much of the day but uncharacteristically came alive when it came to single-lap attempts, moving up to third, ahead of the lead KTM of Pedro Acosta and VR46 Ducati rider Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia), Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM), Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM), Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) and the returning Joan Mir (Honda) picked up the remaining Q2 spots.

The news sent LiveWire’s stock plunging more than 40% on Thursday morning as the company withdrew its full-year financial guidance.
article_paragraphs: Harley-Davidson-born electric motorcycle maker LiveWire has issued a troubling warning about its financial future, announcing that it has substantial doubt about its ability to continue operating as a going concern. The news sent LiveWire’s stock plunging more than 40% on Thursday morning as the company withdrew its full-year financial guidance.

The announcement comes despite some signs of improving sales, with LiveWire reporting a 38% increase in third-quarter revenue to $7.9 million and a 21% rise in motorcycle unit sales. However, the company continues to burn through cash, reporting a net loss of $18.6 million for the quarter.
LiveWire’s cash reserves have also dwindled significantly, falling from $82.8 million at the end of 2025 to just $39.9 million as of September 30, 2026.

The company has now formed a special restructuring committee to explore potential financing arrangements, strategic partnerships, investments, or even a sale. It also withdrew its previous guidance projecting a $70 million to $80 million operating loss for 2026.
The financial warning comes at a particularly pivotal moment for LiveWire, which is preparing to launch its most affordable electric motorcycles yet.

The upcoming LiveWire S4 Honcho series represents a major departure from the company’s existing premium electric motorcycles, offering smaller, lighter, and significantly more affordable models designed to attract a much broader audience of riders with a starting price below US $5,000.

The lower prices could dramatically increase LiveWire’s sales volumes, especially as the company attempts to move beyond the relatively small market for high-dollar electric motorcycles. The Honcho lineup is also expected to help lower the barrier to entry for new riders, with approachable electric motorcycles that eliminate the complexity of clutch and gear shifting.

article_paragraphs: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K.

Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the BZ in the North American market)

The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits.

The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation.
For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio.
But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles.

Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues.

“This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement.

article_paragraphs: The ALSO TM-B is one of the most technologically interesting new e-bikes to hit the road in years, largely because it does away with one of the most fundamental parts of a bicycle: the mechanical connection between the pedals and rear wheel. With only copper wires connecting the pedals to the rear wheel, the TM-B is one of the most revolutionary new e-bikes in years.
But that raises an obvious question. What happens when the battery dies?
One early Launch Edition owner, Aaron Draczynski, decided to find out by deliberately running his TM-B down toward empty to see whether ALSO’s drive-by-wire system would leave him stranded.
He shared the experience on YouTube, discovering that the answer is surprisingly complicated – and involves something called “Infinite Turtle Mode.”

Unlike a conventional e-bike, where the rider’s pedaling mechanically turns the rear wheel through a chain or belt, the ALSO TM-B uses a pedal-by-wire drivetrain. Pedaling generates electricity, while the rear wheel is driven electrically.

That arrangement enables all sorts of interesting features, including electronically simulated gearing and the Launch Edition’s massive Level 10 boost mode, which can multiply rider input by up to 10 times.
But it also means there’s no traditional drivetrain to fall back on when the battery runs out.

The owner began his experiment at 31% charge and quickly watched the bike progressively restrict its maximum assist as the battery drained closer to empty. From 23% to 13%, the maximum boost dropped from Level 8 to Level 5 as it began conserving battery.

article_paragraphs: Jorge Martin can continue with his bid to keep his MotoGP championship chase alive, having been passed fit to race in the Malaysian Grand Prix with a broken wrist.
But while he has cleared that first hurdle, his weekend got off to a mixed start in Friday morning practice at Sepang.
The good news was that he managed to complete the full session, covering 12 laps across multiple runs, and going back out again for the practice starts at the end of the session.

That mileage and his Aprilia team talking confidently about its strategy for Martin through the weekend immediately suggested he was expecting to pass the mandatory medical check after the session - which he duly did half an hour later.

Limiting the title fight damage looks tough, though. While Martin improved from being four seconds off the pace on his tentative first run, he was still 1.835s down and 20th fastest at the end of the session, so will need to find substantially more pace to have a shot at scoring significant points.
And the identity of the pacesetter was bad news for Martin too, with his title rival Marc Marquez's Ducati a comfortable fastest by 0.474s over Martin's Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi.

KTM's Pedro Acosta matched Bezzecchi's time in third, while Acosta's stablemates Enea Bastianini and Brad Binder used fresher tyres to go fourth and fifth at the end, just as sixth-placed Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) did.
While one of Aprilia's injured duo looks set to continue with the weekend, the other was ruled out during practice one.

The early foundations of Goal Zero were established back in 2007, when Robert Workman, who had owned Utah’s Provo Craft & Novelty for 30 years, founded a nonprofit called TIFIE Humanitarian to help Congolese villagers run their own small businesses. When out in the field, his team had nowhere to charge their equipment, and a simple 90 watt solar panel he priced in the nearby city of Kinshasa cost $2,000 USD.

As a result of this, Workman went out and had his own system built. The first version was called the GoBe, it paired a battery with a solar panel and an LED light, and it was being tested in Congolese villages by 2008. It was a simple arrangement and a full day of charging in the sun would give hours of light at night, plus power for other small devices.

Goal Zero launched as a Utah-based company in mid-2009 with the Escape 150, a 13 lb power pack, and sales took off from there. In 2013 it ranked 9th on the Inc. 500 list of the country’s fastest-growing private companies, with an incredible three-year growth rate of 16,981%.

The company’s portable Nomad solar panels debuted in 2011, and then in 2012 came the 103 lb Yeti 1250 power station, which the company says sold out within a day and a half. NRG Energy bought the company in 2014, and lithium-battery Yetis arrived in 2017. BioLite acquired Goal Zero from NRG in April 2025. The company still operates from Draper, Utah, and it now has dozens of products on offer, and they ship around the world.

The Boulder 100 Solar Briefcase from Goal Zero it’s a folding two-panel solar system that provides up to 100 watts, or 50 watts per panel. It was developed to give campers the toughness of a rigid glass solar panel in a size that packs flat and fits neatly in a car trunk.

title: Eugene Becomes 5th Oregon City to Adopt Home Energy Score Requirement
raw_summary: Eugene, Oregon — In a 6-1 vote on Wednesday, October 28th , the Eugene City Council adopted the Residential Energy Performance Disclosure Requirement ordinance , a policy commonly referred to as a Home Energy Score requirement. The vote places Eugene among four other Oregon cities , Portland, Hillsboro, Milwaukie and Bend, that have similar Home Energy Score ordinances. The vote comes in the midst of a larger trend of cities adopting a variety of policies to aid community members navigating home retrofits and efficiency upgrades as support for building electrification grows in Oregon, and nationwide in the face of efforts to undermine existing climate policy at the Federal level. “We applaud the City Council for taking this common sense step and establishing a home energy score requirement in Eugene. This policy will ensure that home buyers have the information that they need to make informed choices when making what is often the most important financial decision in their lives,” said Bethany Cotton, Conservation Director with Cascadia Wildlands . “The vote is an important step forward to tackling building emissions, reducing energy costs, and meeting the City’s Climate Recovery Ordinance goals to reduce emissions by 50% by 2030.”

article_paragraphs: Eugene, Oregon — In a 6-1 vote on Wednesday, October 28th , the Eugene City Council adopted the Residential Energy Performance Disclosure Requirement ordinance , a policy commonly referred to as a Home Energy Score requirement. The vote places Eugene among four other Oregon cities , Portland, Hillsboro, Milwaukie and Bend, that have similar Home Energy Score ordinances. The vote comes in the midst of a larger trend of cities adopting a variety of policies to aid community members navigating home retrofits and efficiency upgrades as support for building electrification grows in Oregon, and nationwide in the face of efforts to undermine existing climate policy at the Federal level.

“We applaud the City Council for taking this common sense step and establishing a home energy score requirement in Eugene. This policy will ensure that home buyers have the information that they need to make informed choices when making what is often the most important financial decision in their lives,” said Bethany Cotton, Conservation Director with Cascadia Wildlands . “The vote is an important step forward to tackling building emissions, reducing energy costs, and meeting the City’s Climate Recovery Ordinance goals to reduce emissions by 50% by 2030.”

The adoption of the ordinance is the first major step from the City to reduce building emissions since the Ninth Circuit’s April 2023 decision on the Berkley building electrification requirement, which invalidated the City’s February 2023 residential building electrification ordinance. The passage of this policy in Eugene also marks more than 1 million Oregonians living in a jurisdiction with a Home Energy Score disclosure policy, representing nearly 1 in 4 Oregon residents (24.4%).

“The Ninth Circuit’s disastrous decision in 2023 set Eugene, and cities across the region, back for years on climate action and energy efficiency. While this policy is just a small step, it is a critical signal that the City is ready to begin moving decisively to regaining lost time and transitioning away from polluting fossil fuels,” said Dylan Plummer, Deputy Director of the Sierra Club’s Clean Heat Campaign . “We look forward to supporting Eugene and other local governments to continue to push the ball forward on common sense policies to require building decarbonization.”

The ordinance requires that a home energy score assessment be conducted and posted when a home is listed for sale. These assessments review the average energy cost of a home, evaluating existing appliances, heating systems, windows, doors and insulation, as well as the climate emissions associated with the home, and score the house’s energy use on a scale of one to ten. The reports include recommendations for how to improve a home’s energy efficiency and reduce emissions, and include key information about existing incentives and subsidies at the local, state and federal level.

“Eugene Water and Electric Board customers can access significant incentives to support home electrification and energy efficiency including zero interest loans and cash subsidies for weatherization and heat pumps for space and water heating. Sadly, these programs are deeply underutilized because many folks are not aware they exist,” said Meredith Tufts, Coalition Coordinator with the Fossil Free Eugene Coalition . “The Home Energy Score requirement will ensure that every new home owner has the information they need to take advantage of these programs to reduce their energy bills and climate pollution.

We already knew Honda was planning to make its Passport "more masculine," but we had no idea this midsize SUV could become an off-road beast. No, it may not be as cool as a Baja-ready classic Porsche 911 , but Honda gave this rig an engine derived from an endurance racing prototype with a total power output of 1,300 hp (969 kW) — and its sights are set on an overall Baja 1000 victory. None of this is very shocking given that the truck comes from Honda Racing .

Honda's new Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck will debut at the 2026 SEMA Show, and it was developed with Mason Motorsports. Menzies Motorsports is also a partner, and two-time Baja 1000 winner Bryce Menzies will drive it in Score World Desert Championship's top Trophy Truck class, where Honda says it will be the first hybrid vehicle to compete in this class. This isn't your mom's Passport, so let's talk a little about the racing technology under this trophy truck.

Today's Trophy Trucks leverage 9.0-liter V8s. Honda says that its 2.4-liter V6-based powertrain will make more power. The engine uses a pair of turbochargers and an 800-volt hybrid system to help it achieve its somewhat wild 1,300 hp figure. Interestingly, the V6 shares very close ties with the engine in Acura's ARX-06 GTP race car , giving it some endurance racing credentials, including victories at Daytona and Sebring. That said, surviving Baja will present a different set of challenges.

The hybrid system here is bespoke and a direct product of HRC's work. The battery uses a previous-generation Formula 1-style pouch cell inside a carbon fiber case. Assembly and validation all take place within a clean room at the brand's Santa Clarita headquarters. Of course, the battery is just one piece of the overall system.

Honda says the truck also features brake-by-wire systems on each axle, adaptive traction control, and what it's calling AI power deployment. Proprietary software ties together the powertrain, chassis, and energy management, with adjustments possible during the race. Honda hasn't detailed the battery's capacity or how much power the electric side contributes.

The rear-mounted engine mates to Mason-developed five-speed transmission, and the all-wheel drive setup uses two rear driveshafts, with individual angled gearsets at the rear wheels replacing a conventional ring-and-pinion arrangement. Up front, portal gearsets at the hubs help provide ground clearance. As the photos make clear, this isn't a simple build.

If there's anything here that hints at the production Passport outside of the name, it's very selective sections of the body. Each panel is carbon fiber to save weight. Deep channels behind the front wheels manage airflow, while high-mounted exhaust outlets sit among fins behind the cockpit. Honda also shaped the cab to channel air toward a cooler mounted low and far back in the truck.

title: The Zombie Engine: How Brussels Bureaucrats Are Breathing False Life Into Combustion
raw_summary: If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. But in the EU Parliament, this fiction is being drafted into law. If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at.
article_paragraphs: If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. But in the EU Parliament, this fiction is being drafted into law.

If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. Yet inside the corridors of the European Parliament, this exact fiction is being drafted into law.

Under heavy pressure from the fossil fuel lobby and legacy carmakers, EU lawmakers are preparing to endorse a bizarre new regulatory beast: the VEEF, or “Vehicle Exclusively running on Eligible Fuels.” In plain English, these are standard combustion-engine cars promised to run exclusively on liquid biofuels or e-fuels. In exchange for that promise, Brussels plans to grant them a legal tailpipe emission score of zero.

It is regulatory alchemy at its worst. Cloaked in the seductive language of “technological neutrality,” this proposal creates an escape hatch for an obsolete technology, all while setting up ordinary European drivers for an expensive logistical nightmare.
It is just another desperate tactic to extend the life of the combustion engine by any means possible.

To understand the absurdity of the biofuel car, look at what actually happens in the engine. It’s still the exact same combustion. A piston firing on biofuels produces the same toxic cocktail of nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and fine particulates that has choked European cities for decades. Labeling these cars “zero-emission” launders the pollution through a regulatory loophole and continues to foster emission-induced pathology.

Nor does it save the climate. The average biofuel blend available today delivers a modest 20% to 40% emissions saving compared to fossil fuels. When you factor in the indirect land-use change of first-generation crop biofuels ploughing up forests to grow food for engines, crop-based biofuel cars actually emit 23% more greenhouse gases than a standard petrol car.

Biofuel cars are being sold to the public under the guise of affordability, yet running them is punishingly expensive. Hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biodiesel costs around €13 per 100 kilometers to run, compared to roughly €7 for an equivalent electric vehicle. Pushing drivers toward these cars locks households into volatile, high fuel costs at the exact moment renewable electricity prices and battery costs are tumbling.

raw_title: Misconceptions about Mobility Growth
title: Misconceptions about Mobility Growth
raw_summary: Higher speed is the main cause of mobility growth. When people go faster, they will travel further. This is the shortest summary of the history of passenger mobility . An illustrative example is the high-speed rail connection between Paris and Lyon. After its opening in 1981, commuters were able to travel daily between these two cities. This was not possible before.
summary: Higher speed is the main cause of mobility growth. When people go faster, they will travel further. This is the shortest summary of the history of passenger mobility . An illustrative example is the high-speed rail connection between Paris and Lyon. After its opening in 1981, commuters were able to travel daily between these two cities.
article_paragraphs: Higher speed is the main cause of mobility growth. When people go faster, they will travel further. This is the shortest summary of the history of passenger mobility .

An illustrative example is the high-speed rail connection between Paris and Lyon. After its opening in 1981, commuters were able to travel daily between these two cities. This was not possible before.
More generally, the rise in both ownership and speed of the car after the second World War, allowed for increasing distances from home to work, to school, shops, hospitals and friends.

The average distance a person travels per day tripled since 1960: from 10 to 30 (Dutch data). This growth is entirely caused by car use, being from door-to-door faster than both public transport and the bicycle.

Many empirical studies underpin that speed is the main cause of mobility growth. Total travel time is roughly constant : a person in a city or country travels on average 1.1 hour per day. When travel time is constant, higher speed inevitably leads to longer trips.

However, conventional wisdom makes us believe in other causes of mobility growth. Such as, rising income, decreasing costs of car driving, working from home or changing preferences in favour or against cars. The dominance of speed is overlooked in standard views by traffic engineers and politicians alike. Even statistics on average speed in urban and rural areas are scarce. This omission hides important consequences for transport policy. Here are three:.

Road building in congested areas does not solve congestion. Directly after opening, there is less congestion and car speed increases. However, after only a few years this gain disappears, because extra road capacity attracts extra traffic . One of the empirical studies showing this, is aptly titled “The Fundamental Law of Road Congestion”.

Secondly, when average car speed does not increase anymore, the growth in car mobility will end. This is the reality in rich countries with a mature motorway grid. Average car speed stabilized in the Netherlands since the turn of the century, and consequently car mobility per person even decreased by 3% between 2005 and 2019 (the last year before the Covid lockdowns). The UK, Spain, Belgium, Sweden and Luxemburg also show a drop in car mobility per person over the same period. Other countries will follow. Neglecting car speed as the main driver behind traffic growth results in traffic forecasts that are systematically too high.
bullet_points: Higher speed is the main cause of mobility growth.
When people go faster, they will travel further.
This is the shortest summary of the history of passenger mobility .

title: It’s Not Enough To Electrify More. We Must Electrify Better.

article_paragraphs: EVs and other electric products are emerging not only as a climate strategy but also as a question of affordability, economic competitiveness, public health, consumer experience, energy security, and resilience to volatile fuel markets.

At 5 a.m., an electric bus glides out of its depot after charging overnight, ready to carry children to school without spewing diesel fumes. As the city stirs, heat pumps have already brought homes and offices to a comfortable temperature, using far less energy than their gas boiler counterparts. By midday, solar power charges delivery vehicles, cools warehouses, and helps factories run their most energy-intensive processes. Then, as millions of people return home and plug in their cars, smart chargers quietly schedule charging for later, when electricity is cheaper and the grid less busy.

Scenes like these are beginning to emerge across the globe: electric buses in Delhi, electric heat pumps warming homes through Norwegian winters, electric trucks entering Chinese freight and construction fleets. The shift to electrification has begun.

Most people will experience this transition not as an energy-system revolution, but as a quieter journey, a more comfortable home, a lower bill, or cleaner air. But taken together, these everyday changes mark an epochal shift in the global economy: from one built on burning fossil fuels to one driven by clean electricity, efficient technologies, and flexible demand.

But what exactly is electrification? How can using more electricity benefit people and the planet? And what happens when millions of new electric vehicles, appliances, buildings, and factories connect to a power system already under strain ?

Put simply, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly—gasoline-fueled cars, diesel buses, gas boilers, industrial furnaces, etc.—with alternatives powered by electricity. (Ideally clean electricity, but more on that later).

This shift is moving center stage not only as a climate strategy but also as a question of affordability, economic competitiveness, public health, consumer experience, energy security, and resilience to volatile fuel markets .

Yet the case for electrification is more compelling—and more interesting—than simply switching fuels. To understand its potential, we first need to look at how far electrification has progressed, why electric technologies use less energy and are cheaper to run, and what needs to happen to ensure electrification brings about societal and environmental benefits. Here, we dive deep into the current state of electrification and how to accelerate it in the right way.

title: This Odd Subaru WRX Prototype Looks Like A Wacky Longtail
raw_summary: Subaru has been building the current-generation WRX for five years and has introduced a plethora of special, limited-edition versions in different markets , including Japan and the U.S. Despite all of this, it still hasn't launched a proper STI model. Could this mystery prototype offer a glimpse of the long-awaited STI, or will it be another package that leaves Subaru fans feeling underwhelmed? Our spy photographers recently snapped this black WRX testing at the Nürburgring, and from the front, it looks pretty much exactly the same as any other. article_paragraphs: Subaru has been building the current-generation WRX for five years and has introduced a plethora of special, limited-edition versions in different markets , including Japan and the U.S. Despite all of this, it still hasn't launched a proper STI model. Could this mystery prototype offer a glimpse of the long-awaited STI, or will it be another package that leaves Subaru fans feeling underwhelmed?

Our spy photographers recently snapped this black WRX testing at the Nürburgring, and from the front, it looks pretty much exactly the same as any other. There's the same familiar grille, bumper, air intakes, and large hood scoop. It all looks rather uninspiring. What makes this test car interesting is its rear end, and it has us scratching our heads.

New panels have been attached to the rear quarters of the WRX and now extend outward, sitting roughly in line with the taillights. Similarly, a new lip spoiler sits in line with these panels, making this prototype look almost like a WRX Longtail. As a way to tweak the car's aerodynamic properties, Subaru's design is certainly intriguing. It's also vastly different from the large fixed rear wings we've come to expect of new WRX models, and any potential future STI. A small piece of camouflage is also visible on a unique rear diffuser.

What's particularly curious about this prototype is that everything other than the rear looks like a normal WRX. It doesn't have enlarged air intakes or bigger brakes as you'd expect for a high-performance STI model . In fact, this prototype doesn't even appear to have the same beefy Brembo brake calipers as the regular model, so it seems unlikely that it has any additional power under the hood.

This raises more questions than answers. Is Subaru simply developing yet another special edition WRX with a distinctive rear? Is it planning to release these new rear panels as an optional extra for the standard model? Or is Subaru simply investigating ways to make the performance sedan slightly more aerodynamically efficient? Either way, it's definitely interesting.

These spy images have emerged just a week after Subaru announced it's bringing back a manual transmission option to the standard WRX in Japan. This transmission is unrelated to the TY75 six-speed of the U.S. model and is instead the same TY85 gearbox as the previous-generation WRX STI. Subaru is clearly willing to invest significant time and resources in the current WRX, but whether that leads to a new STI remains to be seen.

raw_title: Everything we learned on day one of F1's Mexican GP
title: Everything we learned on day one of F1's Mexican GP
raw_summary: The uniquely demanding challenge of Formula 1's highest-altitude race gets even tougher in Mexico this year, and there are some lingering frustrations from last weekend's grand prix in the United States too. This year’s Mexican Grand Prix will be the first of the modern era where F1’s hybrid V6 engines have run without the MGU-H.
summary: The uniquely demanding challenge of Formula 1's highest-altitude race gets even tougher in Mexico this year, and there are some lingering frustrations from last weekend's grand prix in the United States too. This year’s Mexican Grand Prix will be the first of the modern era where F1’s hybrid V6 engines have run without the MGU-H.
article_paragraphs: The uniquely demanding challenge of Formula 1's highest-altitude race gets even tougher in Mexico this year, and there are some lingering frustrations from last weekend's grand prix in the United States too.
This year’s Mexican Grand Prix will be the first of the modern era where F1’s hybrid V6 engines have run without the MGU-H.
Mexico City’s altitude has traditionally put extra strain on the turbochargers as the lack of air density requires everything to function at higher RPM.

According to Honda’s trackside engineering chief, Shintaro Orihara, the loss of the MGU-H for 2026 makes the process of achieving sufficient boost pressure even more difficult here, calling it “quite challenging” to run without the complicated and expensive component ditched under this season’s new engine regulations.
“Last year we had MGU-H, so we have some support from MGU-H, but this year we don't have MGU-H, so it's quite challenging,” he said.

“For example, just only for idle, in idle condition, we have MGU-H support to get enough boost pressure [in 2025], but this year we don't have any support. Even in idle, we have big difference from last year.

“Then also, turbo lag, that's most interesting or important topic in this track. I think not only Honda, but also all manufacturers, they will struggle with turbo lag, or [find it] challenging for turbo lag in this track.

“Also, not only turbo lag, normally in Mexico, turbocharger speed is quite high to get enough airflow. Then we may... we need to check, but we may have some restriction on engine operation condition, if in the worst case.

summary: The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade. According to German news source DW , the company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion for the period July 1 through September 30, 2027. A massive write down of its stake in Porsche was responsible for much of the loss, while its sales in China continued to decline at an alarming rate.
article_paragraphs: The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade. According to German news source DW , the company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion for the period July 1 through September 30, 2027. A massive write down of its stake in Porsche was responsible for much of the loss, while its sales in China continued to decline at an alarming rate.

“The nine month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act quickly and decisively,” chief financial officer Arno Antlitz said in a video statement. DW was quick to point out that the cockamamie tariffs on cars imported into the US from Germany were another significant factory in the dismal financial picture for Volkswagen. The US is Porsche’s largest market and those tariffs have had a devastating effect on its sales in America.

For the third quarter, Volkswagen reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion — four times greater then the loss is posted last year in the third quarter. That marks the company’s worst performance since the Dieselgate crisis in 2015. Revenue from sales fell by 6.3 percent year on year to €75.3 billion. Deliveries to customers, unit sales, and unit production numbers all dipped by roughly 15 percent as the company reduced production levels in an attempt to adjust factory output to match lower demand.

For 2026 so far, the company has had gross sales of €233.4 billion, which was virtually the same as last year, but sales volume was off 11 percent compared to 2025, so it is selling fewer cars but at higher prices. Operating profit was just €0.1 billion, compared with €5.4 billion a year ago. But so-called “special items” totaling €8.7 billion — including a non-cash write down of €6.4 billion on Porsche assets — led to that nearly negligible operating profit.

For the year, Volkswagen now expects its profit margin to be just 1 percent — far less than the 5 percent it projected at the start of the year. The only bright spot in the financial picture for Volkswagen is that sales of battery electric cars are up 39 percent year on year.

Volkswagen’s first joint venture in China was with SAIC in 1984. At that time, China knew next to nothing about manufacturing high quality automobiles. Now more then 40 years later, the tables have turned and China is making what are perhaps the highest quality automobiles in the world. Volkswagen, which was once the teacher, is now the student. If it is to survive, it may be because of the contributions of its Chinese partners — SAIC, FAW, Anhui, and Xpeng.

Together, they have created Vega, a new technology package comprised of software, electronics, and a dedicated EV platform, making Volkswagen the only non-Chinese automaker with a locally developed technology foundation represented in the Chinese market. While the package will first be used for cars made and sold exclusively in China, the company hints it may become part of an export campaign. Sharp eyed readers will immediately spot the irony of a company that is being hammered by Chinese imports in its home market becoming a Chinese import itself, at least in some markets.

The China Main Platform (CMP) is designed for battery-electric and plug-in hybrid models in the A-segment. It is expected to achieve a CLTC range of over 600 km, with an efficient energy consumption of around 11 kWh per 100 km. Charging from 30 to 80 per cent will take 25 minutes. For the premium segment, the China Scalable Platform (CSP) features 850 volt architecture, which makes charging from 10 to 80 per cent in just 13 minutes possible. Models built on the CSP architecture are expected to have a range of 800 km or more, with energy consumption below 13 kWh per 100 km.

raw_summary: Profit-hemorrhaging Volkswagen made headlines last week when it announced it would remotely limit some customer-owned ID 4s battery capacity to prevent owners from charging above 80% in response to a battery fire recall . The root cause of the fires is not currently known, and both Volkswagen and Audi only suspect that 0.1% of their respective cars involved in these recalls actually have the defect, but EV fires are serious and seriously dangerous events, so it pays to err on the side of caution.

Neither Volkswagen nor Audi recommends that owners park their cars outside, nor did they issue a "do not drive" warning, but their primary precaution for owners is to avoid charging their cars above 80%. According to both Volkswagen and Audi's NHTSA recall reports , "...a state of charge above 80% may trigger thermal propagation within the high-voltage battery."

Volkswagen sent out an OTA update to all affected ID 4s that remotely limited the cars to 80% of their maximum charge, though owners had about a week to opt out of this forced limitation. Audi is not aware of any Q4 E-Trons that have caught fire due to this issue, and its owners haven't faced the same forced-limit treatment at the time of publish. Volkswagen is aware of 22 claims of incidents related to the recall between January 2024 and August 2026.

There is no official remedy from the automakers just yet. In the meantime, however, Volkswagen is sending stickers to affected owners so they may remind operators not to charge the battery above 80%. ID 4 owners are expected to be notified by November 27, while Audi Q4 E-Tron owners may not be notified until December 18. For owners trying to determine if their car is affected, VINs are searchable now on the NHTSA website .

Ford is also slashing the cost of its home EV charging and power management equipment.
article_paragraphs: Earlier this week, the Ford Motor Company dropped word that anyone with a home EV charger who buys its new Ford Fathom electric pickup truck will not have to shell out cash for an external, wall-mounted inverter for bidirectional charging. Ford is also slashing the cost of its home EV charging and power management equipment. That’s not all. The automaker is also on a mission to convince all 3,000 utilities in the US and Canada to help accelerate the uptake of bidirectional charging systems.

With bidirectional charging, EVs can do something that gasmobile can. They can feed electricity back into household wiring, transforming themselves into emergency backup generators without the noise, pollution, and fuel cost of gas or diesel generators.

EVs equipped with bidirectional charging can also provide ratepayers with more control over their utility bills. With a home EV charger in hand, ratepayers can recharge their batteries during off-peak periods to take advantage of off-peak discounts, and they can use those discounted kilowatts to power their home during peak periods when rates are higher.
Drivers can also recharge at off-site charging stations that offers discounted rates, and ferry those kilowatts back for use at home.
Either way, the home needs to be equipped with an inverter to convert the DC current of an EV battery into the AC current used in buildings.

Or not, as the case may be. As explained by Ford earlier this week, the forthcoming Fathom pickup will come with its own built-in inverter. By eliminating the expense of an external inverter, Ford aims to sweeten the EV affordability pot, and the company has tapped Fathom to showcase the strategy at an MSRP under $30,000 .

The missing link is the availability of utility-sponsored incentive programs that reward ratepayers for participating in managed demand programs. That includes rooftop solar, home energy storage systems, and even hot water heaters, with EV batteries being the icing on the cake.

“The opportunity is significant for utilities. But there are more than 3,000 utilities across the U.S. and Canada with largely unique interconnection processes,” Ford notes, drawing attention to another bottleneck limiting rapid uptake.

title: GM reaches $220M settlement over selling drivers’ private data
raw_summary: General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers. As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). This settlement does contain a new requirement that GM must have a third party assess the automaker’s compliance with the privacy program it has put in place.
summary: General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers. As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).
article_paragraphs: General Motors will pay $220 million to 36 states to settle allegations that it illegally sold private driving behavior and location information to data brokers.

As part of the settlement, GM must get drivers’ express consent before it collects or shares their driving and location data — terms that are in line with separate agreements it previously reached with California and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). This settlement does contain a new requirement that GM must have a third party assess the automaker’s compliance with the privacy program it has put in place.

The agreement announced Thursday settles a lawsuit brought by a coalition of attorneys general from 36 states that alleged GM had sold the information to data brokers, which in turn then sold it to insurance providers.

“This agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices,” GM said in an emailed statement. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”

The settlement comes more than two years after a New York Times report showed how GM and OnStar collected, used, and sold drivers’ precise geolocation data and driving behavior to third parties, including data brokers LexisNexis and Verisk. The data was collected through GM’s Smart Driver program, a free feature contained within its connected car apps that tracked and rated driving behaviors and seat belt use. Data brokers sold this information to insurance providers, which could affect customers’ rates, the NYT reported at the time.

GM discontinued Smart Driver in 2024, but that didn’t stop legal action. In January, the FTC finalized an order that bans GM and its OnStar telematics service from sharing certain consumer data. The FTC settlement, as well as the multistate one announced Thursday, also requires GM to be more transparent with its consumers and receive their explicit consent for certain collection.

The company now says it is focused on protecting the privacy of its customers and will no longer sell vehicle information that can be linked to an individual, their vehicle location, or how they drive. However, GM may still disclose anonymized data not tied to an individual with certain partners. GM has also updated the language in its privacy policy and created a consumer-facing Privacy Center.

The settlement and mandated changes to how GM handles customer driving data come as more sensor-laden vehicles equipped with computing power enter the market. Automakers have made large bets on software-centric vehicles that drivers and passengers can interact with and connect with other digital apps such as their calendar, messages, and email.

That Nürburg 460 represents the first car a pope (in this case Pius XI) used as an official vehicle, a direct gift from Mercedes in 1930. That actually wasn't the first attempt at giving a pope horsepower: in 1909, Archbishop John M. Farley of New York tried to give Pope Pius X an Itala. "Tried," since the pope refused it! Apparently he liked horse-drawn carriages better.

While everything on display will be a car that a pope officially used, the modern idea of a Popemobile with its signature transparent dome didn't emerge until 1980 with John Paul II's 230 G. That will be at the exhibition, which is pretty exciting. Prior to this innovation, the pope just rode around in the back seat, looking out the window. The current Popemobile is a Mercedes G580 EV , which Francis took one final ride in the day before he died . Today, you could spot Leo XIV riding around in it if you're at the Vatican.

summary: The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants. Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.
article_paragraphs: The $5.8 billion joint venture between Rivian and Volkswagen Group is expanding to include AI assistants.

Rivian is now licensing elements of its AI voice assistant technology to Volkswagen Group as part of the broader joint venture, according to the company’s third-quarter investor presentation released Thursday.

Rivian didn’t disclose the licensing fees, payment terms, or which Volkswagen vehicles will use the technology. However, the AI assistant, which recently rolled out to Riv i an vehicles , could make its Volkswagen debut in the automaker’s low-cost EV called the ID EVERY1 . The small four-door hatchback is slated to be the first VW vehicle to use Rivian’s software and electrical architecture under the joint venture established in 2024.

The joint venture between Rivian and VW Group has already expanded once before, at least financially. The companies initially announced a joint venture valued up to $5 billion , but within months VW upped its commitment to invest up to $5.8 billion in Rivian by 2027. The initial tie-up, formalized through an independent company that kicked off in November 2024, focused on bringing Rivian’s electrical architecture and software to Volkswagen’s next generation of vehicles.
Rivian described the expansion to include elements of its AI assistant technology as “a proof point for the extensibility of the platform we’ve built in-house.”

Rivian spent two years developing its AI assistant before showing it off last year. That development work continued longer than expected, with the assistant finally rolling out in May 2026 to its flagship R1S SUV, R1T pickup truck, and in October to its new midsize R2 SUV.

Rivian has big aspirations for its AI assistant, which allows drivers and passengers to interact with the vehicle and control certain functions. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe told TechCrunch onstage at Disrupt 2026 that the company has created its own in-house agentic framework that understands what action a person wants to take when they talk to the vehicle, and routes it to the right part of the car’s software. That capability could eventually allow Rivian vehicles to run AI agents created by other companies, including Anthropic.
The in-house AI assistant program also fits into Rivian’s push to become more vertically integrated — a strategy the company emphasized in its third-quarter earnings report.

Asked by Autosport whether he had seen driving standards gradually deteriorate in F1, Alonso clarified: "No, I think it's the same over the years.

article_paragraphs: Rivian has started delivering the first major hardware upgrade to its electric van since production began in 2021: a bigger LFP battery pack good for 30% more range, and a new dual-motor AWD version.

The company confirmed in its Q3 2026 shareholder presentation that deliveries of the new variants began in early October. That’s the first real spec bump for a van that has been stuck at about 160 miles of rated range for years.

Rivian first mentioned the upgrade in its Q4 2025 letter, which we covered in February when Amazon’s fleet of Rivian vans grew 50%. At the time, Rivian only said it was “developing” a larger battery and AWD to “expand EDV route coverage” in Amazon’s network.

Now it’s shipping. In today’s presentation, Rivian says the new variants are “specifically designed to expand route coverage into more rural networks,” with the AWD configuration and the bigger pack offering “a 30% increase in range.”

EPA certification documents for the 2027 EDV 700, issued September 17, list the new pack at 129 kWh usable. Rivian has marketed the current van with a 100 kWh LFP pack, so that’s roughly 29% more energy, which lines up with the 30% range claim.
The upgrade is limited to the bigger 700 van, the one with 652 cubic feet of cargo space. The smaller 500 keeps its existing pack and front-wheel drive.
The EPA filing gives unadjusted lab range figures, which always run high because they skip the correction for real-world driving:

Rivian rates the current 700 at “up to 160 miles.” Apply Rivian’s 30% to that and the new FWD van lands around 208 miles. Using the AWD van’s smaller 23% gain from the EPA tests, we estimate the dual-motor version at about 195 to 200 miles.

Except for January (+87.5%), Toyota’s EV sales have more than doubled every month this year compared with 2025.
The higher demand comes after Toyota and Lexus launched updated versions of their first-gen electric SUVs, the bZ4X (now the bZ in the US) and the RZ.

Toyota has added several new electric models, including the C-HR+ (C-HR in the US), bZ4X Touring (bZ Woodland in the US), and Urban Cruiser, while Lexus now offers the ES EV. Both brands will introduce a three-row electric SUV, which is expected to go on sale over the next few months.
According to data from Cleantechnica , the Toyota bZ4X became the 20th best-selling EV worldwide through August, with nearly 100,000 units sold.
While its EVs are catching on, Toyota Motor’s global sales fell for the third straight month in September.

Toyota sold 860,107 vehicles in September, down 2.2% from the previous year. The company said that although overall demand remained steady, sales in China fell, leading to lower overall sales than last year.

article_paragraphs: Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV.

While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000.

It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate.

The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian.

“In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday.

Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois.

Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year.

Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. Even cheaper versions are slated for 2027, which will be available for as low as $44,990.

The results beat Wall Street’s expectations, and Rivian is raising its 2026 guidance on every metric. But the car business is still losing money, and the R2 ramp made the automotive margin worse this quarter.

We already had the volume side. Rivian reported earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248 in the quarter, both records. Deliveries were up 46% from a year ago and 58% from Q2.

Analysts were looking for about $2.02 billion in revenue, an adjusted loss of $0.61 per share, and an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $576 million, according to Bloomberg consensus. Rivian beat all three.

The demand signals for the R2 are good. Rivian says reservation conversion for the launch edition trim stayed above its expectations, it added a second R2 production shift in Normal, Illinois, and demo drives jumped to over 103,000 in the quarter, up from 57,000 in Q2.

The problem is the automotive gross margin. Rivian’s automotive segment posted an $80 million gross loss in Q3, a -5% margin. That’s better than the $130 million loss a year ago, but worse than the $36 million loss (-3%) we saw in Q2 .

Rivian blames about $120 million of extra cost of revenue on the R2 ramp, compared to production at “more normalized levels.” And the quarter got help that won’t repeat on demand: $81 million in regulatory credit revenue and an IEEPA tariff refund receivable.
Strip out the credits and the automotive segment lost about $161 million at the gross level, or roughly $8,400 per vehicle delivered. Not great.

raw_summary: Someone send notice to The Villages: The Fiat Topolino has officially earned street-legal status in the United States. There’s one big caveat to that legality, though, which is that the tiny Topolino is designated as a low-speed vehicle (a.k.a. an LSV). Under the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s rules, LSVs are limited to a top speed of between 20 and 25 mph and a gross vehicle weight rating below 3000 pounds. Given that the Topolino’s 5-kWh battery and 8-horsepower motor already cap its max velocity at just 25 mph, there’s no surprise that it earned the LSV designation. The drawback of being branded an LSV is that you can’t drive it on roads with a posted speed limit of more than 35 mph, but you can cross over roads with a higher limit at intersections.

raw_title: Republican Anti-Flock Bill Might Ban All Automated Traffic Enforcement
title: Republican Anti-Flock Bill Might Ban All Automated Traffic Enforcement
raw_summary: The rise of mass automated license-plate-reader surveillance in recent years, its reckless implementation and rampant abuse by rank-and-file police officers have quickly become unacceptable to many Americans . So it's perhaps unsurprising that U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie and six co-sponsors introduced the Flock-Off Act in Congress last month. The bill proposed withdrawing all federal funding from any municipality with "covered camera system" operator contracts, not just with Flock. The bill's language would also cover automated speed and red light cameras. Massie, a Kentucky Republican who lost his primary in May, said his bill aims to prevent law enforcement from surveilling "law-abiding citizens." Despite good intentions, though, the lawmakers behind the Flock-Off Act seemingly didn't comprehend the ramifications of its catch-all wording. The only Democratic co-sponsor of the bill, California Rep. Ro Khanna, told Streetsblog , "I'm for speed and red light cameras. You don't have speed and red light cameras being abused by police officers." Currently, the Flock-Off Act exempts only cameras used for tolling and cameras placed within a mile of the country's northern and southern borders.

You don't have speed and red light cameras being abused by police officers." Currently, the Flock-Off Act exempts only cameras used for tolling and cameras placed within a mile of the country's northern and southern borders.

Flock's deployment of automated license-plate-reading cameras is fundamentally different from speed and red light cameras. The mass surveillance network captures every license plate that passes, creating a database accessible to virtually every Flock customer. Speed and red light cameras only trigger when they detect an infraction beyond a set threshold. This trigger also makes the cameras serve as a deterrent to drivers breaking the law. According to the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency , speeding dropped by 84% after it first deployed speed cameras in 2025. These cameras also eliminate the need for most traffic stops, which can lead to deadly police interactions either during the stop or in a high-speed pursuit.

Regardless of the outcome of next week's midterm elections, there's a legislative backlash coming for all license-plate-reading cameras. Only time will tell how extensive the restrictions will be if and when the final version of the bill is signed into law. It might seem like a lost cause to me and you, but Flock is desperately trying to salvage its reputation with the public and its massive government contracts. The surveillance company has distributed a handbook to law enforcement agencies on how to "own the narrative" regarding its camera system.

article_paragraphs: XPENG recently launched sales of the new L05 in China and began shipments to global markets. Having seen a camouflaged prototype in Munich a few months ago, I had the impression that it was basically a longer L03. Looking at the production model, other than a few added features and details, that initial impression seems to have been an accurate assessment.

Unlike some of XPENG’s models targeting more premium segments, the L03 and L05 are based on 400V architecture. 3C charging rate goes from 10-80% in around 20 minutes. Overall charge times will come out slightly ahead of a Tesla Model Y (also 400V), but not as fast as other models in China on higher voltage architectures.

In terms of length, the L03 measures 4650 mm, while the L05 increases to 4870 mm. That puts a Model Y in the middle at 4791 mm. The increase in size adds roughly 50 kg to the weight of the L05 across trim levels.

The 58.2 kWh and 71.1 kWh battery sizes in the Chinese L05 are essentially the same as the L03, but the range of the larger battery in RWD drops from 650 km CLTC to 635 km due to the larger size and weight. At this time, the L05 is not being offered with AWD in China, although that might change in export markets. The 183 kW (~245 hp) motor is also the same while the 0-100 km/h time increases from 6.6 s in the RWD L03 to 6.8 s in the larger L05. Both are a little quicker than the European Model Y Standard at 7.2 s. We’ll have to see how the range works out under WLTP.

While the L03 impressed with a larger passenger compartment than the Model Y in a smaller footprint, it did have a somewhat smaller rear cargo area. Of course, because Tesla uses a non-standard measurement for cargo volume, comparing manufacturer numbers is pointless. However, the L05 does have a larger cargo volume than the L03 under standard measurements, which would be even more if measured to the top of the squared-off roof, rather than to the top of the seatbacks. XPENG has shown it holding 9 carryon suitcases with the rear seats up, which should be more than enough for normal people. Overall, the L05 has 41 storage locations throughout the vehicle, including under-seat storage.

In addition, the L05 expands the passenger compartment even more over the Model Y. The rear seats now also have folding rear tray tables and a 17.3” entertainment screen folds from the ceiling. In addition, there are sunshades that deploy to cover the sunroof. Other than the center touchscreen increasing from 15.6” to 17.3” and a few new color options, the interior is essentially the same up front. That includes heated, cooled and massaging seats and an easily visible HUD (European models will likely also get a driver display). Ultra trims include XPENG’s excellent NGP intelligent driving system with VLA 2.0 .

List prices for the L05 range from 144,800 RMB ($21,722 USD at current exchange rates) for the base 560 Plus up to 176,800 RMB ($26,522 USD) for the top 635 Ultra SE trim. An EREV version with 1310 km of combined range comes in at 154,800 RMB ($23,222) up to 166,800 RMB ($25,022 USD). However, XPENG is offering a launch discount of 5000 RMB ($750). For comparison, the L03 EV currently ranges from 123,800 RMB ($18,586 USD) to 156,800 RMB ($23,540 USD) in China.

However, a G6 comes in at the same 176,800 RMB list price as the L05 635 Ultra SE. That premium vehicle has more power and faster charging on an 800V platform with close to the same range. And it isn’t lacking in technology. At 4758 mm long, it only gives up a small amount of space compared to the L05.

title: Toyota's Next Hybrids Will Sip 15% Less Gas, And They Can't Come Soon Enough
raw_summary: Hybrids aren't dead yet, and Toyota's gas-electric models are going to get more fuel efficient High gas prices are one of the big talking points as Americans head to vote in this year's mid-term elections, and while EVs continue to rule the headlines, Toyota is proving that hybrids aren't dead yet. summary: Hybrids aren't dead yet, and Toyota's gas-electric models are going to get more fuel efficient High gas prices are one of the big talking points as Americans head to vote in this year's mid-term elections, and while EVs continue to rule the headlines, Toyota is proving that hybrids aren't dead yet.
article_paragraphs: Hybrids aren't dead yet, and Toyota's gas-electric models are going to get more fuel efficient

High gas prices are one of the big talking points as Americans head to vote in this year's mid-term elections, and while EVs continue to rule the headlines, Toyota is proving that hybrids aren't dead yet. The Japanese automaker has dropped new details about its next generation hybrid vehicles, but the most important is the promise that they'll consume 15% less gas than today's equivalents.

The frugal engine at the heart of this claim is a 1.5L inline-4 that Toyota has been talking about since 2004, but this is the first time we've had any indication of its efficiency. The engine was designed with electrification in mind, and it will work in both straight hybrid and plug-in hybrid setups. Toyota confirmed that a naturally aspirated version will take over the work of today's 1.5L inline-3 and 1.8L inline-4 engines.

Lighter, more compact electric motors will help cut powertrain mass, which is bound to have a small effect on efficiency. But Toyota says most of the fuel savings come from lower mechanical friction, improved thermal management, reduced electrical losses, and lower aerodynamic drag from the car they're bolted to.

The new 1.5, and a punchier 2.0L inline-4 that was also revealed back in 2024, are expected to hit the market in 2027. And it won't only be Toyota customers reaping the benefits. Toyota expects to make $1.7 billion per year selling its next generation hybrid powertrains to other automakers, Auto News reports. The identity of those brands is unconfirmed, but could include Subaru and Mazda, which formed a powertrain alliance in 2024.

Toyota revealed the 1.5L engine's efficiency claim as it detailed its "multi-pathway" platform strategy for future cars. Instead of building its next generation EVs and hybrids on different platforms, as BMW does, Toyota plans to build them on a common platform, something Mercedes and Stellantis already do.

Sharing platforms leads to greater financial and engineering economies of scale, Toyota says, and allows plants to easily flex the powertrain mix to suit changes in customer demand. The traditional downside of sharing is that designers can end up compromising a car with one powertrain type to ensure another type hits all of its marks. But Toyota says neither the hybrid nor battery-electric versions of its next generation cars will be compromised.

The gasoline-electric versions will have the exact same interior space, and even the same silhouette, as their EV brothers. And the lower-profile engine and hybrid packages will allow lower hood heights and "more dynamic vehicle proportions," Toyota says, giving its designers more freedom. A single image shows three identical fastback sedans in silhouetted form, with the EV's battery occupying the full front-to-rear floor, the PHEV's the rear floor, and the hybrid, a small area under the rear seat.

title: Tested: 1991 BMW 318i Has a Case of the Wiggles
raw_summary: There are two reasons you buy a BMW. One, for refined performance. Two, for grand looks and image and that little pro­peller badge on the edge of the hood. We like BMWs that have a lot of One. But the new-for-1991 318i convertible falls short in refinement, and we therefore think its mis­sion is reason number Two. The 318i convertible is mechanically identical to BMW’s 318is two-door sedan. Both use a 134-hp twin-cam four-cylinder and a five-speed manual transmission (no automatic is available). The convertible is heavier by more than 250 pounds. The extra weight comes from additional chassis brac­ing and two very thick beams that run along the doorsills for the length of the passenger compartment.

article_paragraphs: There are two reasons you buy a BMW. One, for refined performance. Two, for grand looks and image and that little pro­peller badge on the edge of the hood. We like BMWs that have a lot of One. But the new-for-1991 318i convertible falls short in refinement, and we therefore think its mis­sion is reason number Two.

The 318i convertible is mechanically identical to BMW’s 318is two-door sedan. Both use a 134-hp twin-cam four-cylinder and a five-speed manual transmission (no automatic is available). The convertible is heavier by more than 250 pounds. The extra weight comes from additional chassis brac­ing and two very thick beams that run along the doorsills for the length of the passenger compartment.

The 318i convertible sells for $29,060, which is nearly $7000 more than the 318is two-door sedan. The soft-top is slower by a second to 60 mph, taking 9.7 seconds. The convertible is also slower in the quarter­-mile by most of a second. Still, the soft-top is not a turtle—it will accelerate about as quickly as a Honda Accord.
See all results for used 1992 BMW 3-series for sale near 97818

The 318’s engine performance and driv­ability are good. The 1.8-liter is enchant­ingly smooth, and it urges you to rev to the redline for every shift. BMW spaced the five gear ratios perfectly for this kind of maximum driving. The flow of power is uninterrupted from a stop to top speed.

Our test car gripped the road as well as the 318is hardtop we tested last September, but there is a big difference in feel between the hardtop and the convertible. Where the hardtop is tight and crisp turning into a cor­ner, the convertible wiggles and twists. Its rear end seems to send waves of jiggles for­ward whenever the pavement turns demanding. This trait pops our BMW refinement bubble—we miss the better ride of the hardtop. And this behavior is surpris­ing, because BMW’s new Wackersdorf assembly plant builds the convertibles as convertibles, not as sedans with their roofs hacked off. That approach usually results in a more rigid chassis.
Wind noise with the top down is accept­ably low, and the standard six-speaker stereo is one of the best. With the unpadded top up, though, normal conversation echoes around inside the car.

Like the 318is, the four-cylinder convertible is intended to be an entry-level BMW. As such, its folding roof is manually operated, and to raise and lower the tight­-fitting top you need to stand outside the car. It’s an easy task to lower the top, and when folded the top lies under a slick hard cover. Raising the top, however, is only gratifying if you bought this convertible for reason number Two. The top fabric is color-matched to the car’s paint and draws a lot of stares.

According to the AP, Iran claims over the last 24 hours, three oil tankers struck mines and caught fire while passing through the strait on an unauthorized route. The report didn't name the ships or include information on the number of people, if any, killed and injured by the mines. So far, the AP says it has been unable to independently verify the report, which originated with Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps. One reason it may be difficult to verify the claims, however, may be that the tankers are out of contact:

Iran's navy said the tankers switched off their radar and navigation systems and ignored warnings as they attempted to exit through a restricted route. It said the damaged vessels were abandoned off the southern coast of the waterway.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center said Thursday that a vessel spotted another vessel on fire while transiting the strait. It said it did not know the status of the crew on the burning vessel or how badly it was damaged. It was not immediately clear whether that vessel was one of the three referenced by the Revolutionary Guard.

Losing three tankers' worth of oil is unfortunate, but not remotely comparable to the likely loss of lives on board. It certainly won't help gas prices, but it won't send them soaring, either. The real problem is that tensions are already high heading into the midterms, fuel is already expensive, and the risk of hitting mines means fewer ships will be willing to risk the trip. We could also see shipping rates climb even higher to account for the risk , which could raise gas prices further.
Aside from claiming its mines blew up three oil tankers, Iran also claims to have captured a U.S. MQM-170 Outlaw drone. The U.S., however, denies Iran's claims. From the AP:

Iranian state television reported Thursday that the Revolutionary Guard, in an "electronic warfare operation," detected and identified the MQM-170 Outlaw drone, and took over of its control systems before landing it in Iranian territory. It did not say when the drone was allegedly seized.
"In the past weeks and months, the IRGC has repeatedly lied out of desperation, and today is no different," said Tim Hawkins, a spokesman for the Central Command. He did not provide more details.

title: I Just Graduated Law School, Time To Upgrade My Toyota To Something Fun! What Should I Buy?
raw_summary: Colby is a recent law school graduate and has been rocking a sturdy but boring 2014 Toyota Venza. He wants a fun car before adult life demands otherwise. He has a $35,000 budget for something with three pedals and good handling. What car should he buy? (Welcome back to What Car Should You Buy? Where we give real people real advice about buying cars.
