article_paragraphs: Colby is a recent law school graduate and has been rocking a sturdy but boring 2014 Toyota Venza. He wants a fun car before adult life demands otherwise. He has a $35,000 budget for something with three pedals and good handling. What car should he buy?
(Welcome back to What Car Should You Buy? Where we give real people real advice about buying cars. Do you want us to help you find a car? Submit your story on our form. )

I'm graduating from law school and I want to get into something fun! I'm currently in a 2014 Toyota Venza and while it's about as practical as it could get, I need something with a personality. I have grown up driving 911s in the Appalachian mountains so I want to car to be something that I can really carve some corners with. I am a Porsche guy at heart so I would love to hop into one of those. I would like a bit of cargo space but it wouldn't be a deal buster with a lack of space. If possible I would like something I could modify a bit but it will be a daily driver as well as a corner carver. A convertible would be fun but again not a dealbreaker if not. I also really want this car to be a manual as well.

Congratulations on the law school degree. That's no easy task, and neither is sourcing a 911 in this market for under $35,000 that isn't a total basket case. There was a time when a decently sorted 996 could be had in the $30k range; those days are long gone.

However, there is a reasonably affordable option that will give you Porsche-like handling and relatively stress-free ownership. The Toyota GR86 and its Subaru BRZ twin were engineered to offer Porsche Cayman/Boxster experiences at less than half the price of what the Germans are asking. While it lacks the horsepower of the Porsche sports cars, if your primary goal is zipping around corners, there are few cars at this price point that can match the Toyobaru twins.

The only real downside is the lack of Toyota depreciation, so used examples in the low $30,000 mark aren't too far off brand new cars, so you may want to consider a budget stretch to get a full warranty. If you insist on adhering to that $35,000 ceiling, here is a 2024 Toyota Certified Premium model with about 30,000 miles.

Congratulations on graduating from Emory, Colby. I mean, I don't know for a fact that you just graduated from Emory, but come on. We both know it's Emory. "ATL metro area"? I highly doubt that's Georgia State. Your football team might not have been as good, but allegedly, there's more to law school than tailgating and football. Emory's a solid choice if you care about those things. Now you just have to pass the bar and buy that new car.

The problem is, I don't know if the car you want to drive in the mountains is the one you want to sit in on your commute. Porsches are pretty comfortable, but I've driven in the Atlanta area for decades, and manuals get old fast. A PDK 911 would work, but the ones in your budget aren't all that nice. So I say split your fun life and your work life. Buy a professional, responsible-appearing commuter like a Toyota Prius or Lexus ES hybrid. Heck, buy this 2014 Lexus GS 350 for $19,000 .

title: Toyota Details the New Hybrid System Bound for the Next-Gen Corolla
raw_summary: An important new Toyota is on the way. The Corolla—Toyota’s fourth bestselling vehicle in the United States last year—is expected to enter its 13th generation for the 2028 model year and will bring with it a new array of powertrains. Toyota previously confirmed that the next Corolla will take a multi-energy approach, and now the company has revealed more details about the hybrid and gas powertrains that will live under the compact car’s hood. While Toyota didn’t explicitly state that these next-generation powertrains would be used in the Corolla, the graphic provided by the automaker shows the silhouette of a vehicle that strongly resembles the Corolla concept car shown at last year’s Tokyo auto show. The graphic shows a traditional hybrid, a plug-in hybrid, and a fully electric powertrain, and the Corolla may follow the Camry and RAV4 by ditching its gas-only option.

raw_title: Not Even The Bentley Torcal Can Avoid The First Edition Treatment
title: Not Even The Bentley Torcal Can Avoid The First Edition Treatment
raw_summary: It's only been a month since the all-electric Bentley Torcal was unveiled, and the British brand has already announced a special First Edition model that will initially top out the range. Loaded with features and the brand's most powerful electric drivetrain, it may be enough to sway some prospective buyers out of a gas-guzzling Bentayga . Bentley has offered a First Edition in the past , but the specialness of the fender badge wears off a little when the same name is used on the Dodge Charger , Ford Bronco , and Lexus IS — just to name a few. Special elements for the Bentley Torcal First Edition include carbon fiber to the front bumper winglets, mirror caps, side sills, and rear diffuser. The most noticeable upgrade is, by far, the distinctive 22-inch wheels with a black and Liquid Silver finish. These wheels show off the self-leveling Bentley badges and give a peak at special Graphene Grey brake calipers.

Just like the Torcal S, the First Edition uses a 113-kWh battery pack, two electric motors, and an 800-volt electrical architecture, providing a combined 875 horsepower and 996 pound-feet (1,350 Nm) of torque with launch control. This grunt is enough to send the SUV to 62 mph (100 kph) in just 2.9 seconds and through to a 162 mph (260 kph) top speed. The First Edition offers support for DC ultra-fast charging at up to 400 kW, meaning the sizeable battery can be charged from 10-80% in less than 20 minutes.

Buyers will be offered two unique color splits by Mulliner , in addition to eight accent colors and the option to add a third interior color. title: Ford Launches A Special Mustang Mach-E, But It's Only For Police
raw_summary: Ford is eager for police forces across the United States to use the all-electric Mustang Mach-E and has launched a Special Service Vehicle (SSV) version as part of its updated 2027 Mach-E range . Some agencies already use their own versions of the Mach-E, and this turnkey model may encourage others to follow suit. The Mustang Mach-E SSV is based on the entry-level Select trim and comes with performance features from higher-spec models. It lacks some of the luxuries of higher-end trim lines, so it should suit enforcement agencies that will make their own upgrades before deploying these EVs. Ford Authority understands the model uses the Mach-E's available extended-range 91-kWh battery pack and dual electric motors. It's unclear if these motors are borrowed from the eAWD versions of the Premium and Select models rated at up to 370 horsepower, or if it has the more spirited 480 hp setup of the Mach-E GT. Since it will ship with GT badges, it'll likely get the more powerful motors.

Alongside the beefed-up powertrain, the Mustang Mach-E SSV will ship with 20-inch aluminum wheels. There will be Brembo front brakes with red-painted calipers, special front and rear fascias, and a gloss black grille shield. Ford will also ship the model with the Co-Pilot360 Active 2.0 system, a drainable frunk, and front parking sensors.

It also includes the Mach-E's Unbridled driving mode, which improves acceleration response, tweaks the steering, and ramps up regenerative braking. Ford has yet to release any photos of the Mustang Mach-E SSV, though it may look similar to the prototype tested by the Michigan State Police in 2021 . Earlier this year, officers in Dearborn, Michigan took delivery of a handful of special Mustang Mach-E GT models with a particular focus on stopping reckless and aggressive drivers in their tracks.

Of course, the Mustang Mach-E is far from the only EV police are using across the United States. Last year, the Palo Alto Police Department received a patrol-ready Rivian R1S . Of all the electric cruisers in operation in the U.S., the Las Vegas police Cybertrucks are perhaps the most striking. Tech entrepreneur Ben Horowitz and his wife donated these heavily modified Cybertrucks to the force, and each is expected to cut the agency's annual fuel costs by $8,800 to $12,000.

A spokesperson for the Anglo-German outfit told media that the championship leader was “feeling under the weather” due to a “viral illness” he has been recovering from, with the FIA therefore excusing him from today’s media activities.

Antonelli is on the brink of a maiden F1 title, which would make him the youngest world champion as he would beat Sebastian Vettel ’s 2010 record by over three years. All he needs on Sunday is ninth place, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win.
The 20-year-old Italian won’t be the only driver to skip media day, with Valtteri Bottas also calling in sick; Cadillac notified media that the Finn was “unwell”.
“The team has taken the decision to allow him a day of rest, to support his recovery,” the statement read.
“This is a precautionary measure and does not currently affect his participation in the remainder of the race weekend. We will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates if necessary.”
Albeit unlikely, there is a chance of a reserve driver being called up for either racer.

At Mercedes, that would be 2023 Formula 2 runner-up Frederik Vesti, who has never competed in a grand prix but is scheduled to make his seventh career Free Practice 1 outing this weekend in George Russell’s car.

article_paragraphs: The duo is accused of running a chop shop in Pennsylvania and reselling at least a dozen stolen cars with altered paperwork

Shopping for a car on Facebook Marketplace has always been a bit sketchy, but some buyers in Pennsylvania encountered something far worse than undisclosed damage or odd odors. In at least 12 cases, buyers ended up purchasing stolen cars that bad been title-washed , which is when a stolen or salvaged vehicle is sold with paperwork that belongs to another vehicle. Now, the alleged sellers — a father and son — are facing several felony charges. Pennsylvania's Attorney General announced that Jermaine Quinones Sr., 42, and Jermaine Quinones Jr., 18, allegedly ran a chop shop operation out of Lehigh County.

Investigators identified sales of 12 vehicles that had washed paperwork during 2025 and 2026 and were reportedly worth a combined value approaching $500,000. Many allegedly changed hands through Facebook Marketplace. The charging documents indicate that the pair used VINs from various vehicles to disguise cars that they knew were stolen. Those counterfeit documents helped the cars in question get through titling and registration without setting off alarms. Put another way, everyday buyers, even those using a VIN history report, could've thought they were buying a legitimate used car.

And these weren't a bunch of old clunkers either. Authorities identified a 2026 Infiniti QX60 valued at $67,599, an Acura Integra worth $35,950, and two Ford Mustangs valued at $32,640 and $31,890. Investigators arrested Quinones Sr. at his Allentown home earlier in October, with cash bail set at $450,000, and then Quinones Jr. was arrested on October 22, with a bail set at $100,000. Both men now face felony charges including theft by deception, washing vehicle titles, and insurance fraud. A single conviction for either individual presents a maximum sentence of 20 years.

Facebook Marketplace might have a bad reputation, but this kind of scam happens all over the used-car industry. This year alone, we've reported on several similar cases of fraud, including another one from Pennsylvania's Attorney General. In that case, a theft ring had targeted 65 luxury and high-end cars and performed a similar title-washing scheme. Another case involved a used-car dealer in U tah that was accused of forging a dead woman's signature on sales documents to resell hail-damaged cars.

The lesson here, for all of us, is to do as much homework as possible when researching used cars — even one that's a 2026 model! Always get a vehicle history report and make sure all the VINs on the car match.

raw_title: Ireland’s Grid Flexibility Assessment Shows Why Location Matters
title: Ireland’s Grid Flexibility Assessment Shows Why Location Matters
raw_summary: Ireland’s electricity regulator has put some useful numbers on the country’s future need for grid flexibility. Its first national assessment identifies about 234 MW and 58 GWh of potential upward flexibility requirements on distribution networks in 2028. Batteries, managed EV charging and industrial demand response could all contribute, but the figures become more interesting at the level of individual substations. The Commission for Regulation of Utilities’ Flexibility Needs Assessment identifies a potential requirement of 0.6 MW and 3 MWh at the Naas 38 kV/10 kV substation in 2028, concentrated in January. Reinforcement is planned by 2030, when the assessment identifies no corresponding flexibility requirement. This describes a modeled network need, without a commitment to purchase a service or install a battery.
summary: Ireland’s electricity regulator has put some useful numbers on the country’s future need for grid flexibility. Its first national assessment identifies about 234 MW and 58 GWh of potential upward flexibility requirements on distribution networks in 2028. Batteries, managed EV charging and industrial demand response could all contribute, but the figures become more interesting at the level of individual substations.
article_paragraphs: Ireland’s electricity regulator has put some useful numbers on the country’s future need for grid flexibility. Its first national assessment identifies about 234 MW and 58 GWh of potential upward flexibility requirements on distribution networks in 2028. Batteries, managed EV charging and industrial demand response could all contribute, but the figures become more interesting at the level of individual substations.

The Commission for Regulation of Utilities’ Flexibility Needs Assessment identifies a potential requirement of 0.6 MW and 3 MWh at the Naas 38 kV/10 kV substation in 2028, concentrated in January. Reinforcement is planned by 2030, when the assessment identifies no corresponding flexibility requirement. This describes a modeled network need, without a commitment to purchase a service or install a battery.

A battery elsewhere in Ireland could provide useful balancing services, help integrate renewable generation and earn revenue in electricity markets while contributing nothing to the particular constraint at Naas. The electrical connection matters. A resource has to change power flows across the affected equipment, in the required direction, during the periods when that equipment is constrained.

The distinction applies equally to demand response. A large fleet of electric vehicles might represent considerable flexible electricity demand nationally, but only vehicles connected in electrically useful locations can relieve a particular transformer. Their charging must also be adjustable without compromising the journeys they need to make. The same questions apply to refrigeration, heating and other industrial or commercial loads.

Timing adds another complication. Naas’s modeled 0.6 MW and 3 MWh figures describe different aspects of the expected requirement. Dividing one by the other does not establish that the network needs a battery discharging continuously for five hours. The duration of individual events, recovery between them and customer operating requirements all affect which resources could help.

There’s an important reality check in Britain. UK Power Networks’ March 2026 network assessment reports that the utility stopped seeking flexibility tenders for certain single-transformer substations whose constraints typically lasted 24 hours. The available flexibility market could not address those requirements effectively on technical and commercial grounds. In those circumstances, reinforcement or another engineering intervention may be more appropriate.

As distribution networks accommodate more electric vehicles, heat pumps, batteries and distributed generation, assessing flexibility at the right electrical location becomes increasingly important. National capacity estimates provide useful context, but investment and procurement decisions need much more specific evidence. The Naas example starts the first article in a series connected to The Flexibility Mesh , an open 99-page strategy report on how physical resources, permissions, operating capabilities and commercial arrangements fit together.

My full TFIE Strategy Briefing analysis examines the Naas case, the alternatives available to utilities and the conditions that turn flexible capacity into a deliverable network service. It also links to the interactive Flexibility Mesh architecture.

raw_title: Ex-Tesla Autopilot head calls vision-only a ‘weird religious stance’
title: Ex-Tesla Autopilot head calls vision-only a ‘weird religious stance’
raw_summary: GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, who ran Tesla’s Autopilot program in 2015 and 2016, says dropping radar for a camera-only self-driving system is “a weird religious stance that ignores physics.” It’s the bluntest rebuke of Tesla’s vision-only bet yet from someone who helped build the original Autopilot. And it lands while Tesla is pushing camera-only Cybercabs into driverless service in Austin.
summary: GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, who ran Tesla’s Autopilot program in 2015 and 2016, says dropping radar for a camera-only self-driving system is “a weird religious stance that ignores physics.” It’s the bluntest rebuke of Tesla’s vision-only bet yet from someone who helped build the original Autopilot.
article_paragraphs: GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, who ran Tesla’s Autopilot program in 2015 and 2016, says dropping radar for a camera-only self-driving system is “a weird religious stance that ignores physics.”

It’s the bluntest rebuke of Tesla’s vision-only bet yet from someone who helped build the original Autopilot. And it lands while Tesla is pushing camera-only Cybercabs into driverless service in Austin.

Anderson made the comments in an interview with The Verge published October 27, after GM’s technology event in New York the week before. Asked whether GM could eventually move to a vision-only approach like Tesla’s, he didn’t leave much room for interpretation.

“If you scale back to vision-only, physics suggests you’ll be in trouble in certain situations,” Anderson said. He added that radar is so cheap that removing it makes no sense, and that “cameras can’t see through dense fog or measure instantaneous velocity like radar can.”
He also said lidar helps camera systems improve faster when the two are trained together. That’s a direct counter to Tesla’s argument that cameras plus fleet data are all you need.

Anderson isn’t a lidar startup CEO talking his book. He led the Model X program at Tesla, then directed Autopilot during its formative years before co-founding self-driving company Aurora. GM hired him as chief product officer in 2025, and Bloomberg reported last year that Mary Barra sees him as a frontrunner to become GM’s next CEO .
His roadmap at GM goes the other way from Tesla’s. The Cadillac Escalade IQ is due to debut GM’s “eyes-off” system in 2028 , with lidar, radar, and cameras.

He took a shot at another Tesla habit in the same interview. Anderson said he avoids “eyes off” marketing language altogether, arguing that a driver-assist system that feels very capable already pushes drivers into complacency. That’s the core problem with selling “Full Self-Driving (Supervised).”

raw_title: Why Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans
title: Why Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans
raw_summary: Last month marked two years since Daniel Ricciardo ’s last motor race to this day, as the eight-time grand prix winner regretfully, discreetly bowed out of Formula 1 – but is his career over? Ricciardo admits it likely is, having come to terms with the way his F1 stint ended – “I’m not 100% there, but I’m 90%,” he said of his quest of closure – but he might still be interested in further opportunities, as long as they don’t require a season-long commitment.
summary: Last month marked two years since Daniel Ricciardo ’s last motor race to this day, as the eight-time grand prix winner regretfully, discreetly bowed out of Formula 1 – but is his career over?
article_paragraphs: Last month marked two years since Daniel Ricciardo ’s last motor race to this day, as the eight-time grand prix winner regretfully, discreetly bowed out of Formula 1 – but is his career over?

Ricciardo admits it likely is, having come to terms with the way his F1 stint ended – “I’m not 100% there, but I’m 90%,” he said of his quest of closure – but he might still be interested in further opportunities, as long as they don’t require a season-long commitment.

“A year ago, I would have said, ‘I will never put a helmet on again, I’m done, that’s it’,” Ricciardo told the Beyond The Grid podcast. “But there is something there where I’m like, it would be nice to finish a racing career a bit more on my terms; to do something that, when I take the helmet off, I’m smiling and happy. Maybe that’s the last bit of closure I need.
“The thought of doing a full championship still doesn’t really sound that exciting. Probably a one-off, like a one-off Le Mans.

“F1 is so selfish – in a necessary way. Yes, you have team-mates, but that’s your first opponent and all that. I think to share a car with other drivers and to actually have real team-mates to share data and help out, I think it would be – especially now, at this point where that insane fire and whatever ruthlessness, that has faded to a degree. I think I’ll just enjoy it. It would be the form of driving and kind of companionship that I would really enjoy, and I think it would make me smile and feel good about the art of competition again.”

Ricciardo explained he never enjoyed driving all that much and mostly revelled in competition, though his last few years in F1 dampened his enthusiasm. Le Mans could be a new way to find fulfillment, but the Australian – who hasn’t been training the way he used to – is cautious about that prospect.

“Do I need to open the box again? I don’t know,” Ricciardo pondered. “That’s why I haven’t rushed into making a decision on anything, because, again, I want to make sure I’m not doing it for ego or for some fairy-tale ending. It has to be because it’s right inside me and I really want to do it, and it’s not to please others.

title: Williams launches 'W50' expo to celebrate F1 milestone
raw_summary: Williams F1 Team will celebrate its 50th anniversary with a two-week fan experience in London, offering fans a look at its five decades of Formula 1 history. W50 Live will be open at Leake Street across February 11 - 28, 2027, bringing together iconic cars, historic memorabilia and installations that will tell the story of one of the sport’s most successful teams.

article_paragraphs: Williams F1 Team will celebrate its 50th anniversary with a two-week fan experience in London, offering fans a look at its five decades of Formula 1 history.

W50 Live will be open at Leake Street across February 11 - 28, 2027, bringing together iconic cars, historic memorabilia and installations that will tell the story of one of the sport’s most successful teams.

Visitors will have the opportunity to see several of Williams’ most significant cars, including the FW06, the first car produced by Williams Grand Prix Engineering, and the FW11B, which Nelson Piquet drove to the 1987 drivers’ championship.

Other highlights include the FW14B, which helped Nigel Mansell secure the 1992 world title, the FW19 from Jacques Villeneuve’s championship-winning 1997 campaign, the FW25 driven by Juan Pablo Montoya in 2003, and the FW38, associated with Valtteri Bottas’ record speed of 378kph.

The event will also look towards the future, with a show car representing Williams’ 2027 challenger, the FW50. The name marks the team’s half-century milestone and follows a similar approach to its 40th anniversary, when it moved from the FW38 designation to the FW40.

Williams’ 50th anniversary celebrations will reflect a remarkable record in F1, including nine constructors’ championship titles, seven drivers’ championship titles and 114 grand prix victories. The team will become only the third in the sport, after Ferrari and McLaren, to reach 50 consecutive years of competition.

The choice of Leake Street also carries historical significance. The venue’s railway arches reflect the setting where team founder Frank Williams discovered co-founder Patrick Head working in a garage, bringing the anniversary celebration back to London’s industrial roots.
Marcus Prosser, marketing director of Williams F1 Team, said the event would provide a new way to connect with supporters.

raw_summary: The Crown Signia, which is being refreshed for 2027 , is already one of Toyota's most striking models. Now, the automaker has used it as the basis for a special one-off concept premiering at next week's SEMA Show in Las Vegas to go with its wild Snowhunter truck and SUV concepts . With dramatic bodywork and several chassis modifications, it makes a bold statement, though it doesn't back that up with any powertrain modifications. Toyota says the idea behind the Crown Signia GT-S Concept was to create a family vehicle that's just as well-versed at transporting kids to school as it is at cruising along a canyon road. One of the most important upgrades is a set of MCS coilovers that drop the ride height by 5 inches while improving handling. With the lowered ride height, this Crown now looks like a proper performance car rather than a bloated crossover. Toyota Motorsports Garage, which handled this special project, did more than upgrade the Crown's suspension. A custom body kit has been designed for the SEMA show car with flared front and rear fenders and a large front lip. The grille has been blacked out, and red accents have been added around the headlights.

Toyota Motorsports Garage, which handled this special project, did more than upgrade the Crown's suspension. A custom body kit has been designed for the SEMA show car with flared front and rear fenders and a large front lip. The grille has been blacked out, and red accents have been added around the headlights.

The crew behind the project may have taken inspiration from cars like the Porsche 911 GT3 RS, adding louvers on the front fenders. Though whether they serve any aerodynamic or brake-cooling effect in this application remains to be seen. Among the other upgrades are extended rocker panels and a new rear end with a bold diffuser and tailpipes.

A distinctive shade of dark gray metallic has been applied to the Crown with more clear coats than usual to give it a particularly glossy finish. The brakes from a Lexus RX 500h F Sport have been adapted for use here, and are positioned behind 21-inch HRE wheels. Rounding out the upgrades are minor interior tweaks, including new seats appointed in black leather with GT-S branding. The electronic shifter also has a bright red GT-S logo.

Toyota's standard Crown Signia — which has seen other wild customizations — is sold in the U.S. with a hybrid 2.5-liter inline-4 and an electronically-controlled CVT. With 238 horsepower, it offers solid performance, although it's certainly not a raging machine like, say, the GR Corolla. Had Toyota really wanted to transform the Crown into a particularly crazy creation for SEMA, perhaps swapping out the hybrid setup for its turbocharged 1.6-liter GR three-cylinder would have been a wise idea.

Hold on to your hats…

If Georgia seems an unlikely spot for an EV ecosystem to arise, guess again. Despite his red-state status, Georgia Governor Brian Kemp has embraced the vehicle electrification movement as a critical economic development strategy for his state.

“Georgia leads the nation in EV battery and vehicle manufacturing investments, totaling over $31 billion and creating over 38,000 jobs since 2015 — outpacing even Michigan by over $10 billion in investments over the same decade,” noted the Georgia Network for Electric Mobility at the University of Georgia in a report last year.

Georgia’s electrification ambitions earned a fresh wave of publicity during the last months of the Biden administration, when Rivian nailed down plans to build a new factory in the state with a $6.57 conditional loan guarantee in its pocket from the Loan Programs Office of the US Department of Energy.

After Trump took office he promptly shut down the LPO, allowing all but a scarce few decarbonization projects to move ahead ( here’s one example). Somehow the Rivian factory loan also survived the Trump chopper, though at the lesser amount of $4.5 billion, and a groundbreaking ceremony took place last year.

If all goes according to plan, Rivian will soon join electric bus maker Bluebird on Georgia’s roster of EV makers. Another potential opportunity surfaced last Saturday, when Audi CEO Gernot Döllner took to the campaign trail with US President Donald Trump.

That was not a typo. Last Saturday, Döllner appeared on stage at a campaign rally in Georgia with US President Donald Trump, during which the two of them announced the culmination of a years-long plan to build Audi’s first ever factory in the US, a $4 billion facility to be constructed in Peach County, Georgia.

The new factory announcement was somewhat premature, to put it kindly. The supervisory board of parent company Volkswagen has yet to sign off on the deal, and the news blew up in Audi’s hometown, Germany, where Volkswagen is laying off workers.

I used to drive my Camaro 50 miles through Michigan winters to go snowboarding. With a good set of skinny snow tires, it drove just fine. Fit myself, a passenger, 2 boards, and our snow gear in the car without a problem. In a parking lot full of small SUV's and Subaru's, the Camaro really stood out.
One morning, it was in the upper 60's, so I figured it would be fine to ride my motorcycle to class. I was wearing an unlined leather jacket and leather gloves with my helmet.
I got to school and everything was fine. I got out of my first class, and it had started raining. Getting cooler, too.
I got out of my second class, and it's snowing. The temp has REALLY dropped, too. Greaaaaat.
When I got out of my third and final class, I went to my bike, and there was 2" snow on the seat. I cleared it off as best I could, fired it up, and rode out of the slushy parking lot.
As soon as I pulled onto the road outside my community college, bike died. Outta gas.

title: The Ford Escape may return as an EV based on the UEV platform [Update]
raw_summary: Ford pulled the plug on the Escape last year after a 25-year run, but the crossover SUV could return as an EV on the new UEV platform. While Ford is preparing to launch the Fathom, its first vehicle based on the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform in 2027, the company is already hinting at what could be its second UEV-based model.

article_paragraphs: Ford pulled the plug on the Escape last year after a 25-year run, but the crossover SUV could return as an EV on the new UEV platform.

While Ford is preparing to launch the Fathom, its first vehicle based on the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform in 2027, the company is already hinting at what could be its second UEV-based model.
The last gas-powered Escape models rolled off the production line at Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant as it retooled the facility to prepare for the new Fathom electric pickup.
Typically, when Ford retires a model, its landing page says something like “we’re discontinuing” it, or “it’s the end of the road,” such as with the Edge SUV.

Meanwhile, the Escape landing page says the “SUV may be taking a breather for now,” declaring the “Ford Escape is tapping the brakes,” with no mention of it being discontinued. Instead, the site directs you to check out Ford’s other vehicles while it’s on hiatus.
According to Ford Authority , the Escape will return as an all-electric crossover SUV based on the UEV platform.

Update 10/29/2026: A Ford spokesperson told Electrek that the Ford Authority report is pure speculation and the company has not announced the Escape will return as an EV or that it will be based on the UEV platform.

If it does come to life, the Ford Escape EV would likely remain close in size to the outgoing gas model, which measures 180.1″ long, 74.1″ wide (without mirrors), and 66.1″ tall, with a 106.7″ wheelbase. That’s about the size of other compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 and Hyundai Tucson.

In this morning's edition, Porsche is stumbling and bringing Volkswagen down with it, Hyundai's slump is getting worse, and Toyota just saw its third-straight month of sales and production slides. Despite it all, though, Carvana is having the time of its life.

It feels like every single day there's a new bit of doom and gloom coming from the Volkswagen Automotive Group . Well, today is no different, as the German automaker sank deeper into the red in the third quarter — posting its worst results in over a decade while it battles ever-growing challenges in key markets and pushes ahead with a massive restructuring effort . Europe's largest automaker just posted a $6.6 billion operating loss for the past three months, hit by about $8.9 billion in one-off items, most of which are linked to a writedown of its now-less-valuable Porsche stake .

The loss was Volkswagen's largest quarterly deficit since Q4 of 2015, when it was in the throes of Dieselgate, and a spokesperson for the automaker said these latest results make it clear that there's no time to lose. From Reuters :

The results ​highlight the pressure on Volkswagen to overhaul its business model as it faces fierce competition in China, billions of ‌euros ⁠in annual tariff costs and heavy investment demands from the transition to electric vehicles in Europe, where Chinese rivals continue to gain ground.

CEO Oliver ​Blume plans to cut ⁠100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands. Up to four plants in Germany face closure under the plan, which has ​drawn fierce opposition from unions and could trigger strikes from early next year.
Antlitz said ​Volkswagen's operating ⁠return on sales margin was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off items.
Volkswagen is targeting an operating profit margin ⁠of ​8%-10% by 2030 under its restructuring programme.

Recovering materials from end-of-life batteries is a key means to secure much needed critical minerals (CRMs) resiliently and sustainably. With increased recycling, Europe can reduce imports of CRMs, in turn reducing external dependencies. However, Europe’s battery recycling industry is struggling to scale, with over half of Europe’s battery recycling capacity currently at risk . The Circular Economy Act must introduce measures to help scale Europe’s battery recycling capacity.

European battery recyclers lack the needed feedstock. Europe currently preprocesses most battery waste domestically but exports the majority of black mass — CRM rich concentrate from shredded lithium-ion batteries — for final refining abroad. Analysis shows at least 60% of Europe’s black mass is leaving the EU, with this likely only the tip of the iceberg, and lots more black mass leaving the EU, hidden in different customs codes, and unable to be traced. This structural leakage undermines EU strategic autonomy, shifts high-value jobs abroad, weakens circularity and environmental protection.

title: What Europe Can Learn From China If It Wants To Save Its Industry
raw_summary: Something I learned from my trip to China: you can be fast followers if you’re willing to learn from the best. Walking down the silent streets of Beijing I listened to the future of mobility. Statistics can’t convey the silence of the streets. article_paragraphs: Something I learned from my trip to China: you can be fast followers if you’re willing to learn from the best.

Walking down the silent streets of Beijing I listened to the future of mobility. Statistics can’t convey the silence of the streets. When an old — usually German or Japanese combustion engine drove by, I heard and smelled China’s smoggy past.
As I checked my phone, together with your ID — your most precious possession in China — I learned France and Germany had agreed a deal to remake Europe’s auto industry.

Brussels-bubble-me might have thought this deal — and the slightly worse European Parliament copy of the deal a week later — was more or less what was to be expected. Seen through a rosy lens the deal maintains a degree of pressure on carmakers to electrify whilst introducing elements of ‘technological neutrality’ the political right so desired.

Perhaps lowering the pressure on carmakers while using local content rules to bar Chinese carmakers like BYD from the company car market could be a clever ploy? It might just buy European industry some time.

But seen from China the car deal is simply terrible and displays exactly the lack of leadership and consistency that Chinese policymakers so deride in western politicians. One of my interlocutors said, “you have politicians, we have statesmen”. I pushed back, spoke up for Europe, but painful as it may be, these days, those words have a ring of truth to them.

In China two-thirds of all new cars are electric. Its car factories churn out the most amazing vehicles. Software defined, developed in record time, with outstanding infotainment and AI features, and electric of course.

Trucks aren’t going electric in some distant future as truck manufacturer bosses in Europe like to say. 40% of sales in China are electric already, with battery swapping not just some utopia but a market reality with trucks queuing at stations waiting for a six minute swap.

raw_summary: BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months. article_paragraphs: BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months.
But the rest of the filing is messier. BYD’s inventory is up 60% since January, its cash pile has shrunk by almost half, and profit is still down for the first nine months of the year.
BYD is still operating at a high level, but its business is changing.
BYD filed its third-quarter report with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday. Here are the key figures for July through September:
That’s BYD’s best quarterly profit since the end of 2024, and the first time revenue has grown year-over-year after four straight quarters of declines.
It’s also a big rebound from the start of the year. BYD’s Q1 2026 profit collapsed 55% to ¥4.08 billion, before recovering to ¥8.24 billion in Q2.
Still, it came in under expectations. Brokerages polled by Reuters were looking for ¥11.4 billion to ¥12.95 billion.

And zoom out to the full year so far, and BYD is treading water. Revenue for the first nine months was ¥566.30 billion, up just 0.01%, while net profit fell 4.2% to ¥22.34 billion. That’s on top of 2025, when BYD’s annual profit had already dropped to ¥32.62 billion from ¥40.25 billion in 2024.

raw_title: Mazda Comes To Its Senses, Cancels Misfit CX-70, Replacing It With Two-Or-Three-Row CX-90s For 2027
title: Mazda Comes To Its Senses, Cancels Misfit CX-70, Replacing It With Two-Or-Three-Row CX-90s For 2027
raw_summary: The automotive industry raised a collective eyebrow a few years back when Mazda announced that it would sell a two-row version of its excellent three-row CX-90 , but as a new model under the new name of CX-70 , and for good reason. When we first saw the CX-70 in early 2024 , we called it out as "literally just a CX-90 with only two rows of seats and a different name," because that's what it was, despite Mazda insisting it was a new model. Now, after just two model years, it seems that Mazda has finally come to its senses, as it announced October 27 that it's canceling the CX-70, and replacing it with a two-row CX-90 that will sell alongside the three-row CX-90 for 2027. We're sure all five members of the CX-70 fan club are devastated by this decision, but we're also sure they'll get over it. The 2027 Mazda CX-90 two-row drops the CX-70's plug-in hybrid option , so it will only be offered with the turbocharged 3.3-liter inline six-cylinder engine and in 280-horsepower Turbo Premium Sport trim or 340-horsepower Turbo S Premium Sport trim level. The CX-90 three-row continues to be offered with both of those engines as well as a plug-in hybrid power train, and a wider array of trim levels. The cheapest 2027 CX-90 three-row is the 3.3 Turbo Select trim, which starts at $41,345, and the cheapest 2027 CX-90 two-row is 3.3 Turbo Premium Sport trim which starts at $1,200 less than its three-row equivalent at $48,525. (All prices include $1,645 destination.)

We're sure all five members of the CX-70 fan club are devastated by this decision, but we're also sure they'll get over it.

The 2027 Mazda CX-90 two-row drops the CX-70's plug-in hybrid option , so it will only be offered with the turbocharged 3.3-liter inline six-cylinder engine and in 280-horsepower Turbo Premium Sport trim or 340-horsepower Turbo S Premium Sport trim level. (All prices include $1,645 destination.)

Beyond the paradigm-shifting departure of the CX-70 model (yes, that's sarcasm), the Mazda CX-90 doesn't change much for 2027. Mazda gave it new rear suspension bushings and a revised suspension crossmember for improved passenger comfort over rough pavement, and there are four new paint colors available, including two colors that are exclusive to the two-row CX-90. All CX-90s are now offered in Navy Blue Mica and Aero Grey Metallic, but only two-row CX-90s can be had in Melting Copper Metallic and Zircon Sand Metallic. Also, the electric motor in plug-in hybrid CX-90s now gets external insulation material for quieter low-speed operation.

Whether in two-or-three-row form, the CX-90 continues to offer a compelling value proposition. The base $41,345 Turbo Select trim has an array of luxurious features offered as standard, including a 7-inch digital driver's display, an eight-way power driver's seat with lumbar, an eight-speaker audio system, keyless entry, three-zone automatic climate control, and a power liftgate.

The name Mazda CX-70 may get erased for 2027, but the CX-90 soldiers forth. It continues to offer three-row SUV buyers — and now midsize two-row SUV buyers, too — a stylish, agile, and affordable option that when properly equipped can hold its own against dedicated luxury brands.

title: What's The Most Haunted Car You've Ever Bought?
raw_summary: It's that time of year once again . The air has a chill. The leaves are changing color. The kids in the neighborhood might be scared of the old, decrepit Victorian house on your street. You, on the other hand, might be more spooked by the machine sitting inside your garage. The car that seemed perfectly fine when you bought it, but now has a life of its own. What's the most haunted car you've ever bought? Do you hear a rattle when coming to a stop at an intersection? When that happens, it's usually a brake or suspension issue. It can be worn-out pads or loose bolts letting the caliper rattle. Did your mechanic say everything's fine after inspecting your brakes? Then, you might start to consider consulting a priest because you could need to perform an exorcism. Your neighbor will start looking at you funny, but it's not their steering rack that's possessed. Just splash some holy water on a tie rod or two, and you'll be fine.

More likely than not, a demonic spirit isn't causing your car to fall apart. Rule out other potential threats first, like snakes. Back in 2023, a Ford Focus owner took their car to a local dealer in South Carolina for routine maintenance. When the mechanic opened the hood, they were shocked to discover an eight-foot-long boa constrictor in the engine bay . Confident the situation was well outside his wheelhouse, the mechanic called a snake wrangler to remove the unwanted passenger. The subject matter expert believed that the snake was an escaped pet that took refuge in the warm compartment.

title: Cadillac 'honoured' to have Perez as special 300th race celebration planned for Mexico GP
raw_summary: General Motors president Mark Reuss has praised Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez ahead of his 300th race in the series, insisting it is "an honour" to have the Mexican on side. Perez will become just the seventh driver in F1 history to reach the milestone - joining Rubens Barrichello , Fernando Alonso , Jenson Button , Lewis Hamilton , Kimi Raikkonen and Michael Schumacher - and will celebrate the achievement in front of his adoring home support at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City.
summary: General Motors president Mark Reuss has praised Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez ahead of his 300th race in the series, insisting it is "an honour" to have the Mexican on side.
article_paragraphs: General Motors president Mark Reuss has praised Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Perez ahead of his 300th race in the series, insisting it is "an honour" to have the Mexican on side.

Perez will become just the seventh driver in F1 history to reach the milestone - joining Rubens Barrichello , Fernando Alonso , Jenson Button , Lewis Hamilton , Kimi Raikkonen and Michael Schumacher - and will celebrate the achievement in front of his adoring home support at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City.

As part of the occasion, Perez has taken to the streets for a demonstration run along the Paseo de la Reforma. He will also visit General Motors staff in the city before taking to the track in the MAC-26. Cadillac has also announced a renewed contract with the Mexican through to 2029.
Asked about the celebrations when speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange New York, Reuss said: "It's a big deal.

"It'll be Checo's 300th, really proud to have him driving for our team, and he's given us so much feedback, and expertise on someone who's run the tracks - and [Valtteri] Bottas - both giving us real feedback around the car, the track, and what the differences are and how to build the models, and how to get those simulations right as we move through and experience our first season.

"This is a big deal for him. It's also a big deal for General Motors. Our Mexico headquarters is in Mexico City, so he's going to speak to our dealers, he's going to speak to our employees, and I can't wait to go and be part of that with him, and all of his fans.

"He's just a great person, who he is as a person; because he's not only a wonderful driver, a wonderful representative for Cadillac and General Motors and Formula 1, but he's just a really good person.
Perez and Bottas joined Cadillac for its maiden F1 season this term, bringing race-winning experience to the GM brand as it made its first steps into the pinnacle of single-seater racing.

title: 47 Years In The Factory Crate: A 1979 Honda CR125R Elsinore
raw_summary: This is a 1979 Honda CR125R Elsinore, it’s been sitting unused in its original factory crate since 1979, and it’s now possibly the only unridden example of its kind left in the world. Honda’s Elsinore series of motorcycles from the 1970s (and very early 80s) are now legendary in the vintage motocross community, they were named after the Southern Californian Elsinore Grand Prix, and they became a force to be reckoned with in their time.
summary: This is a 1979 Honda CR125R Elsinore, it’s been sitting unused in its original factory crate since 1979, and it’s now possibly the only unridden example of its kind left in the world. Honda’s Elsinore series of motorcycles from the 1970s (and very early 80s) are now legendary in the vintage motocross community, they were named after the Southern Californian Elsinore Grand Prix, and they became a force to be reckoned with in their time.
article_paragraphs: This is a 1979 Honda CR125R Elsinore, it’s been sitting unused in its original factory crate since 1979, and it’s now possibly the only unridden example of its kind left in the world.

Honda’s Elsinore series of motorcycles from the 1970s (and very early 80s) are now legendary in the vintage motocross community, they were named after the Southern Californian Elsinore Grand Prix, and they became a force to be reckoned with in their time.

Honda sold its 125cc motocrosser under the Elsinore name for a total of eight model years, from the air-cooled 1974 CR125M to the liquid-cooled 1981 CR125R. The first one came from a company whose founder, Soichiro Honda, had famously said in the late 1960s that Honda would never build a two-stroke motorcycle.

Honda signed rider Marty Smith, who was then just 17 and still in high school, for the inaugural AMA 125cc National Championship in 1974 and gave him the RC125, the factory version of the CR125M. Smith won the first two rounds and finished second in the other two to take the title, with Honda riders filling the top four places. Images courtesy of Honda.

A group of younger Honda engineers was building a two-stroke anyway, as a secret project without the knowledge or approval of Honda management. Their 250cc prototype first raced, in disguise, in August of 1971, and a 125 followed it onto Japanese motocross tracks in July of 1972. Honda ran the smaller 125 model in the All-Japan Motocross Championship while it finished development, then announced the production CR125M at the start of 1973.

The name came from the Elsinore Grand Prix, an early-summer cross-country race in California that had appeared in the 1971 film On Any Sunday . In the United States the 125 arrived a few months after the CR250M, with a 1974 model-year designation, and an MSRP of $749 USD. In May of 1973 Honda added the MT125 Elsinore in Japan, a dual-purpose model which was based on the CR125M, but with lights and other road equipment to ensure it would be street legal.

The engine was a 123cc piston-port single with a 56 mm bore and 50 mm stroke, a 28 mm Keihin carburetor, a capacitor-discharge ignition (CDI) and a 6-speed gearbox. Honda claimed at least 21.7 bhp at 9,500 rpm and 12.3 lb ft at 9,250 rpm – not a bad horsepower number for a 125.

The bike was fitted with a 21 inch front and 18 inch rear wheel on a 53.5-inch (1,360 mm) wheelbase, with 31 mm fork tubes, conventionally mounted twin rear shocks and drum brakes front and back. Its quoted weight of 179 lbs (81 kgs) was close to the FIM’s 176 lb minimum.

There is no more iconoclastic American fighter plane from the Second World War than the P-51 Mustang. What makes that all the more surprising is that the plane was originally commissioned by the British for use by the Royal Air Force. The Brits also gave the P-51 its noble nickname, the Mustang, because the fighter had the same sense of speed and agility as the wild American equine.

Two decades after the P-51 first plied the skies, Ford adopted the Mustang name for its new sporty car model, creating the "pony car" category in the process. While the Mustang used a galloping horse motif for its badging and mascot, Ford execs said the goal was for the car to embody the spirit and nature of the P-51 fighter.

We looked at a Mustang on Wednesday, a 2012 GT with a Coyote V8 and handling mods by Jack Roush Performance . At first glance, that 'Stang had lots going for it. A little digging, however, turned up a recent unsuccessful Bring a Trailer auction that noted some dings (albeit repaired) on the car's Carfax report. Based on that added info, the Roush-massaged GT's $23,950 asking price lost its shine. When all was said and done, that sent the 'Stang packing with a 78% 'No Dice' loss.

While not direct competitors, the Mustang has long played a similar halo-car role for Ford as the Corvette has for crosstown rival Chevrolet. Of course, the Corvette had a decade's head start on the Mustang and has always been more focused in its role than the broader-appealing Ford. Over the years, both cars have forged rivalries on the race track, often going fender to fender in search of that elusive checkered flag.

The 2007 Chevy Corvette Z06 that comes our way today is a street car homologated for racing, lightened throughout, and fitted with the biggest, most powerful engine Chevy could cram into it at the time.

This model doesn't just pay lip service to the goal of eking out the best power-to-weight ratio from the C6 platform; it goes all in. Those efforts included replacing the Corvette's steel chassis with an aluminum one, ditching the standard floorboards for balsa wood/carbon fiber composites, and adding a magnesium front subframe. To stiffen things up and drop a couple more pounds, the Z06's roof is fixed in place and not removable. Even with its wider, wilder bodywork and massive 7.0-liter engine, the Z06 is still almost 70 pounds lighter.

When new, the Z06's 7.0-liter V8, dubbed LS7 by General Motors' product coders, was the highest-output naturally aspirated engine in the company's lineup. It was also GM's largest-displacement small block ever. In the Z06, the hand-built mill reportedly produced 505 horsepower and 470 pound-feet of torque. This 63,600-mile Z06, in Velocity Yellow with a black leather interior, has a dyno run record in that ballpark.

title: New Trek e-bike is first to get Bosch’s new motor with a major power upgrade
raw_summary: Trek is getting a head start on the competition with the latest version of its Marlin+ electric mountain bike, becoming the first North American bicycle manufacturer to feature Bosch’s newly upgraded Active Line Plus motor. The updated drive system brings more power, less weight, and a smaller footprint to Trek’s approachable electric mountain bike platform, helping make the Marlin+ 6 Gen 2 an even more compelling option for riders who want a capable e-bike without necessarily stepping up to a full-blown, high-performance electric mountain bike.
summary: Trek is getting a head start on the competition with the latest version of its Marlin+ electric mountain bike, becoming the first North American bicycle manufacturer to feature Bosch’s newly upgraded Active Line Plus motor.
article_paragraphs: Trek is getting a head start on the competition with the latest version of its Marlin+ electric mountain bike, becoming the first North American bicycle manufacturer to feature Bosch’s newly upgraded Active Line Plus motor.

The updated drive system brings more power, less weight, and a smaller footprint to Trek’s approachable electric mountain bike platform, helping make the Marlin+ 6 Gen 2 an even more compelling option for riders who want a capable e-bike without necessarily stepping up to a full-blown, high-performance electric mountain bike.

The Trek Marlin+ has traditionally occupied an interesting Goldilocks position in the company’s electric mountain bike lineup. It’s designed to offer the versatility of a trail-capable eMTB while remaining practical enough for everyday recreational riding, commuting, and exploring gravel paths.
In other words, it’s the kind of electric mountain bike that doesn’t require you to be an actual mountain biker to enjoy it.
And the new Bosch motor seems particularly well suited to that mission.
The biggest upgrade comes courtesy of Bosch’s new-generation Active Line Plus motor, which now offers up to 600 watts of power and 60 Nm of torque.
That’s paired with up to 340% pedal assistance, giving riders a substantial boost when accelerating or tackling climbs.

Despite the improved performance, Bosch has actually managed to shrink the motor. A redesigned two-stage gearbox reduces its volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) from the previous generation.

title: Toyota's Next Electric SUV Is Hiding Under This Sliced And Diced Corolla Cross
raw_summary: The heavily modified "Franken-mule" reveals that Toyota is secretly testing a new, smaller electric platform beneath recycled sheet metal. Yesterday Toyota revealed its next generation vehicle architecture that works with EVs and hybrids. And today it looks like we might have got our first peek at it. We've got some spy shots of what at first glance looks like a prototype for an updated Corolla Cross . But all is not as it appears.
summary: The heavily modified "Franken-mule" reveals that Toyota is secretly testing a new, smaller electric platform beneath recycled sheet metal. Yesterday Toyota revealed its next generation vehicle architecture that works with EVs and hybrids. And today it looks like we might have got our first peek at it.
article_paragraphs: The heavily modified "Franken-mule" reveals that Toyota is secretly testing a new, smaller electric platform beneath recycled sheet metal.

Yesterday Toyota revealed its next generation vehicle architecture that works with EVs and hybrids. And today it looks like we might have got our first peek at it. We've got some spy shots of what at first glance looks like a prototype for an updated Corolla Cross . But all is not as it appears.

The headlights are wrong, for a start, but that's far from the only suspicious detail. Because the wheelbase is also off. It's much shorter than the real Corolla Cross's 103.9 in (2,640 mm) wheelbase. And then there's the lack of exhaust tailpipes, and the frame visible under the floorpan.

So is Toyota making an EV version of the Corolla Cross? Not out of the current SUV, which went on sale in North America in late 2021, and was facelifted for MY26 . The car we're looking at is a what automaker's call a mule, a prototype made by butchering an existing model, because it's too early in the development process for real prototypes to be ready for the road.

Our hunch says this camouflaged SUV is testing the new "multi pathway" platform Toyota confirmed earlier this week. Almost all of today's unibody passenger cars and SUVs, including the real Corolla Cross, ride on some form of the automaker's TNGA platform. But the e-TNGA variant for models like the electric bZ is substantially different from the straight TNGA one used in combustion and hybrid cars like the Corolla sedan, and its Cross SUV brother. The new platform will change that.

Instead of developing different cars and platforms for each powertrain type, Toyota wants one set of hardware to handle everything, opening the door to the first ever Corolla EV . The shift will streamline Toyota's development and production process, making it easier for plants to flex the production volumes for different powertrains when customer demand shifts from one to another.

Toyota says no one powertrain will be compromised for the sake of another, and that hybrid and plug-in hybrid models will drink 15 percent less fuel. They'll use a new 1.5L inline-3 engine that replaces both the 1.5L three and 1.8L inline-4 engines Toyota currently relies. The new engines and platform hit the road next year, but we can expect plenty more spy shot sightings before they do.

title: Crunch time for MotoGP as Qatar talks ramp up
raw_summary: Fresh doubts have been expressed by figures in the MotoGP paddock about whether next weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix can go ahead - as a looming re-escalation of the war between the USA and Iran continues to prompt meetings between the championship’s 22 riders and the series organisers regarding safety assurances. The MotoGP weekend is set to get underway at Lusail next Thursday, two days after the US midterm elections - but this week has seen a series of warnings issued by governments and media that US president Donald Trump will seek to resume hostilities with Iran as soon as voting is complete.
summary: Fresh doubts have been expressed by figures in the MotoGP paddock about whether next weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix can go ahead - as a looming re-escalation of the war between the USA and Iran continues to prompt meetings between the championship’s 22 riders and the series organisers regarding safety assurances.
article_paragraphs: Fresh doubts have been expressed by figures in the MotoGP paddock about whether next weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix can go ahead - as a looming re-escalation of the war between the USA and Iran continues to prompt meetings between the championship’s 22 riders and the series organisers regarding safety assurances.

The MotoGP weekend is set to get underway at Lusail next Thursday, two days after the US midterm elections - but this week has seen a series of warnings issued by governments and media that US president Donald Trump will seek to resume hostilities with Iran as soon as voting is complete.

Qatar, which hosts the largest US air force base in the region only a few miles from the Lusail circuit, was struck by missile and drone attacks in March when asked the US first attacked Iran. And Houthi forces have launched strikes from Yemen increasingly close to Qatar in recent weeks, amid continued conflict with the neighbouring Saudi Arabia.

The threat of imminent escalation first prompted the MotoGP grid to assemble last week in Australia for a rare all-hands meeting, before follow-ups in Sepang, first with their team bosses and then with MotoGP CEO Carmelo Ezpeleta.

“We cannot go deeply into details,” explained VR46 Ducati racer Fabio Di Giannantonio when by The Race, “but let's say that the goal is to work with MotoGP to try to have the best safety, the best guarantees, insurances, for sure for all the members of the paddock, to do our job in a better way.

“I think it's fair to try to help MotoGP and Dorna to improve our sport - not only on track, also outside and also in these kinds of things. So it's not at all a fight, let's say, what we are doing is completely a cooperation to try to improve everybody's conditions to try to race there.”

However, any sort of guarantee of the 2,000-strong paddock’s safety is likely to be beyond the reach of the championship’s organisers right now, should a regional escalation cause airports in Qatar and its neighbours Saudi Arabia and the UAE to be shut down, potentially leaving the paddock trapped in an active warzone until such time as things once again cool down.

That’s backed up by increasingly severe government warnings in recent days, with a number of countries escalating their risk level for Qatar and warning that citizens should only travel there for essential reasons - as well as have a concrete escape plan for evacuation.

title: Superpower' neutered - Piastri's fresh F1 struggles explained
raw_summary: Oscar Piastri is experiencing new difficulties with the 2026 McLaren compared to team-mate Lando Norris, including a weekend that neutered what team boss Andrea Stella calls his ‘superpower’. In qualifying, Norris has had the upper hand as he leads Piastri 16-8, but the actual average gap between them has only been 0.040s.
summary: Oscar Piastri is experiencing new difficulties with the 2026 McLaren compared to team-mate Lando Norris, including a weekend that neutered what team boss Andrea Stella calls his ‘superpower’. In qualifying, Norris has had the upper hand as he leads Piastri 16-8, but the actual average gap between them has only been 0.040s.
article_paragraphs: Oscar Piastri is experiencing new difficulties with the 2026 McLaren compared to team-mate Lando Norris, including a weekend that neutered what team boss Andrea Stella calls his ‘superpower’.
In qualifying, Norris has had the upper hand as he leads Piastri 16-8, but the actual average gap between them has only been 0.040s.

The more stark gap has been in a good number of grands prix, including Austin. Piastri (green line) is on average half a second slower than Norris (orange line), through the race on the same strategy, and ends up 22 seconds behind. This follows other weekends with big deficits like Barcelona (35 seconds) and Zandvoort (32 seconds), where he admitted there were “too many [races] now that have been really a long way off”.
Asked what the issue with his race pace was, Piastri replied: "It was slow. I don't have any more than that at the moment.

“When [Isack] Hadjar came out of the pits, it looked like he had some kind of issue and his deployment was a bit all over the place. So I was kind of catching him in awkward places and lost a fair bit of time there.
“Then I was kind of defending from George [Russell] for the rest of the race from that. But I think on top of that the pace just clearly wasn't very good. So plenty to try and understand.”

It was a weekend-long struggle for Piastri, as while on paper he outqualified Norris - and Piastri does deserve some credit for setting a faster legal lap - he was actually 0.424s behind Norris’s fastest (track limits-deleted) Q3 lap.

Piastri’s pace deficit was so clear by Saturday that McLaren had factored in the potential need to swap the cars' order in their pre-race meetings, because - as per team boss Stella - "we had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar”.

article_paragraphs: Joan Mir has revealed that vision problems and associated chronic fatigue were behind his absence from MotoGP race action for the past six weeks.
But now with a full treatment plan completed and weeks of rest at home, he feels ready to return at 100% for this weekend's Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang.

Mir withdrew from San Marino GP in mid-September following complaints of fatigue and, following adverse blood tests in the days after, has been on the long term sick list since, missing 44 days from the paddock and races in Austria, Japan, Indonesia, and Australia.

With little information on his condition over the past weeks, there has been plenty of paddock speculation about what exactly the 2020 world champion was suffering from, with vision issues one of the theories raised - something he explained on his return to the paddock without going into too much detail.

"I'm so happy to be back," he replied when asked by The Race about his condition. "As you can imagine. It's been a period that I simply needed to stop, because I had some vision problems that at the beginning we didn't really know what was happening.

"Related to this was the tiredness, but quite extreme. It was a process that was getting worse in the last races I did, in the first part of the season. I was forced to stop. I started treatment with [MotoGP medical director] Doctor Charte, and we could understand a little bit the problem.

"I think the cause was related to one problem I had in the past with the vision, and with the stress of the races it was getting worse. The tiredness was related to this thing, but until the moment where we understood this thing, we made a lot of tests."

Prior to his long-term absence from the paddock, it's not exactly been an easy season for Mir in his final stint as a Honda racer, crashing out of nine of his 14 full distance MotoGP races this season so far.

article_paragraphs: Last week, I attended Greenbuild International Conference + Expo 2026 in the North Hall of the Javits Center here in NYC.

After being overwhelmed by shows like CES and InterSolar Europe , the smaller scale of Greenbuild was a welcome break. At the show, there were a few heat pumps and Copper brought their battery-backed induction range, but less emphasis was placed on renewable energy storage and energy efficiency than other events. Many of the people I talked to had not heard the emissions reduction requirements of New York City’s LL97 , which was a major motivator of Build Expo in the Spring. I also did not see much media presence at the show.

However, what stood out at Greenbuild was an emphasis on green materials. Although some of these companies had appeared at other shows, I had more opportunity to discuss and really get into the details at Greenbuild. A few exhibitors stood out.

Durra Panel was the first product to really attract my attention. Throughout history, straw has gotten a bad rap in parables. In contrast to the “Three Little Pigs” folktale, Durra Panel is using straw to create a building material that is not only more sustainable but, in many ways, better than traditional materials.

The standard boards are 96% compressed straw and 4% recycled craft paper. The process uses heat and pressure to bond the straw together with naturally occurring lignin, with no added binders needed. In the process, the straw panel gains a 1-hour (60-minute) Fire Resistance Level (FRL). The panels are 99.9% VOC-free, but the resulting panel, which incorporates biochar, actually absorb VOCs from the environment where they are installed. Standard panels are 50 or 58 mm thick (~2”).

Due to the mechanical strength of the panel, it can replace a partition wall or form a walkable roof without additional reinforcement or studs. Compared to a stud wall, the embodied energy drops from 153 MJ/m 2 to 12.6 MJ/m 2 . It simply needs a header and footer to be mounted as a wall. According to Durra Panel, these walls provide an 84% time savings and 21% cost savings versus traditional building materials.

In a place like NYC, where rented commercial real estate and offices frequently have partition walls added and removed with high labor costs, those savings could add up quickly. In addition, the walls can be dismantled and re-used, further reducing cost and environmental impact.

The technology was developed in Australia decades ago, but it is expanding globally. Due to the acoustic performance, it is often used to build recording studios . Durra Panel recently selected Brocton, Massachusetts for their first US manufacturing facility.

article_paragraphs: The Trump administration has already delayed implementation of the critical standards for year+

Washington, DC — Last night during a rally in Texas, Donald Trump announced that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency would roll back safeguards finalized in 2024 to limit methane pollution from the oil and gas sector. This dangerous reversal— revealed earlier this month by Administrator Lee Zeldin —would allow bad-actor corporations to release more climate-disrupting compounds and other pollutants into our atmosphere, jeopardizing the health and wellbeing of our families and communities.

In 2024, the Biden Administration issued landmark methane standards for the oil and gas sector that significantly reduce these and other pollutants from both new and existing equipment. These safeguards are based on low-cost, commonsense practices and technologies that have been available to oil and gas operators for years or even decades. For instance, the standards require operators to capture or use gas at oil wells rather than flare it; to conduct regular inspections to identify and fix leaking equipment at well sites and compressor stations; and to use zero-emitting electric pumps and process controllers rather than gas-powered devices.

Soon after taking office in 2025, the Trump EPA suspended the implementation of key provisions from the Biden-era standards, delaying their enforcement by up to 18 months despite no widespread evidence of compliance difficulties. Now, the EPA is preparing a proposal that would permanently eliminate some of the rule’s most important safeguards, including its ban on routine flaring at oil wells and its program to leverage third-party monitoring data to identify and stop particularly large methane releases known as super-emitter events.

The proposal would also shield low-producing wells from leak monitoring requirements, despite consistent evidence showing that such wells do not pollute less than higher-producing wells. Nearly one in ten people in the U.S. live in a county with over a thousand low-producing wells . These sources represent nearly half of the sector’s methane emissions and are primarily owned by large, well-resourced and highly profitable corporations.

Cyrus Reed, Legislative and Conservation Director of Sierra Club’s Lone Star Chapter , said: “No state produces more oil and gas than Texas, and no state has more emissions of methane and associated gases than Texas, and yet the state has no state-level rules to protect us from its dangers. This proposed rollback is an affront to the thousands of Texans who have depended on and called on the EPA to protect us, and yet this proposal is designed to let so-called low-producing oil and gas wells off the hook, even though nearly half of all methane emissions come from these low-producing oil and gas wells.”

Sarah Corcoran, Deputy Director of the Sierra Club Pennsylvania Chapter , said: “Policies that reduce methane waste are commonsense and cost effective. The Trump Administration is not doing anyone any favors by reducing these regulations, not the industry, not the environment and not the American people who will feel the health impacts of these decisions for years to come. Companies have repeatedly made promises to reduce methane pollution – but voluntary measures are often empty promises. We need strict, enforceable regulations in order to hold companies accountable.”

Antoinette Reyes, Sierra Club Rio Grande Chapter Organizer , said: “New Mexico cannot afford a federal retreat on methane. The 2024 EPA safeguards were designed to do basic, practical things: find leaks, stop routine flaring, catch super-emitter events, and require operators to use cleaner equipment that already exists. Rolling those protections back—including protections for low-producing wells that make up a majority of active wells in both New Mexico and Texas—would create a sweeping industry loophole. Oil and gas pollution is like secondhand smoke from the industry: communities are exposed without consent, and the people closest to the source carry the heaviest burden. With the Permian spanning both Texas and New Mexico, pollution knows no boundaries, which is exactly why New Mexico and other states must codify these methane protections into state law and make them strong enough to withstand political rollbacks in Washington.”

article_paragraphs: BYD now has more than 1.02 million employees, according to chairman Wang Chuanfu. That’s more people than Toyota, GM, Ford, and Tesla employ combined.

And it’s a big jump from the start of the year. BYD reported about 869,600 employees at the end of 2025, which means the Chinese automaker has added roughly 150,000 people in 10 months while its vehicle sales are down.

Roughly 960,000 of BYD’s people work in China and about 60,000 work abroad. Up to 120,000 of them are R&D engineers, according to Wang, who shared the figures on stage Wednesday at the China Society of Automotive Engineers’ (CSAE) 33rd annual conference. Their work covers battery cells, motors, electronic controls, and semiconductors.

Wang credits vertical integration for that scale. In his telling, keeping batteries, chips, and motors in-house is what took BYD from a battery maker founded in 1994 to the world’s top-selling new energy vehicle brand several years running. He called the company’s rise a microcosm of China’s auto industry going from follower to leader.
BYD’s workforce has been all over the place in the last few years.

The company had about 570,100 employees at the end of 2022 and 703,500 at the end of 2023. Then it went on a hiring spree. We reported in September 2024 that BYD had passed 900,000 employees and claimed the largest R&D workforce of any automaker, with over 110,000 engineers. It ended 2024 with 968,900 people.
Then came the first big cut. BYD’s 2025 annual report showed roughly 869,600 employees at year-end, a drop of about 99,000, mostly in frontline production jobs.
Now it’s back over a million. Data compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence put BYD at 911,900 employees at the end of June, so the company added more than 100,000 people in about four months.

title: The Truth About Renewable Electricity: Your Questions, Answered
raw_summary: Reliable, affordable electricity is essential for many of the products and services that underpin the modern economy. But the sources of that electricity—and their respective merits and risks—are increasingly the subject of debate and polarization. A flood of narratives and counternarratives is rising in the media and public conversation about the reliability and affordability of renewables, as well as their impacts on the economy, jobs, and communities. But the sources of that electricity—and their respective merits and risks—are increasingly the subject of debate and polarization. A flood of narratives and counternarratives is rising in the media and public conversation about the reliability and affordability of renewables, as well as their impacts on the economy, jobs, and communities.
article_paragraphs: Reliable, affordable electricity is essential for many of the products and services that underpin the modern economy. But the sources of that electricity—and their respective merits and risks—are increasingly the subject of debate and polarization.

A flood of narratives and counternarratives is rising in the media and public conversation about the reliability and affordability of renewables, as well as their impacts on the economy, jobs, and communities. These mixed messages can make it hard to get the accurate information people need as they face important decisions about how they live, spend, or vote.
Here, we answer some common questions about renewable electricity, using the latest evidence, data, and research.
Renewable electricity is power generated from naturally replenishing energy sources, including solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, and biomass.

Solar and wind are considered “variable,” in that their output depends on weather, time of day, and season. Hydropower, geothermal, and biomass are considered “firm” in that their output is reliably available on demand (although no power plant, whether it uses fossil fuels or renewables, is always available). Experience and modeling show that electricity grids can be reliable, affordable, and clean (low-carbon) by combining high volumes of variable and firm renewables with energy storage and other low-carbon generating sources.

Renewables accounted for around 34% of global electricity generation in 2025 , with 15% from hydropower, 8% from wind, and 7% from solar. Wind and solar have grown significantly since 2015, when their shares in global electricity generation were only 3.4% and 1%, respectively.

Still, having been in use for more than a century, fossil fuels remain the dominant electricity generation source globally. They account for nearly 60% of the world’s electricity , primarily from coal (35%) and natural gas (22%).
Renewable electricity is not just growing—it’s skyrocketing. Solar and wind deployment in particular are expanding faster than any other electricity sources.
