article_paragraphs: SUPERIOR, Wisconsin — Today, Dairyland Power Coop announced the cancellation of plans for NTEC, which was proposed to be built on the shores of Lake Superior, and asked the Wisconsin Public Service Commission (PSC) to withdraw its permits.

The Nemadji Trail Energy Center (NTEC), a 625 MW natural gas plant, has faced years of public pushback from local residents, Dairyland Power customers, members of the Fond du Lac and Red Cliff Bands of Lake Superior Chippewa, and environmental groups.

“We applaud Dairyland Power Coop and South Shore Energy for formally cancelling the NTEC gas plant and asking for their permits to be withdrawn, after the clock ran out on their PSC permits,” said Elizabeth Ward, Wisconsin Chapter Director. “NTEC has faced years of public opposition and was outdated as soon as it was proposed. This is a victory for the Great Lakes, our climate, and the city of Superior, whose city leaders have relentlessly worked to protect residents from the air pollution caused by a dirty, expensive gas plant. We thank them for their tireless leadership and attribute this success to them.”

“NTEC was never a good idea,” said Evan Mulholland, Healthy Communities Program Director at MCEA. “NTEC would have been bad for the climate, too expensive, unnecessary for grid reliability, and harmful to public health, and it was proposed in the wrong location. MCEA is grateful for all the organizers and partners who helped with the campaign against NTEC over the past 10 years.”

“This victory is the culmination of more than seven years of relentless work to defeat a project that would have brought tremendous harm to communities in Superior and beyond,” said Clean Wisconsin Director of Legal Advocacy Brett Korte. “Clean Wisconsin first intervened at the Public Service Commission to stop the plant in 2019 and the fight continued in court and city council chambers, before agencies, and in public conversation. We are grateful to all the partners including tribal advocates, other environmental organizations, and community members who never stopped fighting and believing that against all odds, this gas plant would be defeated.”

title: Louisiana DEQ Issues Rushed, Controversial Air Permit to Proposed Hyundai Steel Facility
raw_summary: Donaldsonville, Louisiana — Yesterday, the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) posted the final, approved air permit for Hyundai’s proposed steel plant. Hyundai promised a state-of-the-art, clean facility, but the proposed plan falls short of those promises and would still bring thousands of tons of pollution to Cancer Alley, a region already overburdened with dirty air and water. Throughout 2026, Sierra Club, working with experts and local groups, submitted a series of comments to LDEQ in an effort to bring to light the errors, miscalculations, and omissions in the permit application. Hyundai Steel made some changes to its permit application as a result of those comments, updating plans to electrify some components of the facility, which will lower levels of pollution.

article_paragraphs: Donaldsonville, Louisiana — Yesterday, the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) posted the final, approved air permit for Hyundai’s proposed steel plant. Hyundai promised a state-of-the-art, clean facility, but the proposed plan falls short of those promises and would still bring thousands of tons of pollution to Cancer Alley, a region already overburdened with dirty air and water.

Throughout 2026, Sierra Club, working with experts and local groups, submitted a series of comments to LDEQ in an effort to bring to light the errors, miscalculations, and omissions in the permit application. Hyundai Steel made some changes to its permit application as a result of those comments, updating plans to electrify some components of the facility, which will lower levels of pollution.

Still, the final air permit issued by LDEQ yesterday fails to require Hyundai to significantly reduce pollution by electrifying additional components or blending in green hydrogen, nor does it require best-available technology for controlling toxic dust. Astoundingly, LDEQ found that this massive new greenfield facility would have “no adverse impacts” and therefore failed to include an environmental justice analysis, even though Ascension Parish already experiences toxic pollution at levels exceeding 96% of the rest of the country. (Hyundai Steel initially included, but then completely removed, the environmental justice analysis from the permit application.) LDEQ also did not do any independent analysis of alternative sites to determine if there is a location that would be less harmful to surrounding communities.
In response, Sierra Club Industrial Transformation Campaign Director Matthew Miles Goodrich issued the following statement:

“Hyundai Steel says it wants to be a ‘catalyst for the future steel industry and hydrogen ecosystem,’ but its air permit tells a different story. The company made some improvements to its facility in response to public pressure, but it needs to do more to reduce dangerous pollution through electrification and make a firm commitment to green hydrogen. The South Korean government is mobilizing three-quarters of a trillion dollars to develop and incentivize clean industry, like green steel made with hydrogen, in its own country. That begs the question: why isn’t Hyundai—which is so well-positioned to produce and use steel—bringing the cleanest technologies to one of the most polluted communities in America? We will continue to evaluate the final permit and are exploring our legal options and next steps.”

title: Jetson Launches Fixed Price Heat Pump Water Heater with Installation Included
raw_summary: This Heat Pump Water Heater Week , Jetson dropped some big news. They are bringing a heat pump water heater (HPWH) to market using the same model of vertical integration that they use with heat pump installations, where they procure all equipment as well as install and monitor the HPWHs, all for a fixed price. CEO Stephen Lake talked with the Advanced Water Heating Initiative about the heat pump water heater that the company is launching into the market and the company’s unique way of owning every step of the installation process, which they believe drives down cost and improves customer experiences.

article_paragraphs: This Heat Pump Water Heater Week , Jetson dropped some big news. They are bringing a heat pump water heater (HPWH) to market using the same model of vertical integration that they use with heat pump installations, where they procure all equipment as well as install and monitor the HPWHs, all for a fixed price.

CEO Stephen Lake talked with the Advanced Water Heating Initiative about the heat pump water heater that the company is launching into the market and the company’s unique way of owning every step of the installation process, which they believe drives down cost and improves customer experiences.
Jetson is also joining 17 other HPWH manufacturers in what is becoming a full, efficient water heating marketplace.

Jetson launched its heat pump model for heating and cooling homes just two years ago. They got started in Vancouver BC and Denver, and since have moved into New York, California, Tennessee and Maryland.

Their model is to own the entire process of heat pump installation, from quoting to procurement, to installation, to servicing and repairs. They also analyze data from their equipment to make sure systems are running optimally. Their goal is to tackle the two biggest hurdles to electrification and decarbonization — cost and consumer experience.

From heat pumps for space heating, the company is now moving into the heat pump water heater space. They said they’ve heard from homeowners who wanted their water heater replaced in addition to their furnace. And Jetson is bringing the same philosophy of owning the whole installation process, which could shake things up in the industry.

Heat pump water heaters are at an inflection point. Their sales are still only around 2 to 3% of water heater sales nationally, but they’ve grown consistently since coming to market 15 years ago and there are now many product options and manufacturers to choose from. Plus, an upcoming DOE water heating standard will phase out inefficient, electric water heaters and give a boost to this technology starting in 2029. Sales could rise into the millions by the end of the decade.

But, like most technologies on the early part of their adoption curve, heat pump water heaters can carry an upfront cost that is 2 to 3 times more than other water heaters. Many areas have rebates to help with these costs, and many consumers are DIYing their installations to save money, but the high price barrier remains.

article_paragraphs: They day you get to book an all-electric flight may be closer than you think if Dutch startup Elysian Aircraft gets its way. Their new E9X commercial airliner promises flights that are a whole lot quieter, and at prices that are whole lot less dependent on dumb oil wars .

Aircraft account for more than 2% of global heating when CO₂ and other emissions are taken into account, with the share considerably higher in wealthy countries, according to data cited by climate campaign group Stay Grounded . Elysian Aircraft is keenly aware of the industry’s climate impact, and they believe their planned full-size electric airliner will be perfectly positioned to make a dramatic difference.

“By being able to transport 90 passengers for initially 800 kilometers and eventually 1,000 kilometers you can reduce emissions to zero, from half the world’s flights,” Elysian co-founder Daniel Jacobson told EuroNews . “That is a very large amount of flight activity in the world. And you reduce total emissions from aerospace by 20%.”

At the core of those ambitious emission-reduction goals is the Elysian E9X aircraft. Designed in collaboration with aerospace researchers at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), the E9X packs its oversized wings with modular battery packs, sending power to six propellers driven by electric motors.

Specs on those haven’t been revealed, but the E9X is designed to carry up to 100 passengers up to 1,000 km (~620 miles) from where they started. Elysian says that’s enough range to handle nearly 50% of scheduled commercial passenger flights worldwide and potentially eliminate 20% of total in-flight emissions when the plane enters service in 2034.

That said, the E9X is far more than “just a concept,” and Elysian has completed its second conceptual design review and flown a scaled demonstrator in concert with Germany’s DLR aerospace research center , demonstrating how its unique battery packaging solutions address the challenges of integrating heavy battery packs into an aircraft’s wings (where fuel is traditionally stored).

The company is also working with airline partners KLM and Transavia to explore the operational and commercial requirements for putting electric airliners into service, with aircraft lessor TrueNoord investigating how the E9X could be financed and supported commercially.

raw_title: With Alpina's New 7-Series, You'll Never Think About An M7 Again
title: With Alpina's New 7-Series, You'll Never Think About An M7 Again
raw_summary: For decades, Alpina worked independently of BMW, but maintained a close relationship with the German brand and built some incredible BMW-based models. Now, BMW fully owns Alpina, and work is well underway on its first model under the new ownership. This new car, based on the updated 7-Series , is shaping up to be rather special. These new spy shots offer a glimpse of the luxury sedan's design and show how it will stand out from a regular 7-Series. The changes start at the front, where this prototype, snapped near BMW's test center at the Nürburgring, has unique amber LED daytime running lights. Though it's possible these lights may not make their way into the production model, we suspect they will, serving as an obvious differentiator between the Alpina model and a normal 7-Series. The re-launched Alpina brand previewed its future with the stunning Vision Alpina concept in May , and that car also had amber DRLs, so this may become a signature of all future Alpina models.

Though it's possible these lights may not make their way into the production model, we suspect they will, serving as an obvious differentiator between the Alpina model and a normal 7-Series. The re-launched Alpina brand previewed its future with the stunning Vision Alpina concept in May , and that car also had amber DRLs, so this may become a signature of all future Alpina models.

Other changes are visible. This prototype's large kidney grilles have only three horizontal slats, compared with the seven on the standard 7-Series. The lower part of the bumper and the bottom air intake also appear unique to this car. It is also rolling on a set of eye-catching black wheels with silver elements, ensuring it stands out even further from the base car. Modifications made to the rear of the car appear to be more limited and include Alpina's familiar oval-shaped tailpipes. The production model may also feature a new rear bumper.

Alpina's previous 7-Series-based B7 was built between 2016 and 2022 and came standard with a twin-turbocharged 4.4-liter V8 from the 750Li, upgraded to deliver 600 horsepower. Earlier this month, BMW unveiled the new M760 xDrive in the U.S., equipped with the latest version of this twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 producing around 570 hp and arriving standard with all-wheel drive.

The new Alpina will likely be based on this model and use the same basic engine, albeit slightly fettled to increase horsepower and torque. In typical Alpina fashion, the car will benefit from much more than engine modifications. The brand has always perfectly balanced sporty and dynamic handling with comfort and poise, and we expect nothing less of its new 7-Series model. We also wouldn't count on this prototype's wheels to make the production car, and a set of traditional, tightly-spoked Alpina wheels, seem more likely.

BMW hasn't confirmed a launch date for the new Alpina 7-Series, but it will probably be unveiled next year. If a high-end luxury sedan isn't to your taste, BMW confirmed earlier this year that Alpina will also launch its own version of the next-generation X7, tipped to launch in 2027.

The front of the car retains some elements from the GR Yaris hot hatch, including the headlights and taillights. Other than that, it appears to carry over very little from the production model. Images shared online by CarWatch in Japan show that there's a larger radiator and fan beneath the hood, where the Yaris's turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder usually sits.

The rear half of the race car is particularly interesting. It includes boxy, flared wheel arches and quarter panels with larger air intakes to feed the engine. Toyota has also equipped the car with a fixed rear wing and a unique diffuser. As dramatic as this prototype's exterior is, what's beneath the rear glass is what will really excite Toyota enthusiasts.

Toyota is hard at work developing a new turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four for its new mid-engined production model , and future iterations of the GR Yaris and GR Corolla. It's more powerful than the smaller 1.6-liter turbo three-cylinder and also outperforms the company's outgoing 2.4-liter turbo. Standard, road-legal models with this new engine are tipped to produce around 300 hp and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque, and other higher-performance versions may deliver upwards of 400 hp and 406 lb-ft (550 Nm).

It remains unclear whether Toyota is reviving both the MR2 and Celica or if it's bringing back just one of these models, and which one it is. Whatever the case may be, the car will pair the new 2.0-liter turbo with an all-wheel-drive system and Torsen limited-slip differentials at the front and rear axles, just like Toyota's flagship hot hatches. The company's current eight-speed automatic could be used, or Toyota may even decide to use a six-speed manual transmission. Whatever ends up happening, it's hard not to be excited by Toyota's commitment to high-performance sports cars.

Used EV sales rose to a record 3.3% of total used vehicle sales last month, up from 2.9% in August, according to Cox Automotive .
Used ICE vehicle sales, on the other hand, dropped 4.4% in September as buyers flocked to more efficient options.
As expected, Tesla remains the leading used EV brand, followed by Ford, Chevrolet, Hyundai, and BMW.

By model, the Nissan Ariya led growth, with sales up 42.5% in September, followed by the Chevy Equinox EV (+41.9%), Kia EV9 (+36.2%), and Chevy Blazer EV (+30.2%), while the Ford Mustang Mach-E (+14.7%) and Tesla Model Y (+13.8 %) also saw more demand.

With more options to choose from, which one is best for you? To help you decide, Edmunds , which has tested nearly all of them, put together a list of four top used electric SUVs available for under $25,000.
The first one on the list was the Chevy Equinox EV , or as GM used to call it, “America’s most affordable 315+ range” electric vehicle.

title: The Jeep Gladiator Has Just Become An Even More Capable Off-Roader
raw_summary: The Jeep Gladiator is already a very capable off-roader , and now, it promises to be even better. As part of the updated 2027 Gladiator model, Jeep has unveiled a new version dubbed the 35-inch Tire Launch Edition. The name leaves a lot to be desired, though this model certainly has all the makings of a serious performer. The limited-production package is available for the Gladiator Willys , Rubicon, and Rubicon X models and comes standard with 17-inch bronze-painted beadlock-capable wheels and 35-inch all-terrain tires. The new wheel and tire package is supported by a 1-inch factory suspension lift, boosting the Gladiator's approach and departure angles to 46.7 degrees and 26.7 degrees, respectively. The breakover angle has also been improved to 23.3 degrees. While we would argue the Gladiator is a little too long for some tight trails, these improvements will definitely be helpful for more open off-roading adventures. In addition, it comes equipped with performance brakes, heavy-duty Dana axles at the front and rear, a 4.56 final drive ratio, and a full-time 4:1 transfer case.

The 35-inch Tire Launch Edition package doesn't include upgrades to the Gladiator's engine, meaning it retains the familiar naturally-aspirated 3.6-liter Pentastar V6 with 285 horsepower and 260 pound-feet of torque, working alongside an 8-speed automatic transmission. However, the package does bring with it several visual upgrades beyond the wheels and tires. These include highline fender flares and wheel arch extensions, a performance hood, bronze Jeep badging and accents, graphics for the hood, side, and tailgate, and bronze tow hooks. Gladiator Rubicon models equipped with the package get their own distinctive hood and vent graphics.

"Gladiator customers continue to personalize their vehicles to tackle bigger adventures, and 35-inch tires have consistently been one of the most popular modifications," Jeep CEO Branden Coté said. "The Gladiator 35-inch Tire Launch Edition gives customers the capability, confidence and distinctive look they want straight from the factory, backed by the quality and engineering expected from the Jeep brand." The automaker has not said how many examples of the special package it will produce or how much it'll cost.

raw_summary: Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) wants to bring back the federal EV tax credit and double it. His new bill, the “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” (H.R. 10881), would offer up to $15,000 on a new electric vehicle and $8,000 on a used one, and it would make both credits permanent. summary: Greg Landsman (D-OH) wants to bring back the federal EV tax credit and double it. His new bill, the “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” (H.R. 10881), would offer up to $15,000 on a new electric vehicle and $8,000 on a used one, and it would make both credits permanent.
article_paragraphs: Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) wants to bring back the federal EV tax credit and double it. His new bill, the “21st Century Vehicle Choice Act” (H.R. 10881), would offer up to $15,000 on a new electric vehicle and $8,000 on a used one, and it would make both credits permanent.
The problem is that the bill has virtually no chance of becoming law anytime soon. And if EV shoppers start holding out for it, it could end up hurting the market it’s trying to help.

Landsman introduced H.R. 10881 on October 22. It was referred to three House committees (Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce, and Natural Resources), and as of today, it doesn’t have a single cosponsor.

The big change is to the new clean vehicle credit, Section 30D of the tax code. Under the Inflation Reduction Act, the $7,500 credit came in two $3,750 halves: one for meeting critical mineral sourcing requirements and one for battery components. Landsman’s bill doubles each half to $7,500, for a maximum of $15,000.

It also deletes the termination dates. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act killed the new and used EV credits for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025, and the home charger credit after June 30, 2026. Striking those dates would revive all three credits with no expiration.

The bill doesn’t touch the rest of 30D. North American final assembly, the $55,000 MSRP cap on cars and $80,000 cap on SUVs, pickups, and vans, and the foreign entity of concern rules all stay. So the full $15,000 would only go to EVs that clear both sourcing tests, which has always been a short list.

The rest of the bill is reports. Commerce would deliver a “Vehicle Choice Report” on vehicle variety and ownership costs, and the Department of Energy would file five years of critical minerals reports.

The most interesting part is a DOE study of “gasoline super-users,” defined as the top 10% of light-duty vehicle owners by gas consumption. The study would map the regions where they’re concentrated and their 100 most-used routes, then track charger availability along those routes every year for five years. Coltura, which backs the bill, says the highest-mileage drivers spend over 10% of household income on fuel.

title: Ford Recalls 102,159 F-150 and Super Duty Trucks over Faulty Gauges
raw_summary: Ford is recalling 102,159 F-150 and Super Duty trucks due to analog gauge clusters that could display incorrect speedometer and tachometer information. The automaker’s Super Duty lineup is most affected, with 91,588 F-250, F-350, F-450, F-550, and F-600 vehicles involved in the recall, all from the 2025–2026 model years. F-150s are also affected, but much less so, with just 10,570 units from the 2026 model year included. One 2026 F-750 has also been recalled. Documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) say that analog tachometers and speedometers in the vehicles could get stuck or move erratically, which would show an inaccurate speed reading. No warning lights will appear in affected vehicles, but those with both digital and analog speedometers may see differences between the two readings.

Documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) say that analog tachometers and speedometers in the vehicles could get stuck or move erratically, which would show an inaccurate speed reading. No warning lights will appear in affected vehicles, but those with both digital and analog speedometers may see differences between the two readings.

Ford hasn’t received any accident reports, but the automaker identified 18 warranty and 93 field reports related to the issue by September 16. The affected vehicles aren’t produced in VIN order, so the best way to check a vehicle’s recall status, aside from waiting for an owner notification, is to call Ford’s hotline or contact a Ford or Lincoln dealer.

Owners of affected vehicles will be notified by October 30, but the replacement part won’t be ready until early December. Ford expects to alert owners of the available remedy by December 11. Once the new part is available, a dealer will replace the instrument cluster at no charge to the owner.

raw_title: The BMW X3 M50 Just Got An Extra 44 HP For 2027
title: The BMW X3 M50 Just Got An Extra 44 HP For 2027
raw_summary: The M Performance version of the BMW X3 is already way more powerful than most of its owners need, but because this sort of purchase is anything but rational, BMW is fixing it anyway with a 44-horsepower bump for the upcoming model year. Still powered by the 3.0-liter turbocharged B58 straight-6, the 2027 BMW X3 M50 xDrive will make 437 hp, up from the 2026 model's 393 hp. This will let the luxury performance crossover get from 0 to 60 mph in 4.3 seconds, or 4 seconds flat with a 1-foot rollout. For comparison, BMW lists a 4.4-second 0-60 time for last year's model, presumably without the rollout. The revised X3 M50 also gets an updated exhaust system that BMW says sounds "deeper" and "more resonant."

For comparison, BMW lists a 4.4-second 0-60 time for last year's model, presumably without the rollout. The revised X3 M50 also gets an updated exhaust system that BMW says sounds "deeper" and "more resonant."

In the sphere of luxury compact mid-performance crossovers, this puts the X3 closer to its new Mercedes-AMG GLC53 archrival , which produces 443 hp from its identical-format mild hybrid 3.0-liter turbo straight-6. You can almost hear the angry German boardroom meeting in Munich that led to this somewhat more powerful X3 once BMW got word that Mercedes was Top Trumping them. I mean, Mercedes is still Top Trumping 'em, but the margin is a lot smaller now. To save you the search, the current Audi SQ5 is good for a relatively tame 362 hp and hits 60 mph in 4.6.

All '27 X3 M50s will get the extra hp, but not all of them will get the newly available Black Package option. This $3,800 add-on throws in black 22-inch M alloy wheels, black M Sport brake calipers, black-and-silver M badges throughout, plus a blacked-out interior with lots of Alcantara suede trim, matte carbon-aluminum hard surfaces, smoky silver door sill trim, and an M steering wheel with a different leather airbag cover.

One of the most common criticisms of this new-gen X3 has been its interior materials, and BMW says all 2027 X3s (not just M50s) will get some cabin updates. There's a new "PVC Softskin" surface for the area in front of the touchscreen, new dash stitching, ambient lighting for the center console cubby and door handles, a new glove box opener, and new stainless steel protectors for the cargo sill.
The now-more-powerful 2027 BMW X3 M50 will start at $67,500 plus $1,350 destination.

raw_title: 'You're Not Taking My Bike', Says Rider Whose Bike Was Taken
title: You're Not Taking My Bike', Says Rider Whose Bike Was Taken
raw_summary: There are plenty of ways to approach an interaction with police on the road, but making a run for it on an e-bike isn't a good one. Making a bold prediction about how it's going to end is quite the gamble too. One man in British Columbia allegedly told an officer, "You're not taking my bike," before speeding away. As you've probably gathered from the headline, that confidence had little basis in reality. According to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) , the encounter happened on the evening of October 8 near Lougheed Highway and the Cedar Valley Connector. Police attempted to stop a man riding an electric dirt bike. While e-bikes are legal in most places in Canada, electric dirt bikes like this one aren't the same and are prohibited from roads, sidewalks, and bike lanes. So officers had good reason to want to chat. When they made contact, the rider made his declaration and sped away. His escape didn't last long, as officers caught up and arrested him for fleeing. According to the RCMP, the 41-year-old showed signs of alcohol impairment and refused to provide a breath sample at the scene. While it's only an allegation, impairment might help explain the questionable choices up to this point.

article_paragraphs: There are plenty of ways to approach an interaction with police on the road, but making a run for it on an e-bike isn't a good one. Making a bold prediction about how it's going to end is quite the gamble too. One man in British Columbia allegedly told an officer, "You're not taking my bike," before speeding away. As you've probably gathered from the headline, that confidence had little basis in reality. According to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) , the encounter happened on the evening of October 8 near Lougheed Highway and the Cedar Valley Connector. Police attempted to stop a man riding an electric dirt bike.

While e-bikes are legal in most places in Canada, electric dirt bikes like this one aren't the same and are prohibited from roads, sidewalks, and bike lanes. So officers had good reason to want to chat. When they made contact, the rider made his declaration and sped away. His escape didn't last long, as officers caught up and arrested him for fleeing. According to the RCMP, the 41-year-old showed signs of alcohol impairment and refused to provide a breath sample at the scene. While it's only an allegation, impairment might help explain the questionable choices up to this point.

According to officers, the man is prohibited from driving for 90 days and must pay for the various fines and violations he collected that day. While they didn't list out the charges, the refusal to take a breath test automatically allowed the officers to impose that driving ban. In addition, it gave the officers the right to impound the bike, though the duration of that penalty is unclear. All told, the alleged attempt to keep the bike ended with the rider losing access to it and his driving privileges.

That's a pretty poor return on the effort. In addition, it's possible that the rider is facing more charges that we aren't privy to. Along with being illegal to ride this kind of e-bike on roads or bike lanes, police can also charge a person with additional fines, depending on the violations. The fine for driving without a license, for example, is CA$276 and driving without insurance, a common issue in New Mexico as it turns out, is another CA$598. All of this is just one more good reminder to avoid doing illegal things on the road and, when pulled over, try to let the officer do the predicting.

Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026.
Official information from the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) revealed shortly after that several thousand more VW Group electric vehicles are affected worldwide.
In three separate recalls now under investigation by the KBA, 72,668 VW Group EVs were included worldwide, including 9,881 in Germany.
The recall affects certain batches of the ID. Buzz, ID.3, ID.4, and ID.7 models produced between 2022 and 2025, as well as Cupra Born models from 2022 to 2024.

On October 27, VW Group added another electric vehicle to the KBA recall database. The latest recall impacts 12,734 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles globally, including just one in Germany. In total, Volkswagen’s battery recall now affects 85,402 EVs globally.

In the letter sent to the NHTSA on October 23, Volkswagen Group of America said it was issuing a recall affecting 9,048 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles in the US model years 2024 to 2025.
The recall stems from the risk of the battery overheating and potentially causing a fire under certain conditions when charged to over 80% of its limit.

title: Luxury Around-The-World Cruise Stranded In Cambodia Over Staggering Fuel Costs
raw_summary: Some people fantasize about escaping the world's problems by stepping on a cruise ship and drowning themselves in cocktails and gorging themselves on appetizers from all-you-can-eat buffets. But the real world seems to have gotten in the way of this escapist fantasy for some. The Villa Vie Odyssey announced on Wednesday that it has suspended operations amid rising fuel costs, stranding the ship's passengers in Cambodia. The cruise ship departed Belfast, Northern Ireland, in 2024 to embark on a perpetual around-the-world cruise that has now abruptly ended after two years at sea. The Villa Vie Odyssey wasn't immune to the U.S. war against Iran, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and the resulting spike in fuel prices. The ship's operator, Villa Vie Residences, said the ship's monthly fuel costs have jumped to $8,000 per cabin in parts of Asia. That's a staggering increase, especially since the ship has 485 cabins and the average monthly fuel cost was previously $1,800 per cabin. The Villa Vie Odyssey tried to cut fuel use by spending more time in port. The operator even floated the idea of adding a fuel surcharge, but admitted it couldn't realistically pass the full increase on to passengers.

The Villa Vie Odyssey tried to cut fuel use by spending more time in port. The operator even floated the idea of adding a fuel surcharge, but admitted it couldn't realistically pass the full increase on to passengers.

Passengers had little time to prepare for the voyage's sudden end in Sihanoukville, Cambodia. A couple onboard told the BBC that the CEO of Villa Vie Residences informed everyone onboard at 6:00 a.m. on Tuesday that they had to disembark at 2:00 p.m. the same day. Many passengers and crew are now residing at hotels in the coastal resort city. Others are using the opportunity to travel on their own across Southeast Asia. Passengers purchased their cabin residences for between $120,000 and $440,000, and now they'll have to wait to hear the fate of the company and the ship.

Villa Vie Residences stated that it will "work toward restructuring and recapitalization over the next 60 days." The around-the-world cruise was a rocky operation before it even departed Belfast two years ago. The Villa Vie Odyssey was stuck in port for four months due to maintenance issues. As passengers waited out the delay in nearby hotels, one woman was banned from the cruise after complaining about it . When the Villa Vie Odyssey finally got underway, the ship remained anchored off the coast to complete paperwork . Despite the rough start and abrupt conclusion, passengers say that it was an unforgettable two years at sea.

title: The Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Performance Concept Is Cooler Than You
raw_summary: Confession time: Of all the cars Toyota sells at the moment, the oddball Crown Signia is easily my favorite. It's about as practical and efficient as the RAV4 Hybrid while being significantly nicer to live with in person. It drives better, it looks cooler, and it has a quiet-luxury aura that even a comparable Lexus NX arguably falls short of. Among my car reviewer colleagues, however, it's split — some quietly love it, too, but a lot just find it perplexing . In other words, you either get it or you don't, and it looks like at least somebody within Toyota tasked with managing its presence at the SEMA Show this year absolutely gets it. Toyota is showing up to Vegas next month with the Crown Signia GT-S Performance Concept built by the Toyota Motorsports Garage, a vehicle Toyota calls "a sleek grand touring machine that blends everyday space and comfort with the attitude and road feel of a true sports car." Yep, it's an unnecessary sporty version of an enjoyably un-sporty car, and that's arguably why it's so damn cool.

Toyota is showing up to Vegas next month with the Crown Signia GT-S Performance Concept built by the Toyota Motorsports Garage, a vehicle Toyota calls "a sleek grand touring machine that blends everyday space and comfort with the attitude and road feel of a true sports car." Yep, it's an unnecessary sporty version of an enjoyably un-sporty car, and that's arguably why it's so damn cool.

Sitting nearly 5 inches lower than the stock Signia on one-off MCS coilovers, the Signia GT-S also lets the five-door Crown be the station wagon I feel it always wanted to be. Officially, Toyota describes the standard car as a crossover, but in reality, its ride height almost perfectly splits the difference between that of a Camry and that of a RAV4. What is a slammed half-crossover other than a station wagon?

The fenders are seamlessly swollen, the hammerhead element up front is trimmed red just like all the badges, and it gets both a front lip and rear diffuser that make it look like it came off a Super Street cover. The dark gray metallic paint is a custom mix, and the exhaust with trapezoidal tips is also a custom job. Plus, check out the vents above the front fenders that probably don't do anything, but look wild nonetheless.

Inside, new front seats look both extremely well-bolstered and comfortable, while a red shifter with GTS on it in big letters is undoubtedly goofy, but you know what? I'll allow it. Mods that actually change how the Crown Signia drives are all close to the ground. Brake calipers are borrowed from the 366-horsepower Lexus RX 500h F Sport and sit behind 21-inch HRE wheels and 295-section Toyo Proxes ST III tires.

This is technically a concept car, which means it isn't coming to a Toyota showroom near you any time soon. But if this is Toyota soft-launching the idea of, say, a future GR Sport Crown Signia with more power, more grip, and sportier looks, I'm all for it.

title: Prepare To Inhale Way More Methane Than You're Used To
raw_summary: Methane isn't one of those gases we want polluting our air . It traps more heat than carbon dioxide, worsens ground-level ozone, and is associated with increased breathing problems, heart disease, cancer and strokes. When Americans are so unhealthy and we just saw the hottest summer on record, you'd think the government would want less methane in our air, but no. The Associated Press reports that President Donald Trump just announced plans to increase the amount of methane oil and gas drillers are allowed to dump into our atmosphere. According to AP, getting rid of Biden-era limits on how much methane oil and gas companies could let escape while drilling is an attempt "to encourage more domestic drilling as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran." Considering Republicans' love of pollution and the oil industry's generous donations , it seems more likely this is just a giveaway to Trump's favorite donors, but sure. Maybe it will encourage more domestic drilling, but it doesn't sound like it will do much to lower fuel prices.

Considering Republicans' love of pollution and the oil industry's generous donations , it seems more likely this is just a giveaway to Trump's favorite donors, but sure. Maybe it will encourage more domestic drilling, but it doesn't sound like it will do much to lower fuel prices.

The U.S. should limit methane emissions because trashing the air we breathe is bad for everyone, and the idea of summers getting even hotter sounds miserable, but according to the White House, letting oil companies pollute more would save them billions of dollars while unlocking about 210 million barrels of oil. Except, at the current U.S. level of oil consumption, the AP estimates that's only 10 days worth of oil.

So we won't even get two weeks' worth of oil out of the deal, and all we have to do is let oil companies fill our air with even more of a gas we already know is responsible for about a third of all greenhouse gas emissions globally. Hope you don't mind spending $500 a month to keep your A/C running at 78 next summer.

Trump and Republicans are under a lot of pressure for starting a war with Iran that made gas expensive. At the moment, the average gallon of gas in the U.S. costs $4.27, per the U.S. Energy Information Administration , while a gallon of diesel costs $6.35. Those prices aren't as high as in some other countries, but just a year ago, gas was $3.04, and diesel cost $3.72. An extra $1.23 for a gallon of gas and $2.63 more for diesel adds up, and as a country, we really don't like it when fill-ups cost a small fortune.

In fact, back in July, high fuel prices had made Trump's war with Iran so unpopular, most non-MAGA Republicans said they planned to vote for the other party in November. Since July, Trump's popularity has only continued to fall, and the Republican party's approval recently hit a five-year low. Unfortunately for Republicans, there's no quick way out of this war, or a good way to lower gas prices significantly.

Allowing more methane pollution may temporarily lead to ever-so-slightly lower gas prices, but it's not like emissions were limited because Democrats hate the oil industry. It's because environmental scientists have known for a long time how bad methane is. From the AP:

Cuts in methane emissions have emerged in recent years as a global priority to slow the rate of climate change. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane, which is the main component in natural gas and far more potent to the atmosphere than carbon dioxide in the short term. ...

The PV5, Kia’s first 100% electric van, has been a huge success for the Korean automaker. After launching it at the end of last year, the PV5 has already become Europe’s top-selling small (C-segment) electric van.
Based on its modular skateboard platform, called E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to build custom configurations.

Although the PV5 is primarily sold in Passenger for everyday driving and Cargo for business use, Kia said the platform unlocks “endless possibilities” for different body styles and conversions, including a full-on electric campervan.
Wellhouse Leisure, a family-run campervan manufacturer based in the UK, revealed the Kia PV5 i-Camper.

The fully electric campervan is “now built and ready to view,” the company said. Based on the PV5 Cargo Plus, the campervan measures 4.69 m long, 1.89 m wide, and 1.99 m tall, which is about the size of a Ford Custom.
Although that’s pretty small for a camper, it offers more than you’d expect. Inside, the PV5 i-Camper includes two double beds with an elevating roof, a full kitchen setup, and a 200 W solar panel.
The sliding seat system enables the two rear seats to fold flat to form a bed and can be removed entirely. The upper bed, under the pop-up roof, has “more comfy” Froli Springs.

article_paragraphs: Boston Dynamics makes those cute little robot dogs that amaze and amuse us in videos like this one. How could anyone possibly object to something so endearing?

When it was revealed recently that four of its robot dogs have been acquired by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement for $1.3 million, many workers at Boston Dynamics were aghast. The four machines have been specially modified to include a robotic arm, thermal camera, and sensors for explosive materials.

They were not sold directly by Boston Dynamics but rather by a Connecticut company known as RADeCO, which markets the modified robots under the trade name Cerebus . In Greek mythology, Cerebus is the three headed dog that guards the gates of hell. How charming. While the contract from ICE is with RADeCO, Boston Dynamics is directly involved with technical support.

Boston Dynamics is 100 percent owned by Hyundai, by the way. So now a South Korean company that was humiliated by ICE agents a year ago when hundreds of its employees and sub-contractors were arrested, placed in handcuffs, and frog marched onto buses as undesirable aliens, is supplying ICE with advanced robots so it can better pursue its campaign of terror all across America. Greed conquers all, apparently.

In a letter to top executives reviewed by the Boston Globe , hundreds of Boston Dynamics employees said they are “uncomfortable” with the deal, and warned it could hurt the company’s reputation and workforce. “We cannot be proud of working at BD when that work is being used by a government agency that brutalizes civilians.”

In the letter, they expressed concerns that they will be seen by their family, friends, and community as “working directly with ICE. “Many of us have gotten messages from friends and family, asking us in disbelief and horror if this news is true, and how we can live with ourselves if it is.” The letter says the risks for Boston Dynamics are “simply too great to continue with this deal. We fear we will lose teammates over this decision, and worry about the risk it creates to achieve our shared company goals.”

In response, the company issued a statement saying the purpose of the robots is to keep people safe, and that the Department of Homeland Security must follow the company’s terms and conditions, which prohibit weaponization of the robots or using them for harm or intimidation. A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security told The Globe the robot “provides law enforcement officers with an additional tool to safely assess potentially dangerous situations before placing personnel or the public at risk.”

Anyone who thinks ICE will adhere to any guidelines is a fool. Ask the heirs of Alex Pretti and Rene Good if they think ICE agents can be trusted to act appropriately. Just this week, Pretti’s parents spoke publicly about their son’s execution by ICE in January. At a press conference , they said the federal government had not provided them with meaningful information about his death. “At every turn, they have ignored us, misled us, and shielded Alex’s killers,” said Michael Pretti. “We are a family who love this country. We trust in the institutions of this country. We believe in the rule of law — and that people should be held accountable through that law.”

article_paragraphs: Giant aluminum castings are Ford’s secret weapon to slash build times and revolutionize affordable EV manufacturing.

The 2028 Ford Fathom is a fully electric compact truck that will cost just $29,945 , but hitting that ambitious price target was no easy feat. To get there, Ford had to borrow an idea from Tesla — one not used for any other vehicle with a Blue Oval badge on its nose. We're talking about Ford's unicasting process, which is the equivalent of Tesla's gigacasting. Unicastings are aluminum components that replace multiple smaller parts and massively shorten build times.

The Fathom has two unicastings (one for the front part of the truck and another for the rear), and Ford says these two parts replace what would be 146 structural components in a conventional vehicle's construction.

It's no secret that Ford is using a Tesla-style castings for the Fathom, but this week it explained a little more about the build steps, and the benefits. Ford also revealed that 5,000 units (enough for 2,500 trucks) have already been produced in preparation for the Fathom's official debut next spring. The castings are produced at Ford's Shelbyville Technical Center where each one starts life as an aluminum ingot. The ingots are fed into a furnace by an elevator and melted at 1,300 degrees Fahrenheit (700 degrees Celsius) before moving into a casting machine to become one of the two unicastings fitted to each truck.

Passing a visual inspection isn't the only hoop a casting has to jump through before it can be shipped to Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky, where production Fathoms will be built. It also needs a full coordinate check in a climate-controlled room to make sure every dimension and hole location matches the official spec.

Then an industrial X-ray system checks the inside of the casting for defects like pores and voids, before an optical scanner gives the dimensions another once over. While this is happening, samples of the aluminum are undergoing tensile strength testing, and yet more checks analyze the chemical composition. Entire batches are not released to Louisville until every test is passed.

Once there, they'll enter a radically different built process to the one Henry Ford instigated over a century ago. Instead of vehicles moving down one production line, they will be assembled in three distinct sub-sections to save time , only being united to form a truck late in the build cycle.

No doubt Ford will be issuing a molten aluminum-like drip-feed of other technical teasers between now and the Fathom's debut early next year. We still have plenty to learn about the exterior design, the battery and charging setup, and what kind of range you can expect. But we do know that it will seat five, have more passenger space than a Toyota RAV4, offer bidirectional charging capabilities , and get to 60 mph (97 kph) in around 4.5 seconds.

raw_title: Toyota Snowhunter Concepts Ready To Conquer The Inevitable A.I.-Induced Nuclear Winter
title: Toyota Snowhunter Concepts Ready To Conquer The Inevitable A.I.-Induced Nuclear Winter
raw_summary: Every year, major automotive OEMs, tuners, and accessory manufacturers descend on Las Vegas for the SEMA Show. Although tuned exotics and muscle cars often turn the most heads, some brands love to let their hair down for SEMA, and Toyota has done just that. Seemingly for no reason other than the fun of it, it has unveiled five wild off-roaders with snow tracks , known as the Snowhunter concepts. Toyota will absolutely not sell these vehicles to the public, which is a shame. Toyota brought the five concepts, based on the Tundra, Tacoma, 4Runner, Land Cruiser, and Sequoia, to life at its CALTY Design Research facility in Michigan. The modifications go beyond the fitment of snow tracks, as they all feature other adventure-ready accessories. While none of these SEMA-bound vehicles have any chance of making it to production, we suspect Toyota's designers would be quite giddy if a brave Toyota owner took inspiration from these concepts to create their own tracked vehicle to cross the Arctic Circle.

article_paragraphs: Every year, major automotive OEMs, tuners, and accessory manufacturers descend on Las Vegas for the SEMA Show. Seemingly for no reason other than the fun of it, it has unveiled five wild off-roaders with snow tracks , known as the Snowhunter concepts. Toyota will absolutely not sell these vehicles to the public, which is a shame.

Toyota brought the five concepts, based on the Tundra, Tacoma, 4Runner, Land Cruiser, and Sequoia, to life at its CALTY Design Research facility in Michigan. The modifications go beyond the fitment of snow tracks, as they all feature other adventure-ready accessories. While none of these SEMA-bound vehicles have any chance of making it to production, we suspect Toyota's designers would be quite giddy if a brave Toyota owner took inspiration from these concepts to create their own tracked vehicle to cross the Arctic Circle.

Of the five concepts, the Tundra Snowhunter Concept is perhaps the most important. Beyond the tracks, it also features the Toyota TrailLift Pro Rack System, which transforms the bed with a rugged frame, storage options, and an articulating rack that's said to make it easier to load bikes, kayaks, and other gear onto the roof. If any feature of these concepts reaches the production line, it should probably be this. It's not the craziest custom Tundra we've ever seen, but it would be immensely practical during the next Snowpocalypse.

The special Sequoia Snowhunter Concept rocks cast aluminum running boards, a TRD front skid plate, a Prinsu roof rack, and a Thule Pulse 2 cargo box. Similarly, Toyota's one-off Land Cruiser Snowhunter Concept has the same roof rack, a Thule SnowPack ski rack, and Toyota Genuine rock rails and skid plates.

Toyota says the Tacoma model has been specifically configured for tight winter trails, noting the snow tracks are complemented a roof rack, a full-length bed rack, an awning, cargo storage, bed lighting, and dedicated recovery equipment. The collection is completed by the 4Runner concept, which also uses Toyota rack rails, a Prinsu roof rack, and a Thule cargo box. All models share an eye-catching white paint with grey geometric patterns, perfect for the snowy environments these wild off-roaders are designed to thrive in.
